body.text: Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā
body.translated_text: <s>Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā</s> (The Question of Rāṣṭrapāla)

body.text: namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvāryaśrāvakapratyekabuddhebhyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> //

body.text: nidānaparivartaḥ prathamaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Nidānaparivarta</s> (Introduction Chapter), the first /

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatābhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ pañcabhiśca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ, sarvairasaṅgapratibhānaiḥ kṣāntipratilabdhairnihatamārapratyarthikaiḥ sarvabuddhadharmātyāsannībhūtairekahātipratibaddhairdharaṇīpratilabdhaiḥ samādhipratilabdhairanantapratibhānapratilabdhairasaṅgavaiśāradyapratirṛddhivaśitāparamapāramiprāptairyāvatsarvaguṇavarṇaparyādattaiḥ / tadyathā - samantabhadreṇa ca nāma bodhisattvena mahāsattvena, samantanetreṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena, samantāvalokitena ca samantaraśminā ca samantaprabheṇa ca uttaramatinā ca vardhamānamatinā ca anantamatinā ca vipulamatinā ca akṣayamatinā ca dharaṇīdhareṇa ca jagatīṃdhareṇa ca jayamatinā ca viśeṣamatinā ca dhāraṇīśvararājena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena / mañjuśrīpramukhaiśca ṣaṣṭibhiranupamacittaiḥ bhadrapālapūrvaṃgamaiśca ṣoḍaśabhiḥsatpuruṣaiḥ bramhaṇā ca sahāṃpatinā śakreṇa ca devānāmindreṇa caturbhiśca lokapālaiḥ susīmena ca devaputreṇa susthitamatinā ca devaputreṇa sarvaiśca devendrairnāgendaiḥ kinnarendrairgandharvendrairyakṣendrairasurendrairgaruḍendraiḥ sarvairanekajātiśatasahasraparivāraistatraiva parṣadi saṃnipatitaiḥ saṃniṣaṇṇaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s> on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s>, and five thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — all possessing unobstructed eloquence, having attained <s>kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance), having defeated <s>Māra</s> and his adversaries, having drawn very near to all <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>, bound to a single aim, having attained <s>dhāraṇī</s>, having attained <s>samādhi</s>, having attained infinite eloquence, having reached the supreme <s>pāramitā</s> (perfection) of unobstructed confidence and supernatural mastery, endowed with all excellent qualities. Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Samantabhadra</s> (Universally Worthy), the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantanetra</s> (Universal Eye), <s>Samantāvalokita</s> (Universal Observer), <s>Samantaraśmi</s> (Universal Radiance), <s>Samantaprabha</s> (Universal Light), <s>Uttaramati</s> (Supreme Intellect), <s>Vardhamānamati</s> (Growing Intellect), <s>Anantamati</s> (Infinite Intellect), <s>Vipulamati</s> (Vast Intellect), <s>Akṣayamati</s> (Inexhaustible Intellect), <s>Dharaṇīdhara</s> (Earth-Bearer), <s>Jagatīṃdhara</s> (World-Bearer), <s>Jayamati</s> (Victorious Intellect), <s>Viśeṣamati</s> (Distinguished Intellect), and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dhāraṇīśvararāja</s> (King Lord of Dhāraṇī); together with sixty beings of incomparable mind led by <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, and sixteen noble men headed by <s>Bhadrapāla</s>; <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> lord of the <s>devas</s>, the four <s>Lokapālas</s> (World-Guardians), the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Susīma</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Susthitamati</s>, and all the lords of <s>devas</s>, lords of <s>nāgas</s>, lords of <s>kinnaras</s>, lords of <s>gandharvas</s>, lords of <s>yakṣas</s>, lords of <s>asuras</s>, and lords of <s>garuḍas</s> — all accompanied by retinues of many hundreds of thousands of births — assembled and seated in that very assembly //

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śrīgarbhasiṃhāsane saṃniṣaṇṇo merurivābhyudgataḥ sarvaparṣanmaṇḍalāt, sūrya iva sarvalokamavabhāsayan, candra iva sarvajagadavabhāsayan, bramheva praśāntavihārī, śakra iva durāsadakāyaḥ, cakravartīva saptabodhyaṅgaratnasamanvāgataḥ, siṃha ivānātmaśūnyasarvadharmavādī, agniskandha iva sarvajagadavabhāsakaraḥ, sarvadevaprabhāsamaṇiratnasamuccayamaṇirājavaddedīpyamānaḥ, sarvaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātumābhayā sphuritvā bramhasvararutaravitena sarvasattvavijñāpanānugatena ghoṣeṇāśuviniścitārthaḥ sarvadharmaparamapāramiprāptaḥ parṣadgato dharmaṃ deśayati sma ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇam, svarthaṃsuvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ bramhacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, seated upon the <s>Śrīgarbha</s> lion-throne, rising above the entire assembly like <s>Meru</s>, illuminating the entire world like the sun, illuminating all beings like the moon, dwelling in tranquility like <s>Brahmā</s>, with a body unapproachable like <s>Śakra</s>, endowed with the jewels of the seven factors of awakening like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), proclaiming all <s>dharmas</s> as without self and empty like a lion, illuminating all beings like a mass of fire, blazing like the king of jewels that is the collection of all divine radiant wish-fulfilling gems, having pervaded the entire trisāhasramahāsāhasra (billion-world) realm with fearlessness, with a voice of <s>Brahmā</s>-sound that follows the understanding of all beings, with meaning swiftly determined, having reached the supreme perfection of all <s>dharmas</s>, seated in the assembly, he taught the <s>Dharma</s> — excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, excellent in the end — proclaiming the holy life (<s>brahmacaryā</s>) with good meaning, good phrasing, complete, perfect, pure, and utterly clear //

body.text:
atha khalu prāmodyarājo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatito 'bhūt saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ /
sa bhagavantaṃ siṃhāsanasthaṃ sūryasahasrātirekayā prabhayā sarvaparṣanmaṇḍalaṃ jihmīkurvantamatīva virocamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭatuṣṭaḥ prasādāvarjirahṛdaya utthāyāsanātkṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantamābhirgāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Prāmodyarāja</s> (King of Joy) was assembled and seated in that very assembly. Seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s> seated on the lion-throne, outshining the entire assembly with a radiance surpassing a thousand suns, exceedingly resplendent, he was delighted and joyful, his heart seized with faith. Rising from his seat, with palms joined, he praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these verses —

children.text: abhibhūya jino jagadetān devagaṇāsurakinnaranāgān /
children.translated_text: The <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One), having overcome these hosts of <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>nāgas</s> in the world,

children.text: śrāvakabuddhasutān merutejā bhāsati hemagiriḥ sa yathaiva // 1 //
children.translated_text: with the splendor of <s>Meru</s>, surpassing <s>śrāvakas</s> and sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, shines like that golden mountain // 1 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 121
merurivāmarasaṃghanivāsaḥ sāgaramadhyagato 'pi virājan /
children.translated_text: Like <s>Meru</s>, dwelling-place of the host of immortals, radiant though situated in the midst of the ocean,

children.text: kṛpasāgaramadhyagato 'sau muñcati raśmisahasraśatāni // 2 //
children.translated_text: he, situated in the midst of the ocean of compassion, releases hundreds of thousands of rays // 2 //

children.text: bramhavihāragataḥ sa ca bramha bramhapurastha ivābhirarāja /
children.translated_text: He who has attained the <s>Brahmavihāra</s> (divine abiding) is himself like <s>Brahmā</s>, shining as if standing before <s>Brahmā</s>'s city,

children.text: dhyānavimokṣasamādhivihārī bhāsati sarvajage varasattvaḥ // 3 //
children.translated_text: dwelling in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), and <s>samādhi</s>, the supreme being shines in all the world // 3 //

children.text: śakra iva tridaśeṣu virājan devatamadhyagataḥ pṛthutejāḥ /
children.translated_text: Like <s>Śakra</s> radiant among the thirty gods, situated amidst the <s>devas</s>, of great splendor,

children.text: bhāsati sarvajage munirājā lakṣaṇacitrita jñānaguṇāḍhyaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: the king of sages shines in all the world, adorned with the marks, rich in the qualities of wisdom // 4 //

children.text: dvīpacaturnṛpatirhyavabhāsī śobhati lokamimaṃ tvanubhāsan /
children.translated_text: Like a sovereign of the four continents illuminating, he beautifies this world, shining upon it,

children.text: āryapathe ca neyojayamānaḥ śobhati eṣa kṛpāśayabuddhiḥ // 5 //
children.translated_text: guiding beings onto the noble path, this one of compassionate intent and wisdom shines // 5 //

children.text: agnimaṇiprabhadhyāmakaro 'sau bhāsati khe pratiyanniva sūryaḥ /
children.translated_text: He whose hands have the radiance of fire and jewels, who shines in the sky like the sun advancing,

children.text: sūryasahasraviśiṣṭaprabhāso bhāsati buddharavirjagatīha // 6 //
children.translated_text: with a radiance surpassing a thousand suns, the <s>Buddha</s>-sun shines here in the world // 6 //

children.text: candra ivāmala bhāti niśīthe bhāsati sarvajageṣu viśuddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like the stainless moon shining at night, he shines pure in all the worlds,

children.text: pūrṇaśaśāṅkanibhaṃ jinavaktraṃ sarvaprabhāmabhibhūya vibhāti // 7 //
children.translated_text: the face of the <s>Jina</s>, resembling the full moon, shines overpowering all radiances // 7 //

children.text: parvatamūrdhani agniryathaiva rātripraśānta prabhāsati sattvān /
children.translated_text: Just as a fire on a mountain peak illuminates beings in the quiet of night,

children.text: mohatamo nikhitaṃ vinihatya bhāsati jñānaprabhāsu maharṣiḥ // 8 //
children.translated_text: having destroyed the darkness of delusion completely, the great sage shines in the light of wisdom // 8 //

children.text: parvatakandaradhīraninādī trāsayatīha mṛgān bhuvi siṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like a lion whose deep roar resounds through mountain caves, terrifying animals on the earth,

children.text: śūnyanirātmaninādi narendraḥ bhāsayate hi tathāparatīrthyān // 9 //
children.translated_text: the lord of men, proclaiming emptiness and non-self, thus illuminates the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heretical teachers) // 9 //

children.text: sanmaṇirāja ivojjvalatejā bhāsati sarvamaṇīnabhibhūya /
children.translated_text: Like the king of noble jewels blazing with splendor, outshining all gems,

children.text: kāñcanavarṇanibho jinakāyo bhāsati sarvajagatyabhibhūya // 10 //
children.translated_text: the body of the <s>Jina</s>, resembling the color of gold, outshines all the world // 10 //

children.text: na ca te 'sti samaḥ kvaci loke uttari nāpi ca vidyati sattvaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is none equal to you anywhere in the world, nor is there any being superior,

children.text: puṇyatu jñānatu vīryaupāyaiḥ sarvaguṇaiśca samo na tavāsti // 11 //
children.translated_text: in merit, in wisdom, in vigor and skillful means — in all qualities there is none equal to you // 11 //

children.text: bhāsayate hi jagannaravīro dṛṣṭu mayā guṇasāgara nāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The hero among men illuminates the world; having seen the Lord, the ocean of qualities,

children.text: gauravajātavivardhitaprītiḥ pādatale patito 'smi jināya // 12 //
children.translated_text: with reverence arisen and joy increased, I have fallen at the feet of the <s>Jina</s> // 12 //

children.text: stutya mayā rūpasāgarabuddhiṃ sarvaguṇākara lokapradīpam /
children.translated_text: Having praised the <s>Buddha</s>, ocean of form and wisdom, treasury of all virtues, lamp of the world,

children.text: puṇyamupārjitamatra tena sarvajagatspṛśatāṃ varabodhim // 13 //
children.translated_text: by the merit accumulated here, may all beings attain supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) // 13 //

body.text: atha khalu prāmodyarājo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantamābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya kṛtāñjalipuṭo 'nimiṣābhyāṃ nayanābhyāṃ tathāgatakāyamavalokayan dharmadhātumeva vicārayamāṇo gambhīraṃ duravagāhaṃ durdṛśaṃ duranubodhamatarkyaṃ tarkāpagataṃ śāntaṃ sūkṣmaṃ cānupraviśan, acintyaṃ buddhagocaramanuvicārayamāṇaḥ, sarvadharmaprasṛtaṃ tathāgatajñānamanucintayamānaḥ, asamasamaṃ buddhaviṣayaṃ saṃpaśyamānaḥ, acintyaṃ tathāgatopāyaviṣayagocaramavataran, dahrmadhātunayasvabhāvāvatāratāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmavakalpayamānaḥ, anālayagaganagocarā hi buddhā bhagavanta iti saṃpaśyan, bhūtakoṭyakoṭisvabhāvāvatāraṃ sarvadharmāṇāmityadhimucyamānaḥ, anāvaraṇaṃ ca buddhavimokṣamabhilaṣamāṇaḥ, (

children.text: Vaidya, RP 122
children.translated_text: Vaidya, RP 122

children.text: ) dhruvaṃ śivaṃ śāśvataṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ kāyamityavataramāṇaḥ, sarvabuddhakṣetraprasarānugatāṃ sarvasattvābhimukhatā ca tathāgatakāyasyāvataran, aparāntakalpakoṭibhirapi nāsti buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ guṇaparyantaṃ ityanusmaran, prāmodyarājo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastūṣṇīvyavasthito 'bhūt dharmadhātumeva vicārayamāṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: ) reflecting that the body of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, is firm, auspicious, and eternal; contemplating the all-pervading presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s body throughout all <s>Buddha-fields</s> and facing all beings; recollecting that even in koṭis of kalpas at the end of time, there is no limit to the qualities of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s> — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Prāmodyarāja</s> remained silent, contemplating the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of dharma) itself //

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Prāmodyarāja</s>, having praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these verses, with palms joined, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, extending his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> (

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena āyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālaḥ śrāvastyāṃ traimāsyaṃ varṣamupagataḥ / traimāsyātyayena kṛtacīvaro niṣṭhitacīvaraḥ sa pātracīvaramādāya bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ navakairādikarmikairacirapravrajitairanupūrveṇa janapadacārikāṃ caran yena rājagṛhaṃ mahānagaraṃ yena ca gṛdhrakūṭaḥ parvatarājastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: At that time, the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> had undertaken the three-month rains retreat in <s>Śrāvastī</s>. At the end of the three months, having made his robes and completed his robes, taking his bowl and robes, together with a group of <s>bhikṣus</s> — newcomers, beginners, recently ordained — wandering on a gradual tour of the countryside, he approached <s>Rājagṛha</s>, the great city, and <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>, the king of mountains //

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantaṃ triḥ pradakṣiṇikṛtyaikānte 'tiṣṭhat / ekāntasthitaścāyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālaḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭo bhagavantamābhirgāthābhirabhyaṣṭavīt -
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, with palms joined, praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these verses —

body.text: vandamo naravaraṃ prabhaṃkaraṃ vandamo gaganatulyamānasam // 14 //
body.translated_text: I pay homage to the best of men, the light-maker; I pay homage to one whose mind is equal to the sky // 14 //

children.text: kīrtayanti tava varṇa nāyakāḥ kṣetrakoṭiprasarātsamantataḥ /
children.translated_text: The leaders proclaim your praise from across koṭis of <s>Buddha-fields</s> in all directions,

children.text: śrutva buddhasuta enti harṣitāḥ pūjanāya guṇasāgaraṃ munim // 15 //
children.translated_text: hearing which, the sons of the <s>Buddha</s> come with joy to worship the sage, ocean of qualities // 15 //

children.text: pūja kṛtva sugatānurūpato dharma śrutva virajaṃ mahāmuneḥ /
children.translated_text: Having worshipped in a manner befitting the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), having heard the stainless <s>Dharma</s> of the great sage,

children.text: yānti kṣetra svaka hṛṣṭamānasā varṇamāla tava tāṃ prabhāṣataḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: they return to their own fields with joyful minds, proclaiming a garland of your praises // 16 //

children.text: kalpakoṭinayutānacintiyān sattvakāraṇamacāracārikām /
children.translated_text: For inconceivable koṭis and nayutas of kalpas, you practiced the conduct of benefiting beings,

children.text: no ca asti tava khinna mānasaṃ eṣamāṇa varabodhimuttamām // 17 //
children.translated_text: yet there was no weariness in your mind while seeking the supreme and excellent <s>bodhi</s> // 17 //

children.text: dānaśīlacarito 'si nāyakā kṣāntivīrya api dhyānaśikṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: O leader, you practiced <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and <s>śīla</s> (morality), were trained in <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation),

children.text: prajñupāya sada pāramiṃ gatā tena vandasi mahāvināyakam // 18 //
children.translated_text: having always gone to the perfection of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) — therefore I pay homage to the great guide // 18 //

children.text: ṛddhipādavarabhijñakovidam indriyairbalavimokṣaśikṣitam /
children.translated_text: Skilled in the bases of supernatural power and the excellent <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges), trained in the faculties, powers, and <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations),

children.text: sarvasattvacarite gatiṃ gataṃ vandamo asamajñānapāragam // 19 //
children.translated_text: having gone to mastery of the conduct of all beings — I pay homage to one who has reached the far shore of incomparable wisdom // 19 //

children.text: cittadhāra jagataḥ prajānase yā cariryatha ca karmasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: You know the mental dispositions of the world, what their conduct is and how their <s>karma</s> arises,

children.text: yena vā nayamukhena mucyate taṃ ca vetsi bhagavannarottamā // 20 //
children.translated_text: and by which gateway of method they are liberated — this too you know, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, best of men // 20 //

children.text: rāgadveṣa jahi mohasaṃbhavaṃ yena sattva trirapāyagāminaḥ /
children.translated_text: You have destroyed <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and that which arises from <s>moha</s> (delusion), by which beings go to the three lower realms,

children.text: yena yānti sugatiṃ ca karmaṇā jānase sukṛtaduṣkṛtaṃ jage // 21 //
children.translated_text: and by which actions they go to a good destiny — you know the good and evil deeds in the world // 21 //

children.text: ye jagaddhitakarā atītakāḥ sāṃprataṃ ca naradevapūjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who were benefactors of the world in the past, and those now worshipped by men and gods,

children.text: ye anāgata guṇāgrapāragāstāṃ ca sarvasugatān prajānase // 22 //
children.translated_text: and those in the future who will reach the far shore of the highest qualities — you know all those <s>Sugatas</s> // 22 //

children.text: kṣetraśuddhirapi cāpi saṃbhavo bodhisattvagaṇāḥ śrāvakāstathā /
children.translated_text: The purification of <s>Buddha-fields</s>, their arising, the hosts of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and likewise <s>Śrāvakas</s>,

children.text: yāvadāyuratha vā maharṣiṇāṃ sarvathā hyakhilato vijānasi // 23 //
children.translated_text: and the lifespan of the great sages — all this you know completely and in full // 23 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 123
nirvṛtau ca sthiti dharma yādṛśī yādṛśī ca jinadhātupūjanā /
children.translated_text: And what the <s>Dharma</s> is like when it remains after <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and what the worship of the <s>Jina</s>'s relics is like,

children.text: dharmakośadhara tatra yādṛśā tān prajānasi narottamākhilān // 24 //
children.translated_text: and what the bearers of the treasury of <s>Dharma</s> are like there — you know all those, O best of men, completely // 24 //

children.text: jñāna daśabalasya viditaṃ hyanāvṛtaṃ vartate satatamadhvasu triṣu /
children.translated_text: The knowledge of the one with the ten powers is known to be unobstructed, operating constantly in the three times,

children.text: sarvadharmanayayuktamānasā jñānasāgara jinā namo 'stu te // 25 //
children.translated_text: with a mind engaged in the method of all <s>dharmas</s> — O ocean of wisdom, O <s>Jina</s>, homage to you // 25 //

children.text: nāsti te samasamaḥ kutottaro lakṣaṇaiśca pratimaṇḍitāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is none equal to you, much less superior; your form is adorned with the marks,

children.text: tārakābhiriva khaṃ vicitritaṃ vandamo munivaraṃ narottamam // 26 //
children.translated_text: decorated like the sky with stars — I pay homage to the best of sages, best of men // 26 //

children.text: rūpamapyasamakaṃ manoramaṃ jimha kurvati jagatsadevakam /
children.translated_text: Your form, incomparable and delightful, puts to shame the world with its gods,

children.text: bramha śakra akaniṣṭhadevatā agratastava na te virājite // 27 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> deities — before you, they do not shine // 27 //

children.text: kāñcanācala ivāsi nirmalaḥ snigdha keśa mṛdu dakṣiṇotthitā /
children.translated_text: You are stainless like a golden mountain, with smooth hair, soft, curling to the right,

children.text: merurāja iva uṣṇiṣodgato bhāsate vipulapuṇyasaṃbhavaḥ // 28 //
children.translated_text: with <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) rising like the king of mountains <s>Meru</s>, shining, born of vast merit // 28 //

children.text: raśmikoṭiniyutān pramuñcato rājatorṇa tava ca bhruvostaṭe /
children.translated_text: Releasing koṭis and nayutas of rays, the royal arch between your eyebrows,

children.text: netra utpalanibhaṃ manoramaṃ yena vīkṣyasi jagatkṛpāśayaḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: eyes lovely as the <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), with which you gaze upon the world with compassionate intent // 29 //

body.text:
pūrṇacandra iva nirmale nabhe bhāsate tava mukhaṃ vināyaka /
tṛpyate na hi nirīkṣako jano vandamo suvadanaṃ narottamam // 30 // haṃsabarhimṛgarājavikramā mattavāraṇavilambagāminaḥ /

children.text: kampayan vrajasi medinītalaṃ vandamo daśabalaṃ dṛḍhavratam // 31 //
children.translated_text: making the earth tremble as you walk — I pay homage to the one of ten powers and firm vows // 31 //

body.translated_text: Like the full moon in the stainless sky, your face shines, O guide; the beholding people are never sated — I pay homage to the beautiful face of the best of men // 30 // With the gait of a swan, a peacock, the king of beasts, and the slow stride of a rutting elephant,

children.text: dīrghavṛttarucirā karāṅgulī śuddhatāmra nakhajālacitritam /
children.translated_text: Your fingers are long, rounded, and beautiful, adorned with the web of pure coppery nails,

children.text: utthitaḥ spṛśati jānumaṇḍale vandamo kanakavarṇasaṃnibham // 32 //
children.translated_text: when standing they reach to your kneecaps — I pay homage to one resembling the color of gold // 32 //

children.text: citrayan vrajasi midinītalaṃ cakrajālacitapādavikramaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Adorning the surface of the earth as you walk, with the stride of wheel-marked feet,

children.text: pādaraśmiparipācitāścyutā devalokamupayānti mānavāḥ // 33 //
children.translated_text: those who are ripened and released by the rays from your feet go to the world of the <s>devas</s> // 33 //

children.text: dharmarāja dhanasaptadāyakā dharmadānapati dāntamānasā /
children.translated_text: O <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of Dharma), giver of the seven treasures, lord of the gift of <s>Dharma</s>, of tamed mind,

children.text: śāsamānu jaga dharmacaryayā dharmasvāmi praṇamāmi nāyakam // 34 //
children.translated_text: governing the world through righteous conduct — I bow to the guide, the lord of <s>Dharma</s> // 34 //

children.text: maitra varma smṛti khaḍgamuttamaṃ śīla cāpamiṣu prajñupāyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Loving-kindness as your armor, mindfulness as your supreme sword, morality as your bow, arrows of wisdom and skillful means,

children.text: yena kleśaripavo vighātitāṃ jātimṛtyubhavatṛṣṇavardhakāḥ // 35 //
children.translated_text: by which the enemies — the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — are destroyed, those that increase birth, death, existence, and craving // 35 //

children.text: tīrṇa tārayasi sattvakoṭiyo mukta mocayasi bandhanājjagat /
children.translated_text: Having crossed, you ferry across koṭis of beings; having been liberated, you liberate the world from bondage,

children.text: mārga darśayasi kṣema nirjvaraṃ yena yānti sugatāḥ śivaṃ padam // 36 //
children.translated_text: you show the path that is safe and free from affliction, by which the <s>Sugatas</s> go to the auspicious state // 36 //

children.text: yatra jātimaraṇā na vidyate viprayoga na ca duḥkhasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is neither birth nor death, no separation and no arising of suffering,

children.text: taṃ śivaṃ padavaraṃ hyasaṃskṛtaṃ deśitāsi karuṇāmupetya hi // 37 //
children.translated_text: that auspicious, supreme, unconditioned state you have taught, having embraced compassion // 37 //

children.text: stutya lokapravaraṃ mahāmuniṃ sarvadharmavaśipāragaṃ jinam /
children.translated_text: Having praised the best of the world, the great sage, the <s>Jina</s> who has mastered and gone beyond all <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: puṇyamatra yadupārjitaṃ mayā tena bodhimabhibudhyatāṃ jagat // 38 //
children.translated_text: by the merit I have accumulated here, may the world attain <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) // 38 //

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālo bhagavantamābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya kṛtāñjalipuṭa utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ (

children.text: Vaidya, RP 124
children.translated_text: Vaidya, RP 124

children.text: ) praṇamya bhagavantametadavecat - pṛccheyamahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kaṃcideva pradeśam, sacenme bhagavānavakāśaṃ kuryātpṛṣṭaḥ praśnavyākaraṇāya / evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmāntaṃ rāṣṭrapālametadavocat - pṛccha tvaṃ rāṣṭrapāla yadyadevākāṅkṣasi / ahaṃ te tasyaiva praśnasya pṛṣṭasya vyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣyāmi //
children.translated_text: ) Having bowed to the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), he said this: "I would ask the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain matter, if the <s>Bhagavān</s> would grant me the opportunity to answer [my] question." Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: "Ask, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, whatever you wish. I shall satisfy your mind with the answer to that very question when asked."

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, having praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these verses, with palms joined, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, extending his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> (

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālo bhagavantametadavocat - katamairbhagavan dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sattvadharmaguṇaviśeṣatāmanuprāpnoti, aparādhīnajñānatāṃ ca pratilabhate, āśuprajñatāṃ cānuprāpnoti, viniścayapratibhānatāṃ ca pratilabhate, ālokatāṃ ca pratilabhate, sarvajñatāpraveśaṃ sattvaparipākaṃ vimatiprahāṇaṃ kāṅkṣaprahāṇaṃ sarvajñatāviniścayaṃ pratilabhate, sattvāvatārakauśalyaṃ yathā vāditathākāritāṃ ca bhūtasaṃdhāyavacanaṃ sattvakauśalyatāṃ ca, buddhānusmṛtipratilābhaṃ sarvapraśnaparipṛcchanatāṃ ca, sarvadharmadhāraṇatāṃ ca kṣipraṃ ca sarvajñatā manuprāpnoti ? atha khalvāyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Endowed with which qualities, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> (great being) attain distinction in the qualities of beings and dharmas, obtain independence of knowledge, attain quickness of wisdom, obtain the capacity for definitive eloquence, obtain luminosity, obtain entry into omniscience, ripening of beings, abandonment of doubt, abandonment of uncertainty, certainty regarding omniscience, skill in reaching beings, consistency between words and deeds, speaking truthfully, skill regarding beings, attainment of recollection of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the ability to answer all questions, retention of all dharmas, and quickly attain omniscience?" Then the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: bodhisattvacaryā suniścitā tattvato bhavati yo 'sya saṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The conduct of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, well-ascertained — what is its true origin?

children.text: jñāgasāgarakathāviniścayaṃ bhāṣatāṃ mama jino narottamā // 39 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One), best of men, speak to me the definitive account of the ocean of knowledge.

children.text: uttaptacāmikaravigrahopamā agrasattvavara puṇyasaṃcayā /
children.translated_text: O best of supreme beings, with a body like refined gold, with an accumulation of merit —

children.text: tvaṃ hi trāṇa layanaṃ parāyaṇa agracaryamamalaṃ vadādya me // 40 //
children.translated_text: You are the protector, the refuge, the final resort; proclaim to me now the supreme, stainless conduct.

children.text: jñānalotu(pu ?) bhavate kṣayaḥ kathaṃ dhāraṇī amṛta bodhi udgatam /
children.translated_text: How does the lotus of knowledge come to fruition? <s>Dhāraṇī</s> (retention), nectar, awakening, exalted —

children.text: prajñāsāgara kathaṃ viśudhyate yena chindati jane 'sya saṃśayam // 41 //
children.translated_text: how is the ocean of wisdom purified, by which one cuts the doubt of beings?

body.text:
saṃsaran subahukalpakoṭiyaḥ khedabuddhi na ca jātu jāyate /
vīkṣya lokamapi duḥkhapīḍitaṃ teṣamarthakuśalaṃ niṣevate // 42 // kṣetraśuddhiparivārasaṃpadaṃ āyuragryamatha kṣetrasaṃpadam /

children.text: sattvakāraṇakathā niruttarā bodhicaryamamalāṃ prakāśaya // 43 //
children.translated_text: the unsurpassed account of the purpose of beings — illuminate the stainless conduct of awakening!

body.translated_text: Wandering through many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), weariness of mind never arises; seeing the world afflicted by suffering, one pursues what is beneficial for them. Purity of the [Buddha-]field, excellence of retinue, supreme lifespan, and excellence of the field —

children.text: mārabhañjana kudṛṣṭiśodhanā tṛṣṇaśoṣaṇa vimuktisparśanā /
children.translated_text: O crusher of <s>Māra</s>, purifier of wrong views, desiccator of craving, toucher of liberation,

children.text: dharmanetri rayina pramuhyata sattvaratna nigadottamāṃ carim // 44 //
children.translated_text: O guide to the <s>Dharma</s>, for those bewildered by wealth — proclaim the supreme conduct, O jewel among beings!

children.text: rūpa bhoga pratibhānasaṃpadaṃ snigdhavākparṣadaśca toṣaṇī /
children.translated_text: Excellence of form, enjoyments, and eloquence, speech that is gentle and delighting to assemblies,

children.text: meghavatsugata tarpayañjagat deśayasyapi ca buddhagocaram // 45 //
children.translated_text: like a cloud, O <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), you satisfy the world and teach the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s>.

children.text: mañjughoṣa kalaviṅkususvarā brahmaghoṣa kumatipraṇāśanā /
children.translated_text: With a voice sweet as <s>Mañjughoṣa</s> (sweet-voiced one) and the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, with the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, destroying wrong understanding,

children.text: dharmakāma parṣatsamāgatā tarpayāmṛtarasena tāṃ prabho // 46 //
children.translated_text: the assembly gathered, desiring the <s>Dharma</s> — satisfy them with the nectar of <s>amṛta</s> (immortality), O Lord!

children.text: asti chanda pravarāgrabodhaye dharmachanda vihito na yujyate /
children.translated_text: There is aspiration for the supreme, foremost awakening; aspiration for the <s>Dharma</s> that has been established is fitting.

children.text: deśanāsamaya eṣa nāyakā kāla eṣa vararatnaśrāvaṇe // 47 //
children.translated_text: This is the time for teaching, O Leader; this is the time for hearing the excellent jewel.

children.text: bodhikāṅkṣu mama vidyate mune āśayaṃ mama jina prajānase /
children.translated_text: I who desire awakening — O Sage, the <s>Jina</s> knows my intention.

children.text: prārthayāmi na jinasya heṭhanāṃ sādhu uttamacariṃ prakāśaya // 48 //
children.translated_text: I do not seek to mock the <s>Jina</s>; please, illuminate the supreme conduct!

children.text: Vaidya, RP 125

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmāntaṃ rāṣṭrapālametadavocat - sādhu sādhu rāṣṭrapāla / sādhu sādhu punastvaṃ rāṣṭrapāla yastvaṃ tathāgatametamarthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ manyase / bahujanahitāya tvaṃ rāṣṭrapāla pratipanno bahujanasukhāya arthāya hitāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca, etarhi cānāgatānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ saṃparigrahāya / tena hi rāṣṭrapāla śṝṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru / bhāṣiṣye / sādhu bhagavannityāyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālo bhagavataḥ pratyaśroṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat -
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: "Excellent, excellent, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>! Well done indeed, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, that you consider this matter worth asking of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. You have set out for the benefit of the many, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, for the happiness of the many, for the welfare and benefit of gods and humans, and for the support of present and future <s>bodhisattva mahāsattvas</s>. Therefore, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, listen well and carefully attend! I shall speak." "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>," the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him:

body.text: caturbhī rāṣṭrapāla dharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva etāṃ pariśuddhiṃ pratilabhate / katamaiścaturbhiḥ ? yaduta ārāgādhyāśayapratipattyā sarvasattvasamacittatayā śūnyatābhāvanatayā yathāvāditathākāritayā / ebhī rāṣṭrapāla catirbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattva etāṃ pariśuddhiṃ pratilabhate / iyamatra dharmatā //
body.translated_text: "Endowed with four qualities, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> attains this purification. Which four? Namely: through practice with a deeply devoted intention, through equanimity of mind toward all beings, through meditation on emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), and through consistency between words and deeds. Endowed with these four qualities, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, a <s>bodhisattva mahāsattva</s> attains this purification. This is the nature of things here."

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Herein this is said:

children.text: āśayena hi sadābhiyuktakā bodhimārga avivartyamānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are always devoted with [pure] intention, with minds unshakable on the path to awakening,

children.text: no ca śāṭhya na khilaṃ na māyatā teṣu vidyati anantajñāninām // 49 //
children.translated_text: in them — those of infinite knowledge — neither deceit, nor hardness of heart, nor hypocrisy is found.

children.text: dṛṣṭva sattva dukhitānanāyakān jātivyādhijaramṛtyumarditān /
children.translated_text: Seeing beings suffering, without a guide, crushed by birth, disease, old age, and death,

children.text: tāraṇārtha bhavato * * jagat dharmanāva samudānayanti te // 50 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of saving the world, they prepare the ship of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: sarvasattvasamacitta sūratā ekaputrakavadīkṣate jagat /
children.translated_text: With equanimity of mind toward all beings, with gentleness, one regards the world as one's only child.

children.text: sarvametadapi mocayāmyaham evamāśaya tathāgrapudgalāḥ // 51 //
children.translated_text: "I shall liberate all these" — with such intention are those foremost individuals.

children.text: śūnyatāsu satataṃ gatiṃ gata naiva cātma na ca sattva vidyate /
children.translated_text: Having always entered into the course of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), neither self nor being is found.

children.text: svapnamāyasadṛśaṃ hi saṃskṛtam atra bāla abudho vimohitā // 52 //
children.translated_text: For the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) is like a dream or an illusion; herein the foolish and ignorant are deluded.

children.text: vācayā yatha vadanti te budhāstatra caiva pratipattiyā sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: As those wise ones speak with their words, so they are established in their practice.

children.text: dānta śānta sada doṣavarjitā bodhisattvamārganiratā jinātmajāḥ // 53 //
children.translated_text: Tamed, tranquil, ever free from faults, devoted to the <s>bodhisattva</s> path — the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>.

body.text: catvāra ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāmāśvāsapratilābhā dharmāḥ / katame catvāraḥ ? dhāraṇī pratilābhaḥ kalyāṇamitrapratilābhaḥ gambhīradharmakṣāntipratilābhaḥ pariśuddhaśīlasamācāratā / ime rāṣṭrapāla catvāri bodhisattvānāmāśvāsapratilābhā dharmāḥ / iyamatra dharmatā //
body.translated_text: "There are these four qualities, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, that bring encouragement to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Which four? Attainment of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention), attainment of a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), attainment of patience regarding the profound <s>Dharma</s>, and purity of moral conduct and behavior. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four qualities that bring encouragement to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. This is the nature of things here."

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Herein this is said:

children.text: lābhino bhavanti dhāraṇīṣu te sadā mahāyaśā
children.translated_text: They always become endowed with <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, those of great renown,

children.text: dhārayanti yena dharma śreṣṭha sarvabuddhabhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: through which they retain the supreme <s>Dharma</s>, spoken by all the <s>Buddhas</s>.

children.text: na ca praṇāśayanti jātu bhūyu vardhate rati
children.translated_text: They never lose it; rather, their delight increases further,

children.text: asaṅgameva teṣu jñāna sarvadharmapāragāḥ // 54 //
children.translated_text: and their knowledge regarding all dharmas is unobstructed — they have gone to the other shore of all dharmas.

children.text: kalyāṇamitramāpnuvanti bodhi aṅgavardhakā
children.translated_text: They obtain a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) who increases the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>),

children.text: deśayanti śreṣṭha mārga tasya yena yānti nāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: who teaches the supreme path by which the Leaders go.

children.text: na kvacicca te bhavanti pāpamitrasevakā
children.translated_text: And nowhere do they become followers of evil friends;

children.text: dūrato vivarjayanti te 'gnivacca dāhanātmakān // 55 //
children.translated_text: they avoid them from afar, like fire of a destructive nature.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 126
gambhīra dharma śrutva dhīra śūnyatopasaṃhitaṃ
children.translated_text: Having heard the profound <s>Dharma</s>, courageous, connected with emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>),

children.text: na cātmasattvajīvadṛṣṭi teṣu bhonti sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: views of self, being, and life-force are found in them in no way whatsoever.

children.text: acchidraśīla te bhavanti śāntadāntamānasā
children.translated_text: Their morality is without breach; they are of peaceful and tamed minds.

children.text: anuttare ca buddhaśīli sa tva tāṃ niyojayet // 56 //
children.translated_text: And one should engage them in the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-morality.

body.text: catvāra ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ saṃsāraprāptānāṃ prītikaraṇā dharmāḥ / katame catvāraḥ ? buddhadarśanaṃ rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ prītikaraṇo dharmaḥ / anulomadharmaśravaṇaṃ rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ prītikaraṇo dharmaḥ / sarvasvaparityāgaḥ / anupalambhadharmakṣāntiḥ / ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ saṃsāraprāptānāṃ catvāraḥ prītikaraṇā dharmāḥ / iyamatra dharmatā //
body.translated_text: "There are these four qualities, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, that bring joy to <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have entered <s>saṃsāra</s>. Which four? Seeing the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a quality that brings joy to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Hearing the <s>Dharma</s> in accord [with awakening], <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a quality that brings joy to <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Giving away all one's possessions. Patience regarding the <s>Dharma</s> of non-apprehension. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four qualities that bring joy to <s>bodhisattvas</s> who have entered <s>saṃsāra</s>. This is the nature of things here."

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Herein this is said:

children.text: paśyanti te narottamaṃ saṃbuddhaṃ sarvajātiṣu
children.translated_text: They see the best of men, the Perfectly Awakened One, in all their births,

children.text: sarvaloka bhāsayanta tejasā samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: illuminating the entire world with his radiance on all sides.

children.text: pūjayaṃstathā narendrarāja premagauravasthitā
children.translated_text: They worship him, established in love and reverence for the lord of men,

children.text: varāgrabodhimeṣamāṇa sattvamokṣakāraṇāt // 57 //
children.translated_text: seeking the supreme, foremost awakening for the sake of liberating beings.

children.text: śṛṇoti dharma nāyakāna śāntamānulomikam
children.translated_text: One hears the <s>Dharma</s> of the Leaders, peaceful and in accord [with awakening];

children.text: āśayena śrutva dhīra yoniśaḥ prayujyate /
children.translated_text: having heard it with [pure] intention, the courageous one applies himself wisely.

children.text: anopalambhadharma śrutva kāṅkṣa nāsya jāyate
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>Dharma</s> of non-apprehension, no uncertainty arises in him —

children.text: niḥsattva iti sattvadharma nātra ātma vidyate // 58 //
children.translated_text: "beings are without [inherent] being" — in the dharma of beings there is no self found here.

children.text: sarvasvaparityāgi so bhaveta ityamagraho
children.translated_text: One who gives away everything becomes free from grasping,

children.text: prahṛṣṭacitta dṛṣṭva caiva yācakamupāgatam /
children.translated_text: with a joyful mind upon seeing a supplicant who has come.

children.text: grāmarāṣṭramedinīṃ ca putra dāra jīvitaṃ
children.translated_text: Villages, kingdoms, lands, sons, wives, and life itself —

children.text: saṃtyajanti sarva nāsya jāyate ca cittaiñjanā // 59 //
children.translated_text: they give up everything, and no mental disturbance arises in them.

body.text: caturṣu rāṣṭrapāla dharmeṣu bodhisattvenānapekṣeṇa bhavitavyam / katameṣu caturṣu ? gṛhavāsādrāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvenānapekṣeṇa bhavitavyam / pravrajitvā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvena lābhasatkārādanapekṣeṇa bhavitavyam / kulasaṃstavādrāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvenānapekṣeṇa bhavitavyam / kāyajīvitādrāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvenānapekṣeṇa bhavitavyam / eṣu caturṣu rāṣṭrapāla dharmeṣu bodhisattvenānapekṣeṇa bhavitavyam / iyamatra dharmatā //
body.translated_text: "A <s>bodhisattva</s> should be indifferent to four things, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. Which four? A <s>bodhisattva</s> should be indifferent to household life, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. Having gone forth, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> should be indifferent to gain and honor. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should be indifferent to praise of family, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should be indifferent to body and life, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should be indifferent to these four things, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. This is the nature of things here."

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Herein this is said:

children.text: tyaktvā gehamanantadoṣagahanaṃ cintānapekṣā sadā
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the house, a thicket of infinite faults, always indifferent to cares,

children.text: te 'raṇye ratimāpnuvanti guṇinaḥ śāntendriyāḥ sūratāḥ /
children.translated_text: they find delight in the forest, those virtuous ones, with pacified senses, gentle.

children.text: na strīsaṃstavu naiva cāpi purusaisteṣāṃ kvacidvidyate
children.translated_text: Among them there is no praise of women, nor indeed of men anywhere;

children.text: ekākī viharanti khaḍgavimalāḥ śuddāśayā nirmalāḥ // 60 //
children.translated_text: they dwell alone, pure as a rhinoceros horn, with pure intentions, stainless.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 127
lābhairnāpi ca teṣu harṣita mano līyantyalārbhairna ca
children.translated_text: Their minds are not elated by gains, nor do they cling to non-gains;

children.text: alpecchā itaretarairabhiratā māyākuhāvarjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: of few desires, delighting in each other, free from deceit and fraud.

children.text: sattvārthāya ca vīryayuktamanaso dāne dame 'vasthitā
children.translated_text: With minds yoked to effort for the welfare of beings, established in generosity and self-control,

children.text: dhyāne vīryaguṇe ca pāramigatāḥ saṃbuddhajñānārthinaḥ // 61 //
children.translated_text: gone to perfection in meditation, effort, and virtue — seekers of the knowledge of the Perfectly Awakened One.

children.text: kāye cāpyanapekṣya jīvita tathā tyaktvā priyān bāndhavām
children.translated_text: Indifferent even to the body and life, having abandoned dear relatives,

children.text: yujyante sada bodhimārga sudṛḍhā vajropamādhyāśayāḥ /
children.translated_text: they are always firmly yoked to the path of awakening, with intentions firm as a diamond.

children.text: kāyaśchidyati khaṇḍaśaśca na bhavetteṣāṃ ca citteñjanā
children.translated_text: Even if the body is cut to pieces, no mental disturbance arises in them;

children.text: bhūyo vīryamihārabhanti sudṛḍhaṃ sarvajñatākāṅkṣiṇaḥ // 62 //
children.translated_text: they undertake effort all the more firmly here, those who aspire to omniscience.

body.text: catvāra ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāmananutāpakaraṇā dharmāḥ / katame catvāraḥ ? śīlākhaṇḍanatā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāmananutāpakaraṇo dharmaḥ, araṇyavāsākutsyajanatā, catuṇāmāryavaṃśānāmanuvartanatā, bāhuśrutyapratilābho rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāmananutāpakaraṇo dharmaḥ / ime rāṣṭrapāla catvāro bodhisattvānāmananutāpakaraṇā dharmāḥ / iyamatra dharmatā //
body.translated_text: "There are these four qualities, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, that prevent remorse for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Which four? Non-violation of morality, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a quality that prevents remorse for <s>bodhisattvas</s>; not despising those who dwell in the forest; following the four noble lineages (<s>āryavaṃśa</s>); and attainment of extensive learning, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a quality that prevents remorse for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four qualities that prevent remorse for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. This is the nature of things here."

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Herein this is said:

body.text:
rakṣanti śīlamamalaṃ maṇiratnatulyaṃ na ca teṣu bhoti anuśīla susaṃyato vā /
tatreva śīli sada sattva niyojayanti / ākāṅkṣamāṇamimamuttamabuddhaśīlam // 63 //
body.translated_text: They guard their morality, stainless, like a jewel-gem, and among them there is one well-restrained in morality; therein they always engage beings in morality — those who aspire to this supreme <s>Buddha</s>-morality.

children.text: śūnye ca te hi nivasanti śubhe araṇye naivātmasaṃjña bhavate 'pi na jīvasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: They dwell in empty, beautiful forests, and neither the notion of self arises nor the notion of a living being;

children.text: tṛṇakāṣṭhakothasama paśayati sattvarūpaṃ strī neha nāsti ca pumānna ca ātmanīyam // 64 //
children.translated_text: one regards the form of beings as comparable to grass, wood, and decay — neither woman is here, nor man, nor anything belonging to self.

children.text: caturāryavaṃśaniratā akuhā āśāṭhyā adhyāśayena ca prayujyati so 'pramattaḥ /
children.translated_text: Devoted to the four noble lineages (<s>āryavaṃśa</s>), without deceit, without dishonesty, that heedful one applies himself with [pure] intention.

children.text: kurvanti ca śrutiguṇeṣu sadābhiyogaṃ saṃprārthayan sugatajñānamahānubhāvam // 65 //
children.translated_text: They always make effort in the virtues of learning, seeking the great power of the <s>Sugata's</s> (Well-Gone One's) knowledge.

children.text: bhavacārake jagadavekṣya idaṃ hyanāthaṃ jātījarāmaraṇaśokahataṃ rujārtam /
children.translated_text: Seeing this world wandering in existence, unprotected, struck by birth, old age, death, and grief, afflicted by disease,

children.text: samudānayitva pravarāṃ śivadharmanāvaṃ saṃtārayanti janatāṃ bhavasāgaraughāt // 66 //
children.translated_text: having prepared the supreme ship of the auspicious <s>Dharma</s>, they ferry beings across the flood of the ocean of existence.

children.text: na trāṇamanya śaraṇaṃ hi parāyaṇaṃ vā lokasya saṃskṛtagatau bhramato 'sti kaścit /
children.translated_text: There is no other protection, refuge, or final resort for the world wandering in the course of conditioned existence;

children.text: mayi sarva eva parimocayitavya sattvā ityarthameva praṇidhirmama agrabodhau // 67 //
children.translated_text: "All beings must be liberated by me" — this very purpose is my aspiration for supreme awakening.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 128

body.text: catasra imā rāṣṭrapāla ājāneyagatayo bodhisattvenānugantavyāḥ / katamāścatasraḥ ? sugatipratilābhaḥ, sa ca buddhotpādasamavadhānatayā / guruśuśrūṣaṇā, sā ca nirāmiṣasevanatayā / prāntaśayyāsanābhiratiḥ, sā ca lābhasatkārānapekṣatayā / pratibhānapratilābhaḥ, sa ca gambhīradharmakṣantisamanvāgatatayā / imā rāṣṭrapāla catasra ājāneyagatayo 'nugantavyāḥ / iyamatra dharmatā //
body.translated_text: "There are these four courses of a thoroughbred, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, that should be followed by a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Which four? Attainment of good destinies, and that through attending to the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>. Service to teachers, and that through selfless attendance. Delight in secluded seats and beds, and that through indifference to gain and honor. Attainment of eloquence, and that through being endowed with patience regarding the profound <s>Dharma</s>. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four courses of a thoroughbred to be followed. This is the nature of things here."

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Herein this is said:

children.text: vanakandareṣu satataṃ nivasanti dhīrā lābhena te sada anarthika bhonti nityam /
children.translated_text: They always dwell in forest caves, the courageous ones; they are ever indifferent to gain;

children.text: pratibhānavān sada bhavanti asaṅgabuddhī gambhīradharmakuśalā vigataprapañcāḥ // 68 //
children.translated_text: they are always endowed with eloquence, with unobstructed understanding, skilled in the profound <s>Dharma</s>, free from conceptual elaboration.

children.text: śuśrūṣakāḥ sada bhavanti guruṣu nityaṃ yatha te vadanti hi tathaiva ca te prayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are always devoted to service of their teachers; as [the teachers] speak, so they practice.

children.text: ārāgayanti sugatān bahāvo 'prameyān kurvanti pūja vipulāṃ jinajñānahetoḥ // 69 //
children.translated_text: They please many immeasurable <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-Gone Ones) and make vast offerings for the sake of the <s>Jina's</s> knowledge.

children.text: śreṣṭhā gatirbhavati cāpi mahāśayānāṃ deveṣu caiva manujeṣu ca mūrdhnaprāptāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the destiny of the great-intentioned ones is the best — among gods and humans they attain the summit.

children.text: sambodhimārga sada sattva samādayanti saṃyojayanti kuśaleṣu daśasvathāpi // 70 //
children.translated_text: They always encourage beings on the path of awakening and engage them also in the ten wholesome [courses of action].

children.text: śrutvā ca buddhaguṇa te ca bhavanti tuṣṭā āsanna te tu nacirādbhavitā hi mahyam /
children.translated_text: And having heard the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, they become delighted — "soon this will be mine;

children.text: saṃbudhyate 'pi ca śivāṃ virajāgrabodhiṃ mociṣya sattvaniyutāni anantaduḥkhāt // 71 //
children.translated_text: one will awaken to the auspicious, dustless, supreme awakening and liberate millions of beings from infinite suffering."

body.text: catvāra ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ bodhicaryāpariśodhakā dharmāḥ / katame catvāraḥ ? apratihatavijñānavirahitasya bodhisattvacaryā, kuhanalapananiṣpeṣaṇaparivarjitasyāraṇyavāsaḥ, sarvasvaparityāgino vipākāpratikāṅkṣatā, rātriṃdivaṃ dharmakāmatā dharmabhāṇakānāṃ ca skhalitāgaveṣaṇatā / ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ catvāro bodhisattvacaryāpariśodhakā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: These are four dharmas that purify the <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. What are the four? The <s>bodhisattva</s> (awakening-being) conduct of one whose consciousness is unobstructed and unimpaired; dwelling in the forest for one who has abandoned hypocrisy, flattery, and insinuation; not expecting karmic ripening while renouncing all possessions; desiring the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) day and night, and seeking out the faults of <s>Dharma</s> preachers. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four dharmas that purify <s>bodhisattva</s> conduct.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavaṃstasyāṃ vilāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke these verses on that occasion:

children.text: na khila mala na cāpi roṣacittaṃ na ca punareṣati kasyacit sadoṣam /
children.translated_text: No defilement, no anger in the mind, nor does one seek fault in anyone;

children.text: aśaṭha akuha niṣprapañcacitto bhavati anuttarabodhimīpsamānaḥ // 72 //
children.translated_text: Honest, without hypocrisy, with a mind free from conceptual elaboration — such is one who aspires to unsurpassed <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). 72.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 129
gṛhamativiṣamaṃ ca śokamūlaṃ kujanasamāgamayonimasya dūram /
children.translated_text: Household life is uneven and the root of sorrow; far from the womb of association with wicked people,

children.text: tyajati tadanapekṣya pravrajitvā girigahane vicaranti mokṣakāmāḥ // 73 //
children.translated_text: One abandons it without regard, and having gone forth, wanders in mountain caves, desiring liberation. 73.

children.text: araṇya vividha sevamāno bhavati aniśrita sarvajñātralābhe /
children.translated_text: Frequenting various forests, one becomes unattached, seeking omniscient knowledge;

children.text: kāya api ca jīvite 'napekṣo viharati siṃha ivottrasan jitārim // 74 //
children.translated_text: Heedless of body and life, one dwells like a lion, fearless, having conquered enemies. 74.

children.text: bhavati ca itaretareṇa tuṣṭaḥ śakunisamaḥ sada saṃcayaṃ vihāya /
children.translated_text: One is content with whatever comes, like a bird, always abandoning accumulation;

children.text: na ca bhavati niketu sarvaloke jñāna gaveṣati nitya bodhimārge // 75 //
children.translated_text: Without a fixed abode anywhere in the world, one constantly seeks knowledge on the path of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). 75.

children.text: eka viharati yathaiva khaḍgo na ca puna sa trasate yathaiva siṃhaḥ /
children.translated_text: One dwells alone like a rhinoceros, and does not tremble like a lion;

children.text: na ca bhuvi viśvasate mṛgeva trasto na ca punarunnamate sa pūjanena // 76 //
children.translated_text: One does not trust the world like a frightened deer, nor does one become elated by veneration. 76.

children.text: jagadidamabhivīkṣya ca prapāte prapatitamudyate pramokṣahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing this world fallen into the precipice, one strives for the sake of liberation;

children.text: ahamapi jagato 'sya trāṇabhūto yadi kuśaleṣu careyamapramattaḥ // 77 //
children.translated_text: "I too shall be a refuge for this world, if I practice in wholesome deeds without negligence." 77.

children.text: sumadhuravacanaḥ smitābhilāṣī akaluṣacitta priyāpriyeṣu nityam /
children.translated_text: With sweet speech, a pleasant smile, a mind uncorrupted toward the pleasant and unpleasant always,

children.text: viharati na ca sajjate 'nilo vā naravaracaryāmimābhīpsamānaḥ // 78 //
children.translated_text: One dwells without attachment, like the wind — such is one who aspires to the conduct of the best of men. 78.

children.text: śūnyatamadhimuktamānimittaṃ vicarati saṃskṛta sarvamāyabhūtam /
children.translated_text: One practices devoted to <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and the signless, seeing all conditioned things as illusion;

children.text: śamadamanirato viśālabuddhiḥ amṛtarasena ca sarvadā sa tuṣṭaḥ // 79 //
children.translated_text: Delighting in tranquility and self-control, of vast intelligence, one is always satisfied with the nectar of the deathless. 79.

children.text: prativadasi yathā (vasapathā ?) ca bodhimārge sa tu pariśodhayate sadāśayaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: As one practices on the path of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), one continually purifies one's intention;

children.text: dhāraṇīpratilābhameṣamāṇaḥ sahati ca duḥkha satāṃ guṇābhikāṅkṣī // 80 //
children.translated_text: Seeking the attainment of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mnemonic power), one endures suffering, aspiring to the virtues of the good. 80.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 130
imu carimabhivīkṣya bodhisattvo yo bhavate 'rthiku śo bhaveta tuṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: A <s>bodhisattva</s> who, seeing this conduct, becomes a seeker — that one should be content;

children.text: ya iha bhavati bodhaye asakto janayati doṣaśatāni so 'lpabuddhiḥ // 81 //
children.translated_text: But one who here becomes attached to <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) generates hundreds of faults — that one is of little wisdom. 81.

body.text: catvāra ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ prapātāḥ / katame catvāraḥ ? agauravatā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ prapātaḥ / akṛtajñatā śāṭhyasevanatā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ prapātaḥ / lābhasatkārādhyavasānaṃ rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ prapātaḥ / kuhanalapanatayā lābhasatkāraniṣpādanaṃ rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ prapātaḥ / ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ catvāraḥ prapātāḥ //
body.translated_text: These are four downfalls of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. What are the four? Disrespectfulness, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a downfall of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Ingratitude and resorting to deceit, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a downfall of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Fixation on gain and honor, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a downfall of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Procuring gain and honor through hypocrisy and flattery, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a downfall of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four downfalls of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyā velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke these verses on that occasion:

children.text: nityamagaurava te hi bhavanti āryaguruṣvapi mātṛpitṛṣu /
children.translated_text: They are always disrespectful even toward noble teachers, mothers, and fathers;

children.text: akṛtajña śaṭhāśca bhavanti nityamasaṃyatacāriṇa mūḍhāḥ // 82 //
children.translated_text: Ungrateful and deceitful always, of unrestrained conduct, deluded. 82.

children.text: adhyavasānaparāḥ sada lābhe te kuhaśāṭhyāprayogaratāśca /
children.translated_text: Always fixated on gain, devoted to the practice of hypocrisy and deceit,

children.text: kaścidapīha samo mama nāsti vakṣyati śīlaguṇeṣu kathaṃcit // 83 //
children.translated_text: One will say, "There is no one here equal to me" regarding moral virtues. 83.

children.text: te ca parasparameva ca dviṣṭā chidragaveṣaṇanityaprayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: They hate one another, constantly engaged in seeking faults;

children.text: kṛṣikarmavaṇijyaratāśca śravaṇā (śramaṇā) hi sudūrata teṣām // 84 //
children.translated_text: Devoted to farming and trade, they are far indeed from being <s>śramaṇas</s> (renunciants). 84.

children.text: evamasaṃyata paścimakāle bhikṣava śīlaguṇeṣu sudūre /
children.translated_text: Thus unrestrained in the last age, monks far from moral virtues,

children.text: te 'ntara hāpayiṣyanti madharmaṃ (maddharmaṃ ?) bhaṇḍanavigraha īrṣyavaśena // 85 //
children.translated_text: They will cause my <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) to decline, through quarrels, disputes, and the power of envy. 85.

children.text: bodhipathādapi nitya sudūre āryadhanādapi te ca sudūre /
children.translated_text: Always far from the path of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), far from the noble wealth,

children.text: mokṣapathaṃ ca vihāya praṇītaṃ pañcasu te gatiṣu bhamiṣyanti // 86 //
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the excellent path of liberation, they will wander in the five destinies. 86.

body.text: catvāra ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ bodhiparipanthakārakā dharmāḥ / katame catvāraḥ ? aśraddadhānatā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ bodhiparipanthakārako dharmaḥ / kausīdyaṃ rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ bodhiparipanthakārako dharmaḥ / māno rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ bodhiparipanthakārako dharmaḥ / parapūjerṣyāmātsaryacittaṃ rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ bodhiparipanthakārako dharmaḥ / ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ catvāro bodhiparipanthakārakā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: These are four dharmas that obstruct the <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. What are the four? Lack of faith, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a dharma that obstructs the <s>bodhi</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Laziness, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a dharma that obstructs the <s>bodhi</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Pride, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a dharma that obstructs the <s>bodhi</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. A mind of envy and jealousy toward the worship of others, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a dharma that obstructs the <s>bodhi</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four dharmas that obstruct the <s>bodhi</s> of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke these verses on that occasion:

children.text: aśraddhāḥ kusīdāḥ sada mūḍhacittā abhimāninaste 'pi sadā ca krodhanā /
children.translated_text: Without faith, always lazy, of deluded mind, conceited and always wrathful,

children.text: kṣamiṇaśca dṛṣṭvā sada bhikṣu yuktaṃ dāsyanti daṇḍaṃ vrajato vihārāt // 87 //
children.translated_text: Seeing patient and diligent monks, they will drive them out of the monastery with punishment. 87.

body.text: parasya pūjārthamiherṣya jātā avasthānu cittasya ca teṣu nāsti /

children.text: Vaidya, RP 131
avatāraprekṣī skhalitāṃ gaveṣī ko 'syāparādho 'stiha codayiṣye // 88 //
children.translated_text: Watching for an opening, seeking faults: "What offense does this one have? I shall accuse him!" 88.

body.translated_text: Envy arises here regarding the worship of others, and they have no steadiness of mind;

children.text: dūre itaste mama śāsanasya guṇadveṣiṇaste hi apāyanimnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Far are they from my teaching, those who hate virtue, inclined toward the lower realms;

children.text: tyaktvā jinasyāpi ca śāsanaṃ te yāsyantyapāyaṃ jvalitaṃ pracaṇḍam // 89 //
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), they will go to the blazing, fierce lower realms. 89.

children.text: śrutvā ca teṣāmiha pāpacaryām adharmayuktāṃ ca gatiṃ sudāruṇām /
children.translated_text: Having heard of their evil conduct here and their terrible path joined with unrighteousness,

children.text: yujyadhva nityaṃ sada bodhimārge mā tapsyathā durgatiṣūpapannāḥ // 90 //
children.translated_text: Apply yourselves always and constantly to the path of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening); do not grieve when reborn in the lower realms! 90.

children.text: bahukalpakoṭībhi kadāci buddho utpadyate lokahito maharṣiḥ /
children.translated_text: After many <s>koṭīs</s> (tens of millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), rarely does a <s>Buddha</s>, the great sage, benefactor of the world, arise;

children.text: labdho 'dhunā sa pravaraḥ kṣaṇo 'dya tyaja pramādaṃ yadi mokṣakāmaḥ // 91 //
children.translated_text: Now that excellent moment has been obtained — abandon negligence if you desire liberation! 91.

body.text: catvāra ime rāṣṭrapāla pudgalā bodhisattvena na sevitavyāḥ / katame catvāraḥ ? pāpamitraṃ rāṣṭrapāla pudgalo bodhisattvena na sevitavyaḥ / upalambhadṛṣṭiko rāṣṭrapāla pudgalo bodhisattvena na sevitavyaḥ / saddharmapratikṣepakaḥ pudgalo rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvena na sevitavyaḥ / āmiṣalolupaḥ pudgalo rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvena na sevitavyaḥ / ime rāṣṭrapāla catvāraḥ pudgalā bodhisattvena na sevitavyāḥ //
body.translated_text: These are four types of persons a <s>bodhisattva</s> should not associate with, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. What are the four? A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not associate with an evil friend, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not associate with a person of the view of apprehension, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not associate with a person who rejects the true <s>Dharma</s> (teaching), <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. A <s>bodhisattva</s> should not associate with a person greedy for material things, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four types of persons a <s>bodhisattva</s> should not associate with.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke these verses on that occasion:

children.text: ye pāpamitrāṇi vivarjayanti kalpāṇamitrāṇi sadā bhajanti /
children.translated_text: Those who shun evil friends and always resort to good friends,

children.text: vardhanti te bodhipatheṣu nityaṃ yatha śuklapakṣe divi candramaṇḍalam // 92 //
children.translated_text: They grow constantly on the paths of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), like the moon's disc in the bright fortnight. 92.

children.text: upalambhadṛṣṭyāṃ ca sadā niviṣṭā ātme niviṣṭāstatha jīvapoṣe /
children.translated_text: Those always immersed in the view of apprehension, attached to self and to the notion of a living being,

children.text: viṣakumbhavatte sada varjayanti ye buddhajñānena bhavanti arthikāḥ // 93 //
children.translated_text: They avoid them always as if they were a pot of poison — those who seek the knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>. 93.

children.text: kṣipanti ye dharma narottamānāṃ śāntaṃ virāgamamṛtānukūlam /
children.translated_text: Those who reject the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) of the best of men, which is peaceful, dispassionate, and conducive to the deathless,

children.text: tān varjayenmīḍhaghaṭāṃ yathaiva ya icchate budhyitumagrabodhim // 94 //
children.translated_text: One should avoid them as one would a pot of excrement — whoever wishes to awaken to supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). 94.

children.text: adhyoṣitā āmiṣa pātracīvare kulasaṃstave caiva sadābhiyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are attached to material offerings, robes, and alms-bowls, always engaged in praising families,

children.text: kurvīta sārdhaṃ na hi teṣu saṃstavaṃ tān varjayedagnikhadhāṃ (khadāṃ) yathaiva // 95 //
children.translated_text: One should not engage in flattery with them; one should avoid them as one would a pit of fire. 95.

children.text: yasyepsitaṃ dharṣayituṃ hi māraṃ pravartituṃ cakravaraṃ hyanuttaram /
children.translated_text: For one who desires to defeat <s>Māra</s> and to turn the unsurpassed, excellent wheel,

children.text: sattvārthamevaṃ vipulaṃ ca kartuṃ varjyāśca tenāpi ca pāpamitrāḥ // 96 //
children.translated_text: And to accomplish such vast benefit for beings — evil friends must be avoided by that one too. 96.

children.text: vivarjayitvā ca priyāpriyāṇi lābhaṃ yaśo bhaṇḍanamānamīrṣyām /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned the pleasant and unpleasant, gain, fame, quarrels, pride, and envy,

children.text: eṣeta nityaṃ sada buddhajñānaṃ ya icchate budhyitumagrabodhim // 97 //
children.translated_text: One should always and constantly seek the knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s> — whoever wishes to awaken to supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). 97.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 132

body.text: catvāra ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ duḥkhavipākā dharmāḥ / katame catvāraḥ ? jñānenābhimanyanatā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ duḥkhavipāko dharmaḥ / īrṣyāmātsaryacittaṃ rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ duḥkhavipāko dharmāḥ / anadhimuktī rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ duḥkhavipāko dharmaḥ / apariśuddhajñānakṣāntisaṃbhogaparyeṣṭī rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ duḥkhavipāko dharmaḥ / ime rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ duḥkhavipākā dharmāḥ //
body.translated_text: These are four dharmas of painful karmic ripening for <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. What are the four? Conceit on account of knowledge, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a dharma of painful ripening for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. A mind of envy and jealousy, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a dharma of painful ripening for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Lack of aspiration, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a dharma of painful ripening for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Seeking the enjoyment of impure knowledge and forbearance, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a dharma of painful ripening for <s>bodhisattvas</s>. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the dharmas of painful karmic ripening for <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke these verses on that occasion:

children.text: dharmadharā bhuvi ye tu bhavanti pūjita sarvajageṣu bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Those who are bearers of the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) on earth are honored in all the worlds;

children.text: avamanyati tāni ājñaḥ (?) tena sa vindati duḥkhamanantam // 98 //
children.translated_text: The ignorant one who despises them obtains endless suffering. 98.

children.text: viṣameṇa sa deśati bhogen chandaruciḥ sada jñāni aśuddhe /
children.translated_text: With partiality one teaches for the sake of gain, always fond of impure knowledge according to one's desire;

children.text: mānonnata yaśca hi nityaṃ namate guruāryajaneṣu // 99 //
children.translated_text: One who is always puffed up with pride does not bow before teachers and noble persons. 99.

children.text: adhimukti na vidyati buddhe dharmagaṇe ca na tasyadhimuktiḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no aspiration toward the <s>Buddha</s>, no aspiration toward the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching) and the <s>Saṅgha</s> (community);

children.text: śikṣa dhuteṣu na tasyadhimuktiḥ pāpamatestrirapāyamukhasya // 100 //
children.translated_text: No aspiration toward the training in <s>dhūta</s> (ascetic) practices — such an evil-minded one faces the doors of the lower realms. 100.

body.text: sa itaścyuto hi manujeṣu karmavaśādabudho hi vimūḍhaḥ /

children.text: narakeṣvatha tiryaggatiṣu pretagatiṣu ca vandati duḥkham / 101 //
children.translated_text: In the hells, in animal births, and in the realm of hungry ghosts, one experiences suffering. 101.

body.translated_text: Having fallen from here, among humans, by the force of <s>karma</s> (action), the fool is utterly deluded;

children.text: yasya matirbhuvi lokapradīpo duḥkhakṣayāntakaro naravīraḥ /
children.translated_text: For one whose understanding is that the lamp of the world, the hero among men, puts an end to suffering,

children.text: tena apāyapathaṃ pravihāya bodhipathaḥ satataṃ hi niṣevyaḥ // 102 //
children.translated_text: By that one, having abandoned the path to the lower realms, the path of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) must always be followed. 102.

body.text: catvārīmāni rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ bandhanāni / katamāni catvāri ? parāvamanyanatā bodhisattvānāṃ bandhanam / laukikenopāyena bhāvanatāprayoganimittasaṃjñā bodhisattvānāṃ bandhanam / anigṛhītacittasya jñānavirahitasya pramādasevanatā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvasya bandhanam / pratibaddhacittasya kulasaṃstavo rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvasya bandhanam / imāni rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvānāṃ catvāri bandhanāni //
body.translated_text: These are four bondages of <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>. What are the four? Contempt for others is a bondage of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. The notion that cultivation through worldly methods constitutes the mark of practice is a bondage of <s>bodhisattvas</s>. Indulgence in negligence by one whose mind is unrestrained and devoid of knowledge, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a bondage of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. Praising families while one's mind is fettered, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, is a bondage of a <s>bodhisattva</s>. These, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the four bondages of <s>bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavaṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke these verses on that occasion:

children.text: avamanyati nitya parasya bhāvayate sada laukikadhyānam /
children.translated_text: One who always despises others and cultivates worldly <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation),

children.text: badhyati tebhi sa dṛṣṭiśatebhiḥ paṅki gajo yatha durbalakāyaḥ // 103 //
children.translated_text: Is bound by hundreds of views, like a weak-bodied elephant in the mud. 103.

children.text: kulasaṃstavabandhanayukto yastu pramatta sadā grahacittaḥ /
children.translated_text: One bound by the bondage of praising families, always negligent, with a grasping mind,

children.text: jñānavivarjita mūḍhamatiśca badhyati ebhi ayuktacarībhiḥ // 104 //
children.translated_text: Devoid of knowledge, of deluded understanding — one is bound by these improper practices. 104.

children.text: yo hyata icchati duḥkhabhayebhyo jātijarāmaraṇādivimokṣam /
children.translated_text: Whoever here desires liberation from the fears of suffering — from birth, old age, death, and the rest,

children.text: so avamanyana manyana tyaktvā yujyati bodhipathe satataṃ ca // 105 //
children.translated_text: That one, having abandoned contempt and conceit, engages constantly on the path of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). 105.

children.text: duḥkhamananta sahitvamaśeṣaṃ sarvasukhādanapekṣi bhavitvā /
children.translated_text: Having endured infinite suffering without remainder, becoming indifferent to all pleasures,

children.text: tyaktva priyāpriyajñātramaśeṣaṃ buddha bhavanti vikalmaṣa dhīrāḥ // 106 //
children.translated_text: Having abandoned all dear ones, unloved ones, and relatives without remainder, the steadfast become <s>Buddhas</s>, free from defilement. 106.

children.text: ṣaṭsu prayujyata bhūmiguṇeṣu balendriyajñāne /
children.translated_text: Engaging in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), which are the virtues of the stages, in the <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), and knowledge,

children.text: sarvaguṇaiśca sadā samupetā buddha bhavejjarapañjaramuktaḥ // 107 //
children.translated_text: Endowed always with all virtues, one becomes a <s>Buddha</s>, freed from the cage of old age. 107.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 133
kalpa acintiya pūrva carantaḥ sattvahitāya caran varabodhau /
children.translated_text: For inconceivable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) in the past, practicing for the benefit of beings on the excellent path of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening),

children.text: dānadame niyame 'pi ca nityaṃ susthita āsi tyajitva ca jñātīn // 108 //
children.translated_text: In <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>dama</s> (self-control), and discipline always, I stood firm, having abandoned relatives. 108.

children.text: prāntavane sada nitya rato 'haṃ śoṣita āśrayu bodhinidānam /
children.translated_text: I was always delighted in the secluded forest, emaciated, taking refuge in <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) as my foundation;

children.text: na ca saṃsṛtu vīryaṃ kadācideṣata jñāna mahāpuruṣāṇām // 109 //
children.translated_text: Never did my effort flag in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), as I sought the knowledge of the great beings. 109.

children.text: bhavacārake jagati dṛṣṭvā pañcagatibhramabhrāmita sattvān /
children.translated_text: Seeing beings wandering in worldly existence, whirled about in the five destinies of transmigration,

children.text: kṛtva kṛpāṃ vipulāmiha pūrve ārjita bodhi balājjagadarthe // 110 //
children.translated_text: Having generated vast compassion formerly, I strove for <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) by the force of merit for the sake of the world. 110.

children.text: duhitṛsvasutāḥ priyabhāryāḥ tyakta purā dhanadhānya prabhūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Daughters, sisters, sons, and beloved wives were abandoned, along with abundant wealth and grain;

children.text: jīvita iṣṭa mahī susamṛddhā eṣata bodhivarāṃ bahukalpān // 111 //
children.translated_text: Life, desires, prosperous lands — I sought the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) for many <s>kalpas</s> (aeons). 111.

children.text: phalapuṣpajalāḍhya suramya āsi vane muni kṣāntirato 'ham /
children.translated_text: In a forest abundant with fruits, flowers, and water, beautiful, I was a sage devoted to patience;

children.text: chinna karau caraṇau kalirājñā naiva mano 'pi tadā mama duṣṭam // 112 //
children.translated_text: When <s>Kalirāja</s> (King Kali) cut off my hands and feet, not even my mind was corrupted at that time. 112.

children.text: vanakandari śyāmaku nāma āsi munirbharato gurujīrṇo /
children.translated_text: In a forest cave, there was a sage named <s>Śyāmaka</s>, who cared for his aged parents;

children.text: dṛḍhabāṇahatena nṛpeṇa naiva manaṃ paridūṣitamāsīt // 113 //
children.translated_text: Though struck by the firm arrow of a king, his mind was not defiled. 113.

children.text: śailataṭādanapekṣya śarīraṃ protsṛjataśca subhāṣitahetoḥ /
children.translated_text: Without regard for the body, casting oneself from a mountain cliff for the sake of well-spoken words,

children.text: kāye na ca me na ca jīve bodhinimittamavekṣya babhūva // 114 //
children.translated_text: I had no attachment to body or to life, having fixed my sight on <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). 114.

children.text: vyāghrisutānapi jīvitahetostyajya tanuṃ paritarpita vyāghrī /
children.translated_text: For the sake of the tigress's cubs, abandoning my body, I satiated the tigress;

children.text: gagane 'bhyanadan surasaṃghāḥ sādhu mahāpuruṣa sthiravīrya // 115 //
children.translated_text: The hosts of <s>devas</s> (gods) resounded in the sky: "Excellent, O great being of steadfast heroism!" 115.

children.text: atidānarataśca yadāsīt māṇava pūrvabhaveṣu caraṃśca /
children.translated_text: When in former births I was a youth devoted to supreme generosity, practicing the path,

children.text: śoṣitu ratnanidāna samudraḥ prāpya maṇiṃ sukhitāḥ kṛta sattvāḥ // 116 //
children.translated_text: I dried up the ocean for the sake of jewels; having obtained the gem, beings were made happy. 116.

children.text: sutasoma mahīpatirāsīt viśrutakīrti caraṃśca yadāham /
children.translated_text: When I was <s>Sutasoma</s>, a king of great and widespread fame, practicing the path,

children.text: vadhyagataṃ kṛtakṛtyanayairme rājaśataṃ parimocitamāśu // 117 //
children.translated_text: A hundred kings who had been led to execution were swiftly liberated by my resolute conduct. 117.

children.text: duḥkhita vīkṣya naraṃ ca daridraṃ tyakta mayā priyameva śarīram /
children.translated_text: Seeing a man suffering and destitute, I gave up my own dear body;

children.text: prāpya dhanaṃ sa kṛtaśca mayāḍhyaḥ sarvadadena nṛpeṇa satā me // 118 //
children.translated_text: Having obtained wealth, he was made prosperous by me — such was I, a king who gave everything, a virtuous one. 118.

children.text: śaraṇāgata vīkṣya kapotaṃ svaṃ piśitaṃ vinikṛtya śarīrāt /
children.translated_text: Seeing a pigeon who had come for refuge, having cut my own flesh from my body,

children.text: dattamapi svatanurna bhayārtastyakta ihāpi nṛpeṇa satā me // 119 //
children.translated_text: I gave it; even my own body was not cause for fear — such was I, a virtuous king who abandoned all. 119.

children.text: kṛtsnamupārjitamāpya bhiṣagbhirbhaiṣajamapratimaṃ mama pūrvam /
children.translated_text: Having obtained all the incomparable medicine gathered by physicians in a former life,
