children.text: jīvita tyajya parasya dadau taṃ kesarirāja babhūva yadāham // 120 //
children.translated_text: I gave it up, sacrificing my own life for the sake of another, when I was <s>Kesarirāja</s> (King of Lions). // 120 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 134
caratā ca purā jagadarthe madri pativrata tyakta saputrā /
children.translated_text: And formerly, while pursuing the welfare of the world, <s>Madrī</s>, the devoted wife, was abandoned along with her sons;

children.text: duhitāpyanapekṣyadasaṃgha āsi nṛpātmajo yada sudaṃṣṭraḥ // 121 //
children.translated_text: even my daughter I gave up without attachment, when I was the prince <s>Sudaṃṣṭra</s>. // 121 //

children.text: varṣasahasra mayā paripūrṇā marṣita duṣkarāścaturaśīti /
children.translated_text: For eighty-four full thousands of years I endured hardships,

children.text: uttaptavīryu yada āsīt arthadhanaśriyo 'pi ca purā me // 122 //
children.translated_text: with blazing vigor, and I also gave up wealth, riches, and glory in former times. // 122 //

children.text: jinadhātustūpapurato me jvalita āśrayaḥ paramabhaktyā /
children.translated_text: Before the <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary shrine) of a <s>Jina</s>'s (Victor's) relics, my body was set ablaze with supreme devotion;

children.text: pūjā kṛtā daśabalānām āsi nṛpātmaji vimalatejāḥ // 123 //
children.translated_text: worship was offered to the <s>Daśabalas</s> (Ten-Powered Ones), when I was the princess <s>Vimalatejā</s> (Pure Radiance). // 123 //

children.text: raudrākṣa eva ca ruṣitvā yācitavān sa cāpi mama śīrṣam /
children.translated_text: <s>Raudrākṣa</s> himself, becoming angry, asked me for my head;

children.text: dattaṃ nikṛtya ca mayā tad rāja yadā ca candraprabha āsīt // 124 //
children.translated_text: and it was given, severed by me, when I was King <s>Candraprabha</s> (Moonlight). // 124 //

children.text: sarvatra grāmanagareṣu vīthimukheṣu bhaiṣajamudāram /
children.translated_text: Everywhere in villages, cities, streets, and crossroads, excellent medicine

children.text: sattvārtha sthāpit mayā te puṇyasamo babhūva ca yadāham // 125 //
children.translated_text: was established by me for the welfare of beings, when I was <s>Puṇyasama</s> (Equal in Merit). // 125 //

children.text: srīṇām sahasramabhirūpāḥ kāñcanamuktibhūṣitaśarīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thousands of beautiful women, their bodies adorned with gold and pearls,

children.text: tyaktāṃ pūrvabhaveṣu caratā me āsi yadā śubho nṛpati pūrve // 126 //
children.translated_text: were renounced by me in former existences, when I was formerly the auspicious king <s>Śubha</s>. // 126 //

children.text: puṣpairvarairapi ca gandhaiḥ kāñcanamuktikāpravara śrīmān /
children.translated_text: With excellent flowers, fragrances, and jewels of gold and pearls, resplendent,

children.text: tyaktaśca me makuṭa pūrva āsi nṛpo yadā ratanacūḍaḥ // 127 //
children.translated_text: my crown too was given up, when I was King <s>Ratanacūḍa</s> (Jewel-Crest). // 127 //

children.text: mṛdutūlapicūpamasūkṣmau komalapadmapatrasukumārau /
children.translated_text: Soft as cotton and silk, delicate as tender lotus petals,

children.text: tyaktau karau sacaraṇau me pūrva nṛpeṇa dhṛtimatā ca // 128 //
children.translated_text: my two hands along with my feet were given up by me, the steadfast king, in a former life. // 128 //

children.text: vinigṛhya rākṣasiśatāni nirghṛṇadāruṇaprabalacaṇḍā /
children.translated_text: Subduing hundreds of <s>rākṣasīs</s> (demonesses), merciless, fierce, powerful, and violent,

children.text: kṛta mānuṣā badaradvīpe siṃhala sārthavāha yada āsīt // 129 //
children.translated_text: they were made human on the island of <s>Badaradvīpa</s>, when I was <s>Siṃhala</s>, the caravan leader. // 129 //

children.text: kāmeṣu mṛrcchitamanā me bāli sa rākṣasī pramadasaṃjñā /
children.translated_text: My mind was infatuated with sensual pleasures — that <s>Bālī</s>, the <s>rākṣasī</s> disguised as a woman —

children.text: pañcaśatāni vaṇijānāṃ mokṣita te yadā bhave sunetraḥ // 130 //
children.translated_text: five hundred merchants were liberated by me when in that birth I was <s>Sunetra</s> (Beautiful Eyes). // 130 //

children.text: catvāri koṭi pramadānām apsaratulyarūpiṇāṃ vihāya /
children.translated_text: Leaving behind forty million women of <s>apsaras</s>-like beauty,

children.text: pravrajya nirgatu jinasya śāsane puṇyaraśmi yada āsīt // 131 //
children.translated_text: I went forth into the teaching of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), when I was <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> (Meritorious Radiance). // 131 //

children.text: mayi tyaktamaṅguli udārā sattvahitārthameva caratā me /
children.translated_text: My noble fingers were given up by me while striving for the welfare of beings,

children.text: jālārcitā vimalaśuddhā kāñcanavarṇa pārthiva yada āsīt // 132 //
children.translated_text: adorned with webs, pure and spotless, of golden hue, when I was King <s>Kāñcanavarṇa</s> (Golden-Colored). // 132 //

children.text: śubha nīlapadmasamavarṇā netra manoramā hṛdayakāntā /
children.translated_text: Beautiful eyes, the color of a fine blue lotus, enchanting to the mind and dear to the heart,

children.text: tyaktā mayā ca jagadarthe utpalanetre pārthiva yadāsīt // 133 //
children.translated_text: were given up by me for the sake of the world, when I was King <s>Utpalanetra</s> (Lotus-Eyed). // 133 //

children.text: priyaviprayogahata dṛṣṭvā strī ca pranaṣṭarūpamativeṣā /
children.translated_text: Seeing a woman afflicted by separation from her beloved, her beauty lost and her appearance wretched,

children.text: parimocitā karuṇayā me keśava vaidyarāja yada āsīt // 134 //
children.translated_text: she was healed by me with compassion, when I was <s>Keśava</s>, the king of physicians. // 134 //

children.text: vyādhyāturaṃ ca naramīkṣya svaṃ rudhiraṃ pradattamapi me 'bhūt /
children.translated_text: And seeing a man afflicted by disease, even my own blood was given;

children.text: nirvyādhitaḥ sa ca kṛto me prāgbhava sarvadarśi yadabhūvam // 135 //
children.translated_text: and he was made free from illness by me, in a former birth when I was <s>Sarvadarśī</s> (All-Seeing). // 135 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 135
hitvā svamasthi ca śarīrād vyādhikṛśasya majja mayā dattam /
children.translated_text: Removing my own bone from my body, I gave the marrow to one emaciated by illness;

children.text: na ca sattva tyakta maya jātu āsi nṛpo yadā kusuma nāma // 136 //
children.translated_text: and never was a being abandoned by me, when I was the king named <s>Kusuma</s> (Flower). // 136 //

children.text: sarvasvakośamapi tyaktva jīvita tyakta me priya manāpam /
children.translated_text: Giving up all my treasury, and sacrificing my dear and cherished life,

children.text: naru mokṣito vyasanaprāpta āsi nṛpo 'rthasiddhi yada pūrvam // 137 //
children.translated_text: a man fallen into calamity was liberated by me, when I was formerly King <s>Arthasiddhi</s> (Accomplished in Wealth). // 137 //

children.text: cakrāṅkitaṃ kamalatulyaṃ paṇiyugaṃ pradamattamanapekṣam /
children.translated_text: My pair of hands, marked with the wheel and resembling lotuses, I gave away without hesitation,

children.text: nṛpa āśuketu yada āsīd bodhimabhīpsamāna jagadarthe // 138 //
children.translated_text: when I was King <s>Āśuketu</s> (Swift-Bannered), aspiring to <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) for the sake of the world. // 138 //

children.text: nṛpa sarvadarśi yada āsīt kāruṇiko janārthahitakāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: When I was King <s>Sarvadarśī</s> (All-Seeing), compassionate, desiring benefit and welfare for people,

children.text: tyaktā mayā caturo 'pi ca dvīpāḥ sphītanarairvranarīśataiśca // 139 //
children.translated_text: four continents were given up by me, with their flourishing inhabitants and hundreds of cities. // 139 //

children.text: mṛdu komalaṃ vikalagauraṃ ūru tacchittva hṝṣṭamuditāyā /
children.translated_text: My thigh, soft, delicate, and fair, having cut it off joyfully,

children.text: dattaṃ svamāṃsa rudhiraṃ me jñānavatī yadāsi nṛpaputrī // 140 //
children.translated_text: I gave my own flesh and blood, when I was the princess <s>Jñānavatī</s> (Possessing Wisdom). // 140 //

children.text: kanakābhapīnasukumāraṃ tyakta stanadvayaṃ hṝdayakāntam /
children.translated_text: A pair of breasts, golden-hued, full, and delicate, dear to the heart, were given up;

children.text: strī prekṣya me kṣudhatṛṣārtaṃ sā rūpya (pa ?) vatīti vanitā yadābhūt // 141 //
children.translated_text: seeing a person afflicted by hunger and thirst, when I was the woman called <s>Rūpyavatī</s> (Beautiful One). // 141 //

children.text: varabhūṣaṇānapi suramyān ratnamanekavastrarathayānān /
children.translated_text: Excellent ornaments, magnificent jewels, many garments, chariots, and vehicles,

children.text: saṃtyakta dustyajamanekaṃ viśrutaśrīnṛpeṇa ca mayābhūt // 142 //
children.translated_text: many hard-to-relinquish things were given up by me, the famous and glorious king. // 142 //

children.text: rājñaḥ suto tu vikṛtajñaḥ tārita sāgarādyada kṛtajñaḥ /
children.translated_text: A king's son, ungrateful, was rescued from the ocean by me, the grateful one;

children.text: ratnārtha netra mama tena uddhṛta naiva me ruṣita cittam // 143 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of jewels he tore out my eyes, yet my mind was not angered. // 143 //

children.text: mā bhūtpipīlikavadho me tyakta varāśrayo 'pi canapekṣya /
children.translated_text: "Let there not be even the killing of an ant by me" — thus I gave up my excellent abode without attachment;

children.text: na ca citta kampita tadā me tyakta pūrvabhaveṣu godha yada āsīt // 144 //
children.translated_text: and my mind was not shaken then, when I gave up my body in former births as an iguana. // 144 //

children.text: upasthānagauravarato 'haṃ vṛddhacarīṣu nitya rata āsīt /
children.translated_text: Devoted to attending upon and honoring elders, I was always delighted in serving the aged;

children.text: na ca mānavānapi ca stabdha āsi kapiṃjalo vicaramāṇaḥ // 145 //
children.translated_text: and I was not arrogant even toward humans, when I was a francolin partridge wandering about. // 145 //

children.text: śaraṇāgatasya ca mayārthe tyakta samucchrayaḥ kṛpa janitvā /
children.translated_text: For the sake of one who had come to me for refuge, I gave up my dwelling out of compassion;

children.text: na ca tyakta vānaragatena vyādhanaraḥ śarābhinihatena // 146 //
children.translated_text: and even when in the form of a monkey, struck by an arrow from a hunter, I did not forsake him. // 146 //

children.text: gajavaśagatena śoṣito me tanurapi vṛddhaguruṃ jagatsmaritvā /
children.translated_text: When I was in the form of an elephant, my body emaciated, remembering the old and venerable one of the world,

children.text: suruciramaśanaṃ mayā na bhuktaṃ mokṣita ātma gajā yadā tadāsīt // 147 //
children.translated_text: I did not eat the beautiful food; I gave up my own body as an elephant at that time. // 147 //

children.text: ṛkṣapatirabhūva śailadurge himahata sapta dināni rakṣito me /
children.translated_text: I became the lord of bears in a mountain fortress; for seven days, one stricken by cold was sheltered by me;

children.text: puruṣa vadhaku tena me prayukto na ca pratighāta kṛtaśca me tadāsmin // 148 //
children.translated_text: that man then sent a killer after me, yet no retaliation was made by me against him. // 148 //

children.text: āsi gajo himakundanikāśo bodhivarāśrita buddhaguṇārthī /
children.translated_text: I was an elephant, white as snow and jasmine, devoted to the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), seeking the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: sa viṣeṇa śareṇa ca viddho daṃṣṭravarāṃstyajamāna na dviṣṭaḥ // 149 //
children.translated_text: though pierced by a poisoned arrow, I did not hate even while giving up my excellent tusks. // 149 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 136

body.text:
vanagocari khaṇḍakadvīpe tittiripotaka maitravihārī /
sahadarśanena śamito 'gniṃ devagaṇā kusumāni kṣipanti // 150 // gaṅgataraṅgajalairhiyamāṇaḥ tārita me yada āsi mṛgatve /

children.text: vadhakā mama tenapanītā naiva mano mama tatra praduṣṭam // 151 //
children.translated_text: hunters were led away from me, yet my mind was not corrupted toward them. // 151 //

body.translated_text: Dwelling in the forest on the island of <s>Khaṇḍaka</s>, I was a baby partridge, abiding in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness); by my mere sight the fire was pacified, and hosts of <s>devas</s> (gods) showered flowers. // 150 // Carried away by the waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s waters, beings were rescued by me when I was in an animal birth;

children.text: tārita pañcaśataṃ vaṇijānāṃ sāgaramadhyagatāśca anāthāḥ /
children.translated_text: Five hundred merchants, stranded in the midst of the ocean, helpless, were rescued;

children.text: taiśca hataḥ kṣudhitaiśca tadāhaṃ kacchapayonigato 'pi ca maitraḥ // 152 //
children.translated_text: and though killed by them when they were hungry, I remained friendly even in the birth of a turtle. // 152 //

children.text: bodhicariṃ caramāṇahu pūrvaṃ matsya babhūva yadā jalacarī /
children.translated_text: While pursuing the <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of awakening) formerly, when I was a fish, a water-dweller,

children.text: tyakta mayāśraya sattvahitāya bhakṣita prāṇisahasraśatebhiḥ // 153 //
children.translated_text: my body was given up for the welfare of beings, and I was eaten by hundreds of thousands of creatures. // 153 //

children.text: vyādhiśatābhihataṃ jagadīkṣya samucchraya kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: Seeing the world afflicted by hundreds of diseases, having given up my body,

children.text: sattva kṛtāḥ sukhitā nirujāśca prāṇaku saumya tadā ca yadāsīt // 154 //
children.translated_text: beings were made happy and free from illness, when I was the gentle creature called <s>Prāṇaku</s>. // 154 //

children.text: siṃha babhūva yadā mṛgarājā sthāmabalānvita kāruṇikaśca /
children.translated_text: When I was a lion, king of beasts, endowed with strength and power, and compassionate,

children.text: viddha śareṇa na dūṣita cittaṃ maitri tadā vadhake 'pi tadā me // 155 //
children.translated_text: though pierced by an arrow, my mind was not corrupted; I had <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) even toward the hunter at that time. // 155 //

children.text: śaṅkhatuṣāranibho hayarājā āsi purā ca samudrataṭe 'ham /
children.translated_text: I was a horse-king, white as a conch shell and snow, formerly on the shore of the ocean;

children.text: rākṣasimadhyagatā vaṇijo me tārita kṛtva kṛpāṃ karuṇāṃ ca // 156 //
children.translated_text: merchants who had fallen among <s>rākṣasīs</s> (demonesses) were rescued by me, with compassion and mercy. // 156 //

children.text: bodhicariṃ caramāṇa janārthe āsi kuṇāla ahaṃ yada pakṣī /
children.translated_text: While pursuing the <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of awakening) for the sake of people, when I was the bird <s>Kuṇāla</s>,

children.text: varjita kāmaguṇā bahudoṣā no ca vaśaṃ pramadāna gato 'ham // 157 //
children.translated_text: I avoided the greatly faulty sensual pleasures and did not come under the power of women. // 157 //

children.text: āsi śaśo vanagulmanivāsī śāsatī taṃ sukṛte śaśavargam /
children.translated_text: I was a hare, dwelling in the forest thickets, instructing the hare community in virtuous deeds;

children.text: munirāśramavāsi kṣudhārtastasya kṛtena mayāśrayu tyaktaḥ // 158 //
children.translated_text: a sage dwelling in a hermitage, afflicted by hunger — for his sake I gave up my own body. // 158 //

children.text: āsi śuko drumapuṣpaphalāḍhyo śuṣkadrumo na ca me sa hi tyaktaḥ /
children.translated_text: I was a parrot on a tree rich with flowers and fruits; even when the tree became withered, I did not abandon it;

children.text: dṛṣṭa kṛtajña tadā mama śakrastaṃ kṛtavāṃstaru patraphalāḍhyam // 159 //
children.translated_text: seeing my gratitude, <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) then made that tree full of leaves and fruits again. // 159 //

children.text: vānarasaṃghamupadruta dṝṣṭvā nāganṛpeṇa vivarjītadeśam /
children.translated_text: Seeing a troop of monkeys harassed and driven from their territory by the <s>Nāga</s> king,

children.text: rājabhayāttu vimokṣita te me vānararāja ahaṃ yada āsīt // 160 //
children.translated_text: they were liberated from the fear of the king by me, when I was the monkey king. // 160 //

children.text: śuka bhūta purā guruhetoḥ śāli haraṃśca nareṇa gṛhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: Formerly, as a parrot, for the sake of my parents, while carrying rice, I was caught by a man:

children.text: kiṃ nu śukā harase mama śāli nāśayate 'pi ca pakṣi maśasyam ( matsasyam) // 161 //
children.translated_text: "Why do you steal my rice, O parrot? This bird destroys my crop!" // 161 //

children.text: śuka so 'bravīdbhadra śṛṇuṣva caurya harāmi na te ahu śālim /
children.translated_text: The parrot replied: "Good sir, listen! I do not steal your rice as a thief;

children.text: jīrṇagurudvayapoṣaṇahetoḥ śāli harāmi kṛpārtha tu teṣām // 162 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of nourishing my two aged parents, I carry the rice out of compassion for them." // 162 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 137
bīja prakīrṇa yadā prathamaṃ te bhāga dadāmi sarvajanasya /
children.translated_text: "When your seed was first sown, I gave a share to all beings;

children.text: tacca giraṃ vadato mama śrutvā tenāpi caurya bhavenna kadācit // 163 //
children.translated_text: and hearing this word spoken by me, he said: 'Then there shall never be theft from you.' // 163 //

children.text: sādhu śukā hara śāli yatheṣṭaṃ durlabha mānuṣa yasyimu bhaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Well done, O parrot, take rice as you wish! Rare is the human who has such devotion;

children.text: mānuṣa tvaṃ maya tīryagatehā sādhu damaḥ śama saṃyama tubhyam // 164 //
children.translated_text: you, though born as an animal, are human to me — well done are your restraint, tranquility, and self-control!' // 164 //

children.text: ityevamāni caritāni pūrva caranta duṣkara kṛtāni /
children.translated_text: Thus were these former deeds performed by me, difficult austerities while practicing the path;

children.text: na ca me manasi tatra bhavi kheda eṣata uttamāṃ viraja bodhim // 165 //
children.translated_text: and there was no weariness in my mind, seeking the supreme, stainless <s>bodhi</s> (awakening). // 165 //

children.text: ādhyātmikaṃ hyatha ca bāhyaṃ nāsti hi vastu yanmayā na dattam /
children.translated_text: Whether internal or external, there is no thing that was not given by me;

children.text: śīle ca kṣānti tatha vīrya dhyāna upāya prajña carito 'ham // 166 //
children.translated_text: in <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>upāya</s> (skillful means), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) have I practiced. // 166 //

children.text: māṃsaṃ tvacaṃ tathapi ca majja śoṇitameva datta svaśarīrāt /
children.translated_text: Flesh, skin, and also marrow, blood itself was given from my own body;

children.text: prānte guhāsu ca yadā me śoṣita āśrayo 'pi caratā me // 167 //
children.translated_text: and at the end, in caves, my body was emaciated while I practiced austerities. // 167 //

children.text: dhutayāna deśita jinebhiḥ yatra prayujyato jina bhavanti /
children.translated_text: The <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic practices) taught by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), by which one becomes a <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: tatra dhute satataṃ ca prayukto āsi caranta pure ahu nityam // 168 //
children.translated_text: in those ascetic practices I was constantly engaged, always practicing them in the past. // 168 //

children.text: etādṛśā vrata udārā ye ca niṣevitā caratā me /
children.translated_text: Such were the noble vows that were observed by me while practicing;

children.text: śrutvā ca teṣamimāścaryamekapade na bhaviṣyati chandaḥ // 169 //
children.translated_text: yet upon hearing these, in that very moment, there will be no desire for them among some. // 169 //

children.text: hāsyu bhaviṣyati ima śruṇitvā śāsanametadeva ca taḍānīm /
children.translated_text: There will be laughter upon hearing this teaching at that time;

children.text: āhāramaithunaparāste middhasadābhibhūta śatakāṅkṣāḥ // 170 //
children.translated_text: they will be devoted to food and sexual intercourse, constantly overcome by sloth, full of doubts. // 170 //

children.text: dharmadviṣaḥ sada anāryāḥ śāsanadūṣakā guṇavihīnāḥ /
children.translated_text: Haters of the <s>Dharma</s>, always ignoble, corrupters of the teaching, devoid of virtues;

children.text: śrutvā ca dharmamima śāntaṃ naiṣa jinokta ityabhivadanti // 171 //
children.translated_text: and hearing this peaceful <s>Dharma</s>, they will say: "This is not spoken by the <s>Jina</s> (Victor)." // 171 //

children.text: ācāryo me śrutasamudro āsi bahuśrutaḥ kathikaśreṣṭhaḥ /
children.translated_text: "My teacher was an ocean of learning, greatly learned, the foremost of preachers;

children.text: tenāpi caiṣa pratiṣiddho buddhavaco hi naiṣa tu kathaṃcit // 172 //
children.translated_text: even by him this was rejected — this is certainly not the word of the <s>Buddha</s>." // 172 //

children.text: parato 'pyabhūdapi ca vṛddhaḥ tasya guruḥ sa śāmitaguṇaughaḥ /
children.translated_text: "And beyond him there was another, elder, his teacher, one in whom the flood of virtues was stilled;

children.text: tenāpi naiṣa hi gṛhīto mātra prayujyatha vitathametat // 173 //
children.translated_text: even by him this was not accepted — you are merely practicing what is false." // 173 //

children.text: yatrātma nāsti na ca jīvo deśita pudgalo 'pi na kathaṃcit /
children.translated_text: "Where there is no self and no soul, and no person whatsoever is taught,

children.text: vyarthaḥ śramo 'tra ghaṭate yaḥ śīlaprayoga saṃvarakriyā ca // 174 //
children.translated_text: the effort exerted there is futile, as are the practices of moral conduct and restraint." // 174 //

children.text: yadyasti caiva mahāyānaṃ nātra hi ātma sattva manujo vā /
children.translated_text: "Even if there is the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle), in it there is no self, being, or person;

children.text: vyarthaḥ śramo 'tra hi kṛto me yatra na cātmasattvaupalabdhiḥ // 175 //
children.translated_text: the effort I have made there is futile, where neither self nor being is apprehended." // 175 //

children.text: kavitāni haiva svamatāni pāpamataiḥ kutīrthikamataiśca /
children.translated_text: "These are merely clever compositions, their own fabrications, with wicked views like those of non-Buddhist heretics;

children.text: bhāṣeta no jina kadācit vācamimāṃ hi bhikṣuparibhāṣām // 176 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) would never speak such words" — thus will monks revile them. // 176 //

children.text: hrīrapatrāpaśīlacaritāśca dhvāṅkṣa pragambha uddhatapracaṇḍāḥ /
children.translated_text: Without shame, without moral conscience, conducting themselves shamelessly, bold as crows, arrogant, and violent,

children.text: bhavitā hi bhikṣava mameha śāsani īrṣyamānamadadagdhāḥ // 177 //
children.translated_text: such will be the monks in my teaching here, burnt by envy, pride, and conceit. // 177 //

children.text: vidhyanta hasta tathā pādāṃścīvarakarṇakā nidhunantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Scratching their hands and feet, shaking the corners of their robes,

children.text: kāṣāyakaṇṭha vicarantā grāmakuleṣu madyamadamattāḥ // 178 //
children.translated_text: wearing the saffron robe around their necks, they will wander among village households, intoxicated with drink. // 178 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 138

body.text:
buddhasya te dhvaja gṛhītvā sevakarā gṛhasthajanatāyām /
lekhaṃ vahanti satataṃ te śāsanadaṃ vihāya guṇarāśim / 179 // gogardabhāśvapaśudānātsaṃbhavate hi dāsya pi teṣām /

children.text: kṛṣikarmavāṇijyaprayogā yuktamanāśca te 'niśamāryāḥ // 180 //
children.translated_text: engaged in farming, trade, and commerce, their minds always occupied — these so-called noble ones! // 180 //

body.translated_text: Having taken up the banner of the <s>Buddha</s>, they become servants of the laity; they constantly carry messages, abandoning the heap of virtues that is the teaching. // 179 // From the giving of cows, donkeys, horses, and livestock, even servitude arises for them;

children.text: naiṣāmanāryamapi vācyaṃ naiva ca kiṃcidasti yadakāryam /
children.translated_text: Nothing is unspeakable for these ignoble ones, and there is nothing that is not done by them;

children.text: staupika sāṃghikaṃ hyapi ca vittaṃ paugdalikaṃ ca yacca samameṣām // 181 //
children.translated_text: even the wealth belonging to <s>stūpas</s> (reliquary shrines), the <s>Saṅgha</s> (community), and individuals is the same to them. // 181 //

children.text: bhikṣuṇa vīkṣya ca guṇāḍhyaṃ teṣvapi cāpyavarṇa kathayanti /
children.translated_text: Seeing a monk who is rich in virtues, they speak ill of him too;

children.text: duḥśīla vañcaka praviśya kuhāste strī ca vināśayanti hi sughorāḥ // 182 //
children.translated_text: immoral and deceitful ones enter, and with their tricks and women they wreak terrible destruction. // 182 //

children.text: gṛddho gṛhīṇa tathā kāmairyādṛśe pravrajitva te gṛddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Greedy for the same sensual pleasures as householders — such is their greed even after going forth;

children.text: bhāryāṃ sutā duhitaraśca teṣu bhaviṣya gṛhisamānam // 183 //
children.translated_text: they will have wives, sons, and daughters, living just like householders. // 183 //

children.text: yatraiva satkṛta kule te cīvarapiṇḍapātaparibhogaiḥ /
children.translated_text: In whatever family they are honored with robes, alms-food, and requisites,

children.text: tasyaiva dāraparigṛddhā kleśavaśānugāḥ sada anāryāḥ // 184 //
children.translated_text: they become greedy for the wives of that very family — always ignoble, following the power of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). // 184 //

children.text: kāmā ime khalu na sevyāḥ pātana tiryakpretanirayeṣu /
children.translated_text: "These sensual pleasures should indeed not be indulged in — they cause one to fall into animal realms, <s>preta</s> (hungry ghost) realms, and hells" —

children.text: vakṣyanti te sada gṛhīṇāṃ te ca svayamadānta anupaśāntāḥ // 185 //
children.translated_text: thus they will constantly preach to the householders, yet they themselves are untamed and unpeaceful. // 185 //

children.text: svayameva te yatha adāntāḥ śiṣyagaṇo 'pi teṣa na sudāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as they themselves are untamed, the group of their disciples is also not well-tamed;

children.text: āhāramaithunakathāyāṃ rātridivāni teṣu gamiṣyanti // 186 //
children.translated_text: their days and nights will pass in talk of food and sexual intercourse. // 186 //

children.text: sevārthameva na guṇārthaṃ te khalu saṃgrahaṃ dadati teṣām /
children.translated_text: Only for the sake of service, not for the sake of virtue, do they gather followers;

children.text: śiṣyagaṇaiḥ svakaiḥ parivṛto 'haṃ pūja jane sadātra cala sidhya // 187 //
children.translated_text: "Surrounded by my own group of disciples, I shall always be honored among people; come, succeed!" // 187 //

children.text: kathayanti te 'pi ca janasya saṃgraha eṣa me karuṇayaiṣām /
children.translated_text: They tell the people: "This gathering of mine is out of compassion for them;

children.text: upasthāma prārthayāmi tebhya śiṣyagaṇebhya eva na kadācit // 188 //
children.translated_text: I seek service from them" — yet never truly for the sake of their disciples. // 188 //

children.text: rogābhibhūta bahu tatra kuṣṭhilāścitragātrasuvirūpāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many there will be overcome by diseases — lepers, with mottled and deformed bodies,

children.text: pravrajiṣyanti narakeṣu āgatā āgatā sada anāryāḥ // 189 //
children.translated_text: they will go forth as monks, but destined for the hells, always arriving and arriving again, ever ignoble. // 189 //

children.text: uddeśasaṃvaravihīnā bhikṣuguṇeṣu te sada viyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Devoid of scriptural recitation and moral restraint, always lacking the qualities of a monk,

children.text: gṛhiṇo na te 'pi vna ca bhikṣū varjita te yathā śmaśāna iva dāruḥ // 190 //
children.translated_text: they are neither householders nor monks — they are rejected like firewood in a cremation ground. // 190 //

children.text: śikṣāsu cādara na teṣāṃ syānna ca prātimokṣavinaye vā /
children.translated_text: They will have no respect for the training rules, nor for the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (code of discipline) and <s>Vinaya</s> (monastic rules);

children.text: uddāmagāḥ svavaśagāste aṅkuśamuktakā iva gajendrāḥ // 191 //
children.translated_text: unrestrained, following their own will, they are like lordly elephants released from the goad. // 191 //

children.text: vanavāsināmapi hi teṣāṃ grāmagataṃ bhaviṣyati hi cittam /
children.translated_text: Even among those who dwell in the forest, their minds will be fixed on the village;

children.text: kleśāgninā prapatitānāṃ cittamavasthitaṃ hi na ca teṣām // 192 //
children.translated_text: for those who have fallen into the fire of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), their minds have no stability. // 192 //

children.text: vismṛtya buddhaguṇa sarvān śikṣadhutāṃśca te 'pi ca upāyāna /
children.translated_text: Having forgotten all the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, and those trainings and <s>dhūta</s> (ascetic) practices as well,

children.text: madamānadarpaparipūrṇāṃ te prapatanti dāruṇavīcīm // 193 //
children.translated_text: filled with intoxication, pride, and arrogance, they fall into the terrible [hell of] <s>Avīci</s>. // 193 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 139
rājakathāratāśca satataṃ te corakathābhikīrtanaratāśca /
children.translated_text: And they are constantly delighted in tales of kings, and fond of recounting tales of thieves,

children.text: jñātiniṣevane ca niratāste cintayamāna rātriṃdivasāni // 194 //
children.translated_text: and absorbed in attending to relatives, thinking about [such things] day and night. // 194 //

children.text: dhyānaṃ tathādhyayanaṃ tyaktvā nitya vihārakarmaṇi niyuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned meditation and likewise study, always engaged in monastery tasks,

children.text: āvāsagṛdhrakuṭīkāste ca adāntaśiṣyaparivārāḥ // 195 //
children.translated_text: greedy for dwellings and cells, surrounded by undisciplined disciples. // 195 //

children.text: na ca karmiko hyahaṃ vihāre ātmana hetureṣa hi kṛto me /
children.translated_text: 'I am surely not a laborer in the monastery—this was made for my own sake.'

children.text: ye bhikṣavo mamānukūlāsteṣvavakāśamasti hi vihāre // 196 //
children.translated_text: 'Those monks who are agreeable to me—for them there is room in the monastery.' // 196 //

children.text: ye śīlavanta guṇavanto dharmadharā janārthamabhiyuktāṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Those who are virtuous, endowed with good qualities, who uphold the <s>Dharma</s>, who are devoted to the welfare of people,'

children.text: damasaṃyame satatayuktāḥ saṃgraha teṣu te na kurute ca // 197 //
children.translated_text: 'who are constantly engaged in self-restraint and discipline—they make no accommodation for them.' // 197 //

children.text: layanaṃ mamaitaduddiṣṭaṃ sārdhavihāriṇo 'pi ca mamedam /
children.translated_text: 'This dwelling was designated as mine; and these are my co-residents;'

children.text: saṃmodikasya ca mamedaṃ gaccha na te 'sti vāsa iha kaścit // 198 //
children.translated_text: 'and this belongs to my companion—go away, there is no place for you here!' // 198 //

children.text: śayyāsanaṃ nikhila dattaṃ bhikṣavaḥ sthāpitā iha prabhūtāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Beds and seats—all have been given away; monks have been installed here in abundance.'

children.text: na ca lābhasaṃbhava ihāsti kiṃ paribhokṣyase 'tra vraja bhikṣo // 199 //
children.translated_text: 'There is no possibility of gain here—what will you enjoy? Go away, O monk!' // 199 //

children.text: śayyāsanoddiśana teṣāṃ naiva bhaviṣyate 'pi ca kadācit /
children.translated_text: 'There will never be any designation of beds and seats for them;'

children.text: gṛhisaṃcayāśca bhavitāraste ca prabhūtabhāṇḍaparivārāḥ // 200 //
children.translated_text: 'they will become householders with accumulations, surrounded by abundant possessions.' // 200 //

children.text: nirbhartsitā pi ca samantātte hi mamaurasāścarimakāle /
children.translated_text: 'Even though rebuked from all sides, for they are my own [spiritual] sons in the final age,'

children.text: vacanaṃ na caite mam hi smṛtvā prāntavane tadābhinivasanti // 201 //
children.translated_text: 'they do not heed my words; remembering, they then take up dwelling in remote forests.' // 201 //

children.text: hā śāsanaṃ jinavarasya nāśamupekṣya hi nacireṇa /
children.translated_text: 'Alas! The teaching of the supreme <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One)—looking on with indifference as it is destroyed before long,'

children.text: lābhābhibhūta guṇadviṣṭā bhikṣavaḥ prādurbhūta bahu yatra // 202 //
children.translated_text: 'overcome by gain, hostile to good qualities—[a time] where many such monks have appeared.' // 202 //

children.text: paribhūtakāśca satataṃ te paścimakāli śīlaguṇayuktāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'And constantly scorned in the last age will be those endowed with moral virtue and good qualities;'

children.text: te cāpyaraṇyavanavāsī grāma vihāya rāṣṭranagarāṇi // 203 //
children.translated_text: 'they too will dwell in the wilderness forests, having abandoned villages, kingdoms, and cities.' // 203 //

children.text: sada satkṛtā guṇavihīnā bhedaka sūcakāḥ kalahakāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Always honored [will be] those devoid of qualities—slanderers, informers, lovers of quarrel;'

children.text: te śāstṛsaṃmata janasya te ca bhaviṣyanti mānamadadagdhāḥ // 204 //
children.translated_text: 'they will be [regarded as] approved by the Master by people, and they will be burned by pride and intoxication.' // 204 //

children.text: ima śāsanaṃ guṇanidhānaṃ sarvaguṇākāraṃ paramaramyam /
children.translated_text: 'This teaching, a treasury of qualities, the embodiment of all virtues, supremely beautiful,'

children.text: nāśaṃ prayāsyati mameha śīlavipattirirṣyamadadoṣaiḥ // 205 //
children.translated_text: 'will go to destruction here through the faults of moral failure, envy, and intoxication.' // 205 //

children.text: ratnākaro yatha viluptaḥ sthāsyati padminīva pariśuṣkā /
children.translated_text: 'Like a mine of gems that has been plundered, it will stand like a dried-up lotus pond;'

children.text: yūpa vararatnamayaṃ bhagnaṃ naśyati śāsanaṃ carimakāle // 206 //
children.translated_text: 'like a broken sacrificial post made of excellent jewels—the teaching is destroyed in the final age.' // 206 //

children.text: pretādṛśaścarimakāle dharmavilopa vartato sughoraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Like ghosts in the final age, those who engage in the destruction of the <s>Dharma</s>—terribly—'

children.text: te cāpi bhikṣava adāntā nāśayitāraḥ śāsanaṃ mamedam // 207 //
children.translated_text: 'those undisciplined monks too will be the destroyers of this my teaching.' // 207 //

children.text: ma caryasevaniratānāṃ dūrata saṃgatiḥ kvacana teṣām /
children.translated_text: 'Those who are devoted to evil conduct—far away is any association with them;'

children.text: pretagatirnrake 'pi ca vāsaḥ tiryagatiśca ito hi cyutānām // 208 //
children.translated_text: 'the realm of hungry ghosts (<s>pretagati</s>), and dwelling in hell, and the animal realm—[these await] those who have fallen from here.' // 208 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 140
anubhūya tīvrakaṭukāni duḥkhamananta varṣaśatamanekaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having experienced intense and bitter sufferings for innumerable hundreds of years,'

children.text: labdhvā sa mānuṣabhavaṃ vā jāyati duḥkhitaḥ satata śocyaḥ // 209 //
children.translated_text: 'even if they obtain a human birth, they are born miserable, constantly to be pitied.' // 209 //

children.text: andho 'tha vā badhira kāṇo jāyati citragātra suvirūpā /
children.translated_text: 'Blind, or deaf, or one-eyed—they are born with disfigured bodies, ugly,'

children.text: bībhatsarūpabhayadarśī pāpacarīmimāṃ satata sevī // 210 //
children.translated_text: 'of fearful, loathsome appearance—one who constantly pursues this evil conduct.' // 210 //

children.text: viśrambhate 'sya na ca kaścit śraddadhate 'sya cāpi na ca vākyam /
children.translated_text: 'No one trusts him, nor does anyone have faith in his words;'

children.text: nirbharstito bhavati nityaṃ yo 'bhiniṣevate viṣamacaryām // 211 //
children.translated_text: 'constantly rebuked is the one who pursues wrong conduct.' // 211 //

children.text: te rogaduḥkhaśatataptāstāḍita loṣṭakāṣṭhapraharebhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'They are tormented by hundreds of diseases and sufferings, struck by blows of clods and sticks,'

children.text: kṣuttṛṣṇa yena paritaptāste ca bhavanti sadā suparibhūtāḥ // 212 //
children.translated_text: 'afflicted by hunger and thirst, they are constantly greatly despised.' // 212 //

children.text: duḥkhā ananta iti jñātvā dūra pāpacaryaṃ vijahitvā /
children.translated_text: 'Having understood that sufferings are infinite, having abandoned evil conduct far away,'

children.text: sevetha sādhucari nityaṃ mā bhavitānutāpa iha paścāt // 213 //
children.translated_text: 'always pursue good conduct—let there not be remorse afterward!' // 213 //

children.text: yasya priyo bhavati buddho āryagaṇaśca śikṣa dhutadharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'One to whom the <s>Buddha</s> is dear, and the noble <s>Saṃgha</s>, and the trainings and <s>dhūta</s> (ascetic) practices—'

children.text: abhiyujyathā satatamevaṃ tyaktva ca jñātralābhayaśakīrti // 214 //
children.translated_text: 'strive always thus, having abandoned relatives, gain, fame, and glory!' // 214 //

children.text: māyopamaṃ hi (bhi ?) durametatsvapnasamaṃ ca saṃskṛtamavīkṣyam /
children.translated_text: 'For this [existence] is like an illusion, difficult [to see through], and like a dream—conditioned [reality] is not to be regarded [as permanent];'

children.text: nacirādbhaviṣyati viyogaḥ sarvapriyairna nityamiha kaścit // 215 //
children.translated_text: 'before long there will be separation from all that is dear—nothing here is permanent.' // 215 //

children.text: udyujyatāṃ ghaṭata nityaṃ pāramitāsu bhūmiṣu baleṣu /
children.translated_text: 'Exert yourselves, strive constantly in the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), in the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), and in the powers!'

children.text: mā jātu saṃśayata vīryaṃ yāvanna budhyathā pravarabodhim // 216 //
children.translated_text: 'Never doubt your vigor until you awaken to the supreme <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment)!' // 216 //

body.text: nidānaparivartaḥ prathamaḥ //
body.translated_text: End of the first chapter, the <s>Nidāna-parivarta</s> (Introduction Chapter).

body.text: dvitīyaḥ parivartaḥ /
body.translated_text: Second Chapter.

body.text: yadbhūyasā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvayānīyānāṃ pudgalānāmime doṣā bhaviṣyanti - anabhiyuktā anabhiyuktān pūjayiṣyanti, śaṭhāḥ śaṭhān pūjayiṣyanti, ajñā ajñān satkartavyān manyante, āmiṣapriyāśca bhaviṣyanti / adhyavasāne bahulāḥ kulamatsarāḥ śaṭhā dhvāṅkṣā mukharāḥ kuhakāḥ kṣātragurukāḥ / anyonyavarṇabhāṣaṇatayā lābhaṃ niṣpādayiṣyanti / lābhaparyeṣṭyarthaṃ ca te grāmaṃ pravekṣyanti, na sattvaparipākārthaṃ na sattvānukampārtham / te ajñānino jñānanimittamātmānaṃ pratijñāsyanti - kathaṃ māṃ pare vijānīyuḥ ? bahuśrutaḥ kalyāṇadharma iti / agauravāśca bhaviṣyanti yathātrānabhiyuktāḥ / bhinnabhājanībhūtā bhaviṣyanti anyonyaskhalitagaveṣiṇaḥ / naṣṭaprayogā ajñāḥ kusīdājñānā navakalpanabahulāḥ / anyonyabhinnadharmasaṃgāyanatayā svacchandā dṛḍhavairā ākīrṇavyāpādā ayuktaparibhāṣāñjanasaṃjñaptyā iha śāsane cariṣyanti āparipṛcchanaśīlāḥ / dharmaśravaṇenānarthikāḥ / ayuktacaryayā daridrakuleṣūpapattiṃ parigṛhīṣyanti / te daridrakule pravrajitāḥ samānā lābhamātrakeneha śāsane tuṣṭimutpādayiṣyanti / teṣāmatyayadeśanāpi na bhaviṣyati kiṃ punarjñānābhisamayaḥ / te buddhaguṇān ricitvā jñātralābhamātrakena śrava(ma)ṇāḥ sma ityātmānaṃ pratijñāsyanti / nāhaṃ rāṣṭrapāla teṣāṃ tathārūpāṇāṃ (

children.text: Vaidya, RP 141
children.translated_text: (Vaidya, RP 141)

children.text: ) pudgalānāmānulomikāmapi kṣāntiṃ vadāmi kutaḥ punarbuddhajñānam / sugatisteṣāṃ dūre, kiṃ punarbodhiḥ / teṣāṃ punā rāṣṭrapāla tathārūpāṇāṃ pudgalānāmaṣṭau bodheḥ paripanthakarān dharmān vadāmi / katamānaṣṭau ? apāyopapattiḥ daridrakulopapattiḥ pratyantajanapadopattiḥ nīcalukopapattirdurvarṇatāndhatvagatikāḥ pāpamitrasamavadhānaṃ bahumānyatā viṣamāparihāreṇa kālakriyāḥ / imān rāṣṭrapāla aṣṭau dharmān bodheḥ paripanthakarān vadāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ ? nāhaṃ rāṣṭrapāla vacanapratijñasya bodhimiti vadāmi / na kuhakasya caryāpariśuddhiṃ vadāmi / na śaṭhasya bodhicaryāṃ vadāmi / nāmiṣagurukasya buddhapūjāṃ vadāmi / nābhimāninaḥ prajñāpariśuddhiṃ vadāmi / nāhaṃ duṣprajñasamanvāgatasya saṃśayacchedanaṃ vadāmi / nāhaṃ matsariṇa āśayapariśuddhiṃ vadāmi / nāhamanadhimuktibahulasya dhāraṇīpratilābhaṃ vadāmi / nāhamasadguṇaparyeṣakasya sugatipratilābhaṃ vadāmi / na kulamatsarasya kāyapariśuddhiṃ vadāmi / nāhamakalpitāryapathasya buddhasamavadhānaṃ vadāmi / na kulādhyavasitasya vākpariśuddhiṃ vadāmi / na gauravasya cittapariśuddhiṃ vadāmi / nāhamamātrajñasya dharmakāmatāṃ vadāmi / na kāyajīvitasāpekṣasya dharmaveṣṭiṃ vadāmi / nāhaṃ rāṣṭrapāla ṣaṭaśāstṝṃstathā vigarhāmi yathā tān mohapuruṣān vigarhāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ ? anyathāvādinaste anyathākāriṇaḥ, visaṃvādakāḥ sadevakasya lokasya //
children.translated_text: persons, much less of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. A good destiny is far from them, how much more so <s>bodhi</s>! Furthermore, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, I speak of eight <s>dharmas</s> that obstruct <s>bodhi</s> for such persons. What are the eight? Rebirth in the lower realms, rebirth in a poor family, rebirth in a border region, rebirth in a low tribe, ugliness, blindness and [defective] gait, association with evil friends, excessive pride, and death through incurable ailments. These, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, are the eight <s>dharmas</s> that I declare to be obstructive to <s>bodhi</s>. For what reason? I do not speak, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, of <s>bodhi</s> for one who merely claims it by words. I do not speak of purification of conduct for the fraudulent. I do not speak of <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct toward awakening) for the deceitful. I do not speak of worship of the <s>Buddha</s> for one devoted to material gain. I do not speak of purification of wisdom for the conceited. I do not speak of the cutting of doubt for one possessed of poor wisdom. I do not speak of purification of intention for the miserly. I do not speak of attainment of <s>dhāraṇī</s> (power of retention) for one lacking aspiration. I do not speak of attainment of a good destiny for one who seeks unreal qualities. I do not speak of purification of body for one who is covetous of families. I do not speak of encountering a <s>Buddha</s> for one who has not cultivated the noble path. I do not speak of purification of speech for one devoted to families. I do not speak of purification of mind for one lacking reverence. I do not speak of love of the <s>Dharma</s> for one who does not know moderation. I do not speak of devotion to the <s>Dharma</s> for one who clings to body and life. O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, I do not condemn the six [non-Buddhist] teachers as much as I condemn those deluded men. For what reason? Because they speak one way and act another way; they are deceivers of the world with its gods.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, for the most part, these faults will arise among persons belonging to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle: the undiligent will honor the undiligent; the deceitful will honor the deceitful; the ignorant will consider the ignorant worthy of respect; and they will be lovers of material gain. They will be abundant in worldly pursuits, covetous of families, deceitful, crafty, garrulous, fraudulent, and devoted to <s>Kṣatriya</s> teachers. Through mutual praise, they will procure gain. They will enter villages for the purpose of seeking gain, not for the ripening of beings, not out of compassion for beings. Those ignorant ones will claim to be knowledgeable—'How shall others recognize me as learned, of good qualities?' And they will be disrespectful, just as the undiligent [are] here. They will become broken vessels, seeking each other's faults. With lost practice, ignorant, lazy in their ignorance, abundant in new fabrications. Through mutual disagreement in reciting the <s>Dharma</s>, self-willed, with firm enmity, filled with malice, they will conduct themselves in this teaching through the notion of inappropriate censure, being of the nature of not inquiring. They will have no interest in hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Through improper conduct, they will take rebirth in poor families. Having gone forth [as monks] in those poor families, they will generate contentment in this teaching through mere gain alone. For them, there will not even be confession of transgressions, much less the realization of knowledge. Having abandoned the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, through mere acquisition of relatives, they will claim 'We are <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics).' I do not speak, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, even of the acquiescent patience (<s>ānulomikī kṣānti</s>) of such

body.text: atha khalu bhagavaṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: asaṃyatā uddhata unnatāśca agauravā mānina lābhautsadā /
children.translated_text: Unrestrained, excited, haughty, disrespectful, proud, obsessed with gain—

children.text: kleśābhibhūtāḥ sakhilāḥ sakiṃcanāḥ sudūra te tādṛśa agrabodhaye // 217 //
children.translated_text: overcome by the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), with impediments, with possessions—such ones are far from the supreme <s>bodhi</s>. // 217 //

children.text: lābhābhibhūtasya kusīda vardhate kusīdabhūtasya pranaṣṭa śraddhā /
children.translated_text: For one overcome by gain, laziness increases; for the lazy one, faith is destroyed;

children.text: śraddhāvipannasya pranaṣṭa śīla duḥśīlabhūtasya pranaṣṭa saṃgatiḥ // 218 //
children.translated_text: for one whose faith has failed, morality is destroyed; for the immoral one, good association is destroyed. // 218 //

body.text:
daridrabhūtāśca hi pravrajitvā dāridyramuktāṃ samavāpya pūjām /
taiḥ kāñcano bhāramivāpaviddhaḥ sa sasyabhāraḥ punarudgṛhītaḥ // 219 // lābhārthikoaraṇyamupaiti vastuṃ gaveṣate tatra gataśca jñātīn /

children.text: abhijñavidyāpratibhānasaṃpado vihāya gṛhṇāti sa cāpi jñātīn // 220 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned the wealth of <s>abhijñā</s> (higher knowledge), <s>vidyā</s> (science), and eloquence, he grasps after relatives. // 220 //

body.translated_text: Having become poor and then gone forth, having obtained worship free from poverty, they cast away as if a golden burden, and take up again the burden of worldly life. // 219 // One seeking gain goes to the forest to dwell, and having gone there, seeks out relatives;

children.text: apāyabhūmiṃ gatimakṣaṇeṣu daridratāṃ nīcakulopapattim /
children.translated_text: The lower realms, birth in inopportune [conditions], poverty, rebirth in a low family,

children.text: jātyandhadaurbalyamathālpasthāmatāṃ gṛhṇanti te mānavaśena mūḍhāḥ // 221 //
children.translated_text: congenital blindness, weakness, and lack of endurance—the deluded grasp these through the power of pride. // 221 //

children.text: te vṛtticaryāparihīnabhāvāḥ pramādalābhena smṛtipranaṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: They, having fallen away from proper conduct and livelihood, with mindfulness destroyed through negligent gain,

children.text: ghoraṃ prayāsyanti mahāprapātaṃ yato na mokṣo 'styapi kalpakoṭibhiḥ // 222 //
children.translated_text: will go to the terrible great abyss from which there is no liberation even in koṭis of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages). // 222 //

children.text: yadīha lābhina bhaveta bodhistaddevadatto 'pi labheta bodhim /
children.translated_text: If those who [merely] gain were to attain <s>bodhi</s>, then <s>Devadatta</s> too would have attained <s>bodhi</s>;

children.text: vairambhavātena yathaiva pakṣī kṣipyanti lābhena tathā ayuktāḥ // 223 //
children.translated_text: just as a bird [is tossed] by a whirlwind, so the undisciplined are cast about by gain. // 223 //

children.text: puṇyairvihīnāḥ paradāragṛddhā aśuddhaśīlāḥ kuśaleṣu boddaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Devoid of merit, lustful after others' wives, of impure morality, dull regarding what is wholesome—

children.text: te śāsane 'narthaśmaśānadāruvat ye bodhicittena alabdhajñānāḥ // 224 //
children.translated_text: they are like funeral-pyre wood in the teaching, those who, having [aroused] the mind of <s>bodhi</s>, have not attained knowledge. // 224 //

children.text: bodhyarthiko 'nveṣati buddhadharmān na tiṣṭhate cāpi yathā samokṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: One seeking <s>bodhi</s> searches for the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> and does not remain as though [already] liberated;

children.text: dṛḍhāḥ sa lepena kṛtaḥ kapirvā mānābhibhūtasya tathaiva bodhiḥ // 225 //
children.translated_text: firmly [trapped] like a monkey caught with glue—so is <s>bodhi</s> for one overcome by pride. // 225 //

children.text: Vaidya, RP 142
bodhyarthikenāpi mayā svajīvaṃ tyaktaḥ priyaḥ dharmapadasya hetoḥ /
children.translated_text: Even by me, the seeker of <s>bodhi</s>, my own dear life was given up for the sake of a word of <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: tyaktvā ca dharmāṃsta ayuktayogāḥ nirarthabhūtā nipatanti śāsanam // 226 //
children.translated_text: but having abandoned those <s>dharmas</s>, those engaged in wrong practice, having become purposeless, fall away from the teaching. // 226 //

children.text: mahāprapātaṃ jvalitaṃ hutāśanaṃ subhāṣitārthe patito 'smi pūrve /
children.translated_text: Into a great abyss, blazing with fire, I fell in former [lives] for the sake of well-spoken [<s>Dharma</s>];

children.text: śrutvā ca tasmin pratipattiye sthito vihāya sarvāṇi priyāpriyāṇi // 227 //
children.translated_text: and having heard [it], I stood firm in that practice, having abandoned all that is dear and not dear. // 227 //

children.text: śrutvā guṇāḍhyaṃ ca vicitraśāsanaṃ teṣāṃ spṛhā naikapade 'pi jāyate /
children.translated_text: Having heard the teaching, rich in qualities and of manifold [aspects], not even a desire for a single word arises in them;

children.text: adharmakāmasya kuto 'sti bodhiḥ yathaiva cāndhasya pathi prakāśanam // 228 //
children.translated_text: how can there be <s>bodhi</s> for one who loves <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness)? It is like illumination of the path for the blind. // 228 //

body.text: iti //
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ rāṣṭrapāla atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyaeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairacintyairatulyairapramāṇairvipulairaprameyairyadāsīt / tena kālena tena samayena siddhārthabuddhirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān / tena ca samayena arciṣmānnāma rājābhūt / arciṣmataḥ punā rāṣṭrapāla rājño jambūdvīpe rājyamabhūtṣoḍaśayojanasahasrāṇi / tena ca rāṣṭrapāla kālena tasmin jambūdvīpe viṃśatinagarasahasrāṇyabhūvan sarvāṇi kulakoṭisahasrikāṇi / tasya khalu punā rāṣṭrapāla rājño 'rciṣmato ratnaprabhāsaṃ nāma nagaramabhūdrājadhānī yatra sa rājā arciṣmān prativasati dvādaśayojanānyāyāmena pūrveṇa paścimena ca, sapta yojanāni vistareṇa dakṣiṇenottareṇa ca, saptānāṃ ratnānāṃ ca saptaprākāramaṣṭāpadasukṛtam / tena ca samayena daśavarṣakoṭiniyutāni sattvānāmāyuḥpramāṇamabhūt / rājñaḥ punā rāṣṭrapāla arciṣmataḥ puṇyaraśmirnāma putro 'bhūdabhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgataḥ / tasya jātamātrasyaiva nidhānasahasraṃ prādurbhūtam / saptānāṃ ratnānāmekaṃ cātra nidhānaṃ rājñaḥ prāsāde prādurbhūtaṃ daśapauruṣapramāṇaṃ saptānāṃ ratnānām / tasya khalu punā rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśme rājakumārasya jātāmātrasyaiva sarve jāmbūdvīpakāḥ sattvā āttamanaso 'bhūvan / ye ca sattvā bandhanagatāsteṣāṃ bandhanamokṣo 'bhūt / tena khalu punā rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśminā rājakumāreṇa saptabhirdivasaiḥ sarvaśilpānyadhigatāni yāvanti laukikāni //
body.translated_text: In the past, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, in a former time, [going back] incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, more than incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, immeasurable, vast, and immense ago, there appeared in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (Perfectly Awakened One) named <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, unsurpassed, Charioteer of persons to be tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. At that time there was a king named <s>Arciṣmat</s>. And, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, King <s>Arciṣmat</s>'s kingdom in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> extended sixteen thousand <s>yojanas</s>. At that time, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, there were twenty thousand cities in that <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, all having a thousand <s>koṭis</s> of families. And, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, King <s>Arciṣmat</s> had a capital city named <s>Ratnaprabhāsa</s>, where King <s>Arciṣmat</s> resided—twelve <s>yojanas</s> in length from east to west, and seven <s>yojanas</s> in breadth from south to north, with seven ramparts of the seven [kinds of] jewels, well-constructed like a chessboard. At that time, the lifespan of beings was ten <s>koṭi-niyutas</s> (billions) of years. And, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, King <s>Arciṣmat</s> had a son named <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, handsome, pleasing, beautiful to behold, endowed with a complexion of supreme auspicious radiance. At his very birth, a thousand treasuries appeared; and one treasure-trove of the seven jewels appeared in the king's palace, ten men's heights [high], made of the seven [kinds of] jewels. And, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, at the very birth of Prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, all beings in <s>Jambudvīpa</s> became joyful; and those beings who were imprisoned—their bonds were released. And, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, within seven days, Prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> mastered all the worldly arts and crafts.

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśme rājakumārasya śuddhāvāsakāyikā devatā ardharātrakālasamaye saṃcodayanti sma - apramattena te kumāra sadā bhavitavyam / anityatāpratyavekṣaṇakuśalena bhavitavyam / alpaṃ hi kumāra jīvitaṃ manuṣyāṇām / gamanīyaḥ saṃparāyaḥ / paralokabhayadarśinā ca te bhavitavyaṃ na sarmakriyoddhureṇa / tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, deities of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) realm used to urge Prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> at midnight—'You must always be heedful, O Prince! You must be skilled in contemplating impermanence! For the life of humans is short, O Prince! The next world must be journeyed to. And you must be one who sees the danger of the other world, not one who is indifferent to making [spiritual] effort.' At that time, [a deity] spoke these verses:

children.text: mā kumāra bhava supramattako mā pramādavaśamabhyupeṣyase /
children.translated_text: Do not be heedless, O Prince! Do not fall under the power of negligence!

children.text: apramāda sugatena varṇito ninditā hi sugataiḥ pramattakāḥ // 229 //
children.translated_text: Heedfulness (<s>apramāda</s>) has been praised by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One); the heedless are condemned by the <s>Sugatas</s>.

children.text: apramatta iha ye ca sūratā dānasaṃyamaratā amatsarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are heedful here, gentle, delighting in generosity and self-control, free from envy,

children.text: sarvasattvakṛpamaitramānasā te bhavanti nacirānnarottamāḥ // 230 //
children.translated_text: with minds of compassion and friendliness toward all beings — they will soon become the best of men.

children.text: ye 'prameya sugatā atītāḥ sāṃprataṃ ca hi ye 'pyanāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: The immeasurable <s>Sugatas</s> who have passed, those of the present, and those yet to come —

children.text: sarvaeva kuśalaista udgatā apramādapatha eva susthitāḥ // 231 //
children.translated_text: all of them arose through wholesome deeds, well-established on the very path of heedfulness.

children.text: annapānamatha vastrabhojanaṃ hemarūpyamaṇibhūṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Food, drink, clothing, meals, gold, silver, gems, and ornaments —

children.text: dattaṃ tairapi ca kalpakoṭiyaḥ prārthayadbhiriha bodhimuttamām // 232 //
children.translated_text: these were given by them for hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), seeking the supreme awakening here.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 143
hastapādamatha karṇanāsikā yācitā dadati saṃpraharṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hands, feet, ears, and noses — when asked, they give them with great delight,

children.text: sarvabodhiguṇapūritāśayāḥ te bhavanti nacirānnarottamāḥ // 233 //
children.translated_text: their intentions filled with all the qualities of awakening — they will soon become the best of men.

children.text: rajyasaukhyavibhavāṃśca sarvaśo viprahāya dayitāḥ sriyo 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Having completely abandoned the pleasures, happiness, and splendors of kingship, and beloved fortunes too —

children.text: raṅgamāyasadṛśaṃ hi saṃskṛtaṃ saṃśrayasva vanameva niḥspṛhaḥ // 234 //
children.translated_text: for the conditioned is like a show or an illusion — resort to the forest alone, free from craving.

children.text: jīvitaṃ capalamadhruvaṃ sadā mṛttikāghaṭaka eva bhedi ca /
children.translated_text: Life is ever fickle and impermanent, breaking like a clay pot,

children.text: yācitopamamaśāśvataṃ sadā nātra nityamaśubhaṃ kumāraka // 235 //
children.translated_text: always like something borrowed, impermanent — there is nothing permanent or beautiful here, O youth.

children.text: neha mātra na pitā na bāndhavā dhārayanti yatamāna durgatim /
children.translated_text: Neither mother, nor father, nor kinsmen here can hold back one heading for a bad destiny;

children.text: yatkṛtaṃ hi śubhāśubhaṃ tatprāyantamanuyāti pṛṣṭhataḥ // 236 //
children.translated_text: whatever good or evil one has done, that follows one from behind.

children.text: kāmahetu bahukalpasāgarā anyamanyavadhitā nirarthakāḥ /
children.translated_text: For the sake of desires, through many oceans of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), killing one another, to no purpose —

children.text: kasyacinna ca kṛtaṃ tvayā hitaṃ vyartha eva ca niveśitaḥ śramaḥ // 237 //
children.translated_text: you have not done anything beneficial for anyone, and effort has been invested in vain.

children.text: adya te jagata eṣato hitaṃ bodhiśāntamatulaṃ padottamam /
children.translated_text: Today, seeking what is beneficial for the world — awakening, peace, the incomparable, supreme state —

children.text: majjamāṃsamapi carma śuṣyate yadyapi tvamapi mā kṛthā śramam // 238 //
children.translated_text: even if flesh, blood, and skin dry up, do not give up your effort.

children.text: durlabho hi sugatasya saṃbhavaḥ śāntadharmaśravaṇaṃ sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: For rare is the arising of a <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), and hearing the peaceful <s>Dharma</s> is exceedingly rare;

children.text: mārapakṣamavadhūya yatnato buddhajñāna nacireṇa lapsyase // 239 //
children.translated_text: having cast off the forces of <s>Māra</s> with effort, you will obtain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge before long.

children.text: bhadramitraparisevakaḥ sadā pāpamitraparivarjako bhava /
children.translated_text: Always be one who attends upon good friends and avoids evil friends;

children.text: satpathe upanayanti te sadā duṣpathā ca satataṃ nivārakāḥ // 240 //
children.translated_text: they always lead one to the good path, while [evil friends] are constant obstacles.

children.text: sādhu vīryamapi kṛtva susthiraṃ kāyajīvitaspṛhāṃ vihāya ca /
children.translated_text: Having made effort that is firm and good, and having abandoned longing for body and life,

children.text: vajrakalpahṛdayā dṛḍhāśrayā buddhamārgamimameva suśrutam // 241 //
children.translated_text: with hearts firm as a diamond, with steadfast resolve — [follow] this very path of the <s>Buddha</s>, well-heard.

children.text: durlabhaṃ padavaraṃ hyanuttaraṃ sarva eva purimā narottamā /
children.translated_text: Rare is this supreme, unsurpassed state; all the previous best of men

children.text: araṇyagocararatāḥ prabhaṃkarāḥ teṣa tvaṃ cara pathe 'nuvartakaḥ // 242 //
children.translated_text: delighted in forest-wandering and were illuminators — you should follow in their path.

children.text: araṇyavāsanirataḥ sadā bhava mātṛputrapitṛbāndhavān priyān /
children.translated_text: Always be devoted to forest-dwelling; dear mother, son, father, and kinsmen,

children.text: viprahāya sakalaṃ suhṛjjanaṃ kāyajīvitakṛtāmapi tṛṣṇām /
children.translated_text: having abandoned all beloved people, and even the craving for body and life —

children.text: eṣatādya vipulaṃ sugatajñānasaṃcayam eṣatā padavaraṃ hyanuttaram // 243 //
children.translated_text: seek today the vast accumulation of the <s>Sugata's</s> knowledge; seek the supreme, unsurpassed state.

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumārastata upādāya daśabhirvarṣairna jātu styānamiddhamavakrāmitavān, na jātu hasitavān, na krīḍito na ramitaḥ, na paricārito na jātūdyānabhūmiṃ gato na jātu sakhāyān dṛṣṭvā vismitaḥ / na jātu gītābhilāṣyabhūt / na rājyadhanagṛhanagareṣu spṛhāmutpāditavān / evaṃ sarvavastuṣu anapekṣo 'bhūt / ekaḥ pradhyāyamānaḥ sthito 'bhūt pratisaṃlīnaḥ paramadaurbalyabhāvaṃ vicintayan / asāramitvaraṃ ca lokamanāśvasan / apriyasamavadhānaṃ priyavinābhāvaṃ bālollāpanaṃ saṃsāraratinirāsvādaṃ rājyasukhaṃ vimoghadharmaṃ (

children.text: Vaidya, RP 144
children.translated_text: (Vaidya, RP 144)

children.text: ) bhavābhīṣṭaṃ śamatṛptaṃ pṛthagjanatvaṃ sadā viruddham / bālāyuktajanamadhyagato 'smi yannvahaṃ tūṣṇībhāvenātināmadhyeyam / sa ekānte tūṣṇībhūtaḥ apramādaṃ vicintayan priyavinābhāvamekākī viharati sma //
children.translated_text: the craving for existence, and the nature of ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) as always sated with tranquility yet always opposed [to it]. "I am situated in the midst of a company of fools and enemies; let me pass this time in silence." Thus, secluded, in silence, contemplating heedfulness, [contemplating] separation from the beloved, he dwelt alone.

body.translated_text: Now, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, from that time onward, for ten years, the prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> never once fell into sloth and torpor, never laughed, never played or enjoyed himself, never indulged, never went to a pleasure garden, never marveled at seeing companions, never had a desire for songs, never generated longing for kingdom, wealth, home, or cities. Thus he was indifferent to all things. He stood alone, meditating, withdrawn, contemplating the state of extreme weakness, not taking comfort in [this] world devoid of essence and [full of] haste, [contemplating] the association with the unpleasant and separation from the pleasant, the prattle of fools, the tastelessness of delight in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the illusory nature of royal happiness,

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla rājñārciṣmatā anyatarasmin pṛthivīpradeśe ratipradhānaṃ nāma nagaraṃ māpitamabhūt kumārasya paribhogārtham / dakṣiṇenottareṇa ca sapta vīthīśatāni, saptabhiḥ prākāraiḥ samantato 'nuparikṣiptamabhūtsaptaratnamayaiḥ kiṅkiṇījālasamucchritairmuktājālaratnayaṣṭivitānaiḥ / sarveṣu ca vīthīmukheṣu aśītiratnayaṣṭisahasrāṇi sthāpitānyabhūvan / sarvasyā ca ratnayaṣṭayāṃ yaṣṭiratnasūtrasahasrāṇi nibaddhānyabhūvan / sarvatra ca ratnasūtre caturdaśa tālapaṅktikoṭyo nibaddhānyabhūvan, yāsāṃ vāteneritānāṃ vātasaṃghaṭṭitānāṃ tadyathāpi nāma tūryaśatasahasrasya ghoṣaśabdaḥ syāt / sarveṣu ca vīthīmukheṣu pañca pañca kanyāśatāni sthāpitānyabhūvan gītakuśalāni nṛttakuśalāni prathamayauvanaprāptāni sarvajagatparibhogyāni / tāsāṃ ca rājñārciṣmatā ājñā dattābhūt - rātridivaṃ bhavantībhirnānyā kthā kāryāṃ anyatra nṛttagītavāditena / sarve rañjayitavyā ye keciccaturṣu dikṣvāgacchanti / apyevaṃ nāma kumārasya raticittamutpadyeta / na ca kasyacit sattvasyāpanāyaṃ vaktavyam / teṣu ca punaḥ sarvavīthīmukheṣu annamannārthikebhyo dīyate, pānaṃ pānārthikebhyaḥ, yānaṃ yānārthikebhyo yāvadvadvastragandhamālyavilepanaśayyopāśrayajīvitapariṣkāraṃ suvarṇarūpyamaṇimuktāvaiḍūrya śaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajata hastyaśvaśodhanaṃ sarvābharaṇaṃ ratnarāśayaśca sthāpitā abhūvan sarvajanaparibhogārtham / tena ca samayena madhye nagarasya samantato yojanaṃ gṛhaṃ kumārasya māpitamabhūtparibhogāya saptānāṃ ratnānāmaṣṭāpadanibaddhaṃ toraṇasaptapratimaṇḍitam / tatra caikaḥ prāsādaḥ kārito 'bhūt, yatra catasraḥ śayanakoṭyaḥ prajñaptamabhūtkumārasya paribhogārtham / tatra ca madhye udyānaṃ māpitamabhūtsarvapuṣpavṛkṣasarvaphalavṛkṣasarvaratnavṛkṣapratisphuṭaṃ saṃchāditamabhūta / tasya khalu punā rāṣṭrapāla udyānasya madhye puṣkariṇi kāritābhūt saptaratnamayī catūratnasopānī, tadyathā suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya / aṣṭottaraṃ ca siṃhamukhaśataṃ yena gandhodakaṃ praviśati tasyāḥ khalu punaḥ puṣkariṇyāḥ / aṣṭaśatameva siṃhamukhānāṃ yena punareva tadvāri nirvahati / utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkaiḥ satatasamitaṃ saṃpuṣpitā samantataśca ratnavṛkṣaparivāritā sarvakālikaiśca puṣpaphalavṛkṣaiḥ parisphuṭā / tasyāḥ puṣkariṇyāḥ tīre aṣṭaśataṃ ratnavṛkṣāṇāṃ māpitamabhūt / sarvasmin ratnavṛkṣe ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭi ratnasūtrāṇi nibaddhāni / sarvatra ca tālapaṅktikoṭyo nibaddhāḥ / tāsāṃ ca vāteneritānāṃ vātasaṃghaṭṭitānāṃ śabdo niścarati tadyathāpi nāma tūryaśatasahasrasya saṃpravāditasya / sā ca puṣkariṇi upariratnajālasaṃchāditābhūt, mā kumārasya rajo pāṃśurvā śarīre nipatiṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, King <s>Arciṣmat</s> had caused to be built in a certain region of the earth a city called <s>Ratipradhāna</s> (Preeminence of Pleasure) for the prince's enjoyment. On the south and north there were seven hundred streets, and it was surrounded on all sides by seven ramparts made of the seven precious substances, adorned with nets of bells, pearl-net canopies on jeweled poles. At the entrance of every street, eighty thousand jeweled pillars had been erected. On every jeweled pillar, a thousand jeweled thread-strings had been fastened. On every jeweled string, fourteen hundred thousand rows of palm-trees had been attached, and when stirred and struck by the wind, a sound arose as if from a hundred thousand musical instruments being played. At the entrance of every street, five hundred maidens each had been stationed — skilled in song, skilled in dance, having attained the prime of youth, fit to be enjoyed by all the world. And King <s>Arciṣmat</s> had given them this command: "Day and night you shall engage in nothing other than dance, song, and music. All who come from the four directions are to be delighted. Perhaps thereby a desire for pleasure will arise in the prince. And no one shall be turned away." And at the entrance of every street, food was given to those who sought food, drink to those who sought drink, vehicles to those who sought vehicles, and likewise clothing, perfume, garlands, ointments, beds, shelters, necessities of life, gold, silver, gems, pearls, beryl, conch, crystal, coral, wrought gold, refined silver, elephants, horses, and provisions — and heaps of jewels had been placed for the enjoyment of all people. And at that time, in the middle of the city, a palace for the prince's enjoyment had been built, extending one <s>yojana</s> (league) on all sides, constructed of the seven precious substances in a checkered pattern, adorned with seven gateways. And in it a single mansion had been built, where four hundred million seats had been prepared for the prince's enjoyment. And in the middle, a garden had been established, thickly covered with every kind of flower-tree, fruit-tree, and jewel-tree. And in the middle of that garden, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, a lotus pond had been made of the seven precious substances with four jeweled stairways — of gold, silver, beryl, and crystal. And one hundred and eight lion-faced fountains through which scented water entered that lotus pond. And one hundred and eight lion-faced fountains through which the water flowed out again. It was constantly blooming with blue lotuses, red lotuses, white water-lilies, and white lotuses, surrounded on all sides by jewel-trees, and thickly covered with flower and fruit trees of all seasons. On the bank of that lotus pond, eight hundred jewel-trees had been planted. On every jewel-tree, sixty jeweled thread-strings had been fastened. On all of them, rows of hundreds of thousands of palm-trees had been attached. When stirred and struck by the wind, a sound issued forth as if from a hundred thousand musical instruments being played. And that lotus pond was covered above with a jeweled net, lest dust or sand should fall on the prince's body.

children.text: ) niṣetsyata iti / sarvatra cāsanamūle agarugandhaghaṭikā dhūpyate / triṣkṛtvo divasasya triṣkṛtvo rātreḥ puṣpasaṃstaraḥ kriyate / suvarṇachadanācchāditaṃ suvarṇapadmapralambitaṃ muktājālavitataṃ maṇiratnaprabhāvabhāsitamaśītisahasrapralambitam / sarvatra ca ratnavṛkṣe patākāśatāni pralambitānyabhūvan / sarvatra codyāne navatirmaṇiratnaśatasahasrāṇi yojanaprabhāṇi sthāpitānyabhūvan, teṣāṃ ca prabhayā sarvaloko 'vabhāsito 'bhūt / tasmin punā rāṣṭrapāla udyāne śukasārikakroñcakokilamayūrahaṃsacakravākakunālakalaviṅkajīvaṃjīvakā manuṣyapralāpinaḥ pakṣiṇo 'bhūvan / yeṣāṃ nikūjitāni nadatāṃ nandane devānāmiva madanīyaḥ śabdo niścarati / kumārasya ca paribhogārthaṃ pañcarasaśataprakārāṇi bhojanāni satatasamitamabhisaṃskṛtānyabhūvan sarvākārasaṃpannāni //
children.translated_text: was to sit. And at the base of every seat, incense of <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood) was burned. Three times during the day and three times during the night, a carpet of flowers was laid. It was canopied with a golden covering, hung with golden lotuses, spread with pearl-nets, illuminated by the splendor of jewels and gems, with eighty thousand [ornaments] hanging down. On every jewel-tree, hundreds of banners hung. And in every part of the garden, ninety hundred thousand jewels of a <s>yojana's</s> radiance had been placed, and by their light the entire world was illuminated. And in that garden, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, there were parrots, mynahs, herons, cuckoos, peacocks, swans, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, <s>kunāla</s> birds, <s>kalaviṅka</s> birds, and <s>jīvaṃjīvaka</s> birds — birds that spoke like humans — whose warbling sounds issued forth as intoxicating as those in the <s>Nandana</s> garden of the gods. And for the prince's enjoyment, five hundred varieties of food of five flavors had been constantly prepared, perfect in every respect.

body.translated_text: And at that time, in that mansion, four hundred million seats had been prepared, made of the seven precious substances. On every seat, five hundred silk cloths had been spread. And in the middle, a seat of the seven precious substances had been prepared, seven man-heights in elevation, spread with eighty hundred million silk cloths, where the prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>

body.text: tena ca punaḥ samayena viṃśavarṣāḥ samānāḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣātikrāntāḥ kumārakāḥ sarvanagarebhyaḥ samudānīya tatra ca nagare praveśitā abhūvan sarvaśilpasthānakarmasthānavidhijñāḥ / sarvaloikikaratyupakaraṇavidhijñānāmaśītikoṭyaḥ tasminnagare praveśitā abhūvan / tasya mātāpitṛbhyāṃ koṭiḥ kanyānāṃ dattā, jñātisaṃghena koṭiḥ, naigamajñānapadaiḥ koṭiḥ, sarvarājena koṭiḥ kanyānāṃ dattā abhūvan / tāśca sarvā abhurūpāḥ prāsādikā darśanīyāḥ sarvāḥ ṣoḍaśavarṣapramāṇā jātyā gītakuśalā vādyakuśalā nṛttakuśalā hasitakuśalāḥ puruṣopasaṃkramaṇakuśalā ārjavāḥ śiśavā madhurā vṛddhayaḥ pūrvābhilāpinyaḥ smitamukhāśopacārakuśalāḥ sarvakalāsu vidhijñā nātidīrghā nātihrasvā nātisthūlā nātigauryo nātiśyāmāḥ / yāsāmutpalagandho mudhāt pravāti, candanagandho gātrebhyaḥ pravāti / vyaktāṃ iva devakanyakāḥ, ekāntamanāmayacāroṇyaḥ / tāsāṃ madhyagataḥ puṇyaraśmī rājakumāraḥ saṃgītisaṃprabhāṇitena tatra ca saṃgītiśabde caivaṃ cittamutpādayati - mahānamitrasaṃgho batāyaṃ mama prādurbhutaḥ kuśaladharmaparimoṣakaḥ / hanta anapekṣo bhaviṣyāmi / sa tasmin samaye syādyathāpi nāma vadhyaḥ puruṣo dṛṣṭvā na vismayacitta mutpādayati, evameva puṇyaraśmī rājakumāraḥ tāṃ pramadāṃ dṛṣṭvā na viṣmayati, nāpi tatra nagare, na ca sakhībhiṃrvismayati sma / taiśca daśabhirvarṣairna jātu rūpanimittamudgṛhītavān / na śabdanimittaṃ na gandha nimittaṃ na rasanimittaṃ na sparśanimittamudgṛhītavān / anyatraivaṃrūpaṃ cittaṃ pravartayate sma - kadā tāvadevaṃrūpādamitrasaṃghamadhyānmama mokṣo bhaviṣyati ? kadāhamapramādacaryāṃ cariṣyāmi yena me mokṣo bhaviṣyati ? atha khalu tāḥ kanyakāḥ rājño 'rciṣmata ārocayanti sma - na deva kumāraḥ krīḍati, na ramate, na paricārayati ? atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla rājā arciṣmānaśītibhī rājasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ yena puṇyaraśmī rājakumārastenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramyāśrumukhaḥ pravepamānena kāyena śocamāno dharaṇitale prapatitaḥ / sa utthāya dharaṇitalātpuṇyaraśmiṃ rājakumāraṃ gāthābhidhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: And at that time, youths of twenty years of age, having passed sixteen, had been gathered from all the cities and brought into that city — skilled in all arts, crafts, and trades. Eighty hundred million [persons] skilled in the arts of all worldly pleasures had been brought into that city. His parents had given [him] ten million maidens, the kinsmen's assembly [gave] ten million, the citizens and elders [gave] ten million, and all the kings [gave] ten million maidens. And all of them were beautiful, graceful, lovely to behold, all of sixteen years of age, naturally skilled in song, skilled in playing instruments, skilled in dance, skilled in laughter, skilled in approaching men, sincere, youthful, sweet, mature, the first to speak, with smiling faces, skilled in courteous conduct, knowledgeable in all arts, neither too tall nor too short, neither too stout, neither too fair nor too dark. From their mouths wafted the fragrance of the blue lotus, and from their limbs the fragrance of sandalwood. They were manifestly like celestial maidens, with flawless and charming complexions. The prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, situated among them, when [there was] the sound of concerts and entertainment, generated this thought: "Alas, this great company of enemies has appeared before me, robbers of wholesome qualities. Truly, I shall remain indifferent." At that time, just as a man condemned to death, seeing [the pleasures], does not generate a mind of wonder, even so the prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, seeing those women, did not marvel, nor did he marvel at that city, nor at his companions. And during those ten years, he never grasped at the sign of form, nor at the sign of sound, nor of smell, nor of taste, nor of touch. Rather, he set his mind in this way: "When indeed shall I be freed from the midst of such a company of enemies? When shall I practice the conduct of heedfulness, by which I shall be liberated?" Then those maidens reported to King <s>Arciṣmat</s>: "O Lord, the prince does not play, nor enjoy himself, nor take pleasure." Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, King <s>Arciṣmat</s>, together with eighty thousand kings, approached the prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>. Having approached, with tear-stained face, with trembling body, grieving, he fell upon the ground. Having risen from the ground, he addressed the prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> with verses:

children.text: prakṣasva putravararatna mama pralāpaṃ śokārdito nipatito 'smi bhuvi kṣapānte /
children.translated_text: "Hear my lament, O son, most excellent jewel! Struck by grief, I have fallen to the ground at the end of night.

children.text: kenāpriyaṃ tava kṛtaṃ mam tadbravīhi jyeṣṭhaṃ dadāmi yadihāsya kṣaṇena daṇḍam // 244 //
children.translated_text: Who has done something displeasing to you? Tell me that, and I shall instantly give the harshest punishment to that person.

children.text: Vaidya, RP 146
prekṣasva me 'dya nagaraṃ surasaṃgharamyaṃ manasā mayābhiracittaṃ yadidaṃ tvadarthe /
children.translated_text: Behold today my city, delightful as a gathering of gods, which I had built with my mind set upon your sake.

children.text: kimihāṅgamadya vikalaṃ mama tadvadāśu śakrasya vādya vibhavaṃ tava darśayāmi // 245 //
children.translated_text: Is some limb impaired today? Tell me quickly — I shall show you the splendor of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) himself today.

children.text: śokārditaṃ kamalalocanacārunetraṃ strīsaṃghamapsarasamaṃ vilapantamīkṣa /
children.translated_text: Behold this group of women, lotus-eyed, with beautiful eyes, equal to <s>Apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), lamenting with grief —

children.text: etābhiranyaiśca ramasva vinīya śokaṃ kiṃ śalyaviddha iva dhyāyasi dīnavakraḥ // 246 //
children.translated_text: enjoy yourself with these and others, dispelling your sorrow! Why do you brood, dejected and downcast, as if pierced by a thorn?

body.text:
etāḥ svaraṅgarucirāḥ suratervidhijñāḥ saṃgītitālasamaye ca viniścayajñāḥ /
kālastavādya suratasya na śocitasya mlānaṃ saroruhamivāsi kimadya dīnaḥ // 247 // udyānapuṣpaphalapatravikīrṇaśākhā udviddhacitramiva citrarathaṃ surāṇām /

children.text: saṃcintayasva prathamaṃ hi vayastavedaṃ kālo rate rama ihādya suta prasīda // 248 //
children.translated_text: consider first that this is your youth; this is the time for pleasure — enjoy yourself here today, my son, be pleased!

body.translated_text: These women are beautiful in form and complexion, skilled in the arts of love, knowledgeable in the proper time for concert and rhythm. This is your time for pleasure, not for grieving — why are you wilted today like a faded lotus, so dejected? The garden with its flowers, fruits, and leaves scattered on the branches, raised up like the colorful chariot <s>Citraratha</s> of the gods —

children.text: tulyā taveyamapi puṣkariṇī surāṇāṃ snānārthamutpalasarojavanābhikīrṇā /
children.translated_text: This lotus pond of yours, equal to that of the gods, strewn with blue lotuses and red lotuses, for the purpose of bathing —

children.text: padmāni mattavaraṣaṭpadabhūṣitāni saṃcintya tāṃ ka iha nābhirameta putra // 249 //
children.translated_text: lotuses adorned with intoxicated bees of the finest kind — having considered these, what son here would not delight? [249]

children.text: haṃsā mayūraśukasārikakokilāśca koṇālajīvakalaviṅka manojñaghoṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Swans, peacocks, parrots, <s>sārikā</s> birds, cuckoos, <s>koṇāla</s> birds, <s>jīvaka</s> birds, and <s>kalaviṅka</s> birds with enchanting songs —

children.text: gandharvamādana ivā himavatsamīpe śrutvā naraḥ ka iha nātra ratiṃ labheta // 250 //
children.translated_text: hearing [them], as if near the <s>Himavat</s> like on <s>Gandharva-mādana</s>, what person here would not find delight? [250]

body.text:
etā vimānamaṇicūḍasamuktajālā vaiḍūryakāñcanacitā iva vaijayante /
ratnāsanāni ca varāṇi varāstṛtāni cārusvarā kanakakaṅkaṇatālapaṅktyaḥ // 251 // gambhīradhīravaratūryaninādaghuṣṭā vīthīṣu dānavisarāstava cāpi hetoḥ /
