kasmān triviṣṭapasame bhavane manojñe vikṣiptacitta iha kiṃ na ratiṃ karoṣi //
children.translated_text: why in this delightful palace equal to heaven, with a distracted mind, do you not take pleasure here? [252]

body.translated_text: These palaces with jewel-crested canopies of nets, adorned with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> and gold, appear like banners; and excellent gem-thrones with fine coverings, and rows of lovely-sounding golden bangles keeping rhythm; [251] Resounding in the streets with deep, solemn, and excellent musical sounds, and gifts distributed on your behalf — maidens singing the songs of a thousand melodies are presented, just as <s>apsaras</s>es [sing] in the <s>Nandana</s> grove;

children.text: ete kumāra tava devasamānagarbhāḥ krīḍāsakhāya saha putra ramasva caibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: These, O prince, are your playmates, born of divine-like wombs; enjoy yourself with them, my son!

children.text: mātā pitā ca tava saṃsthita sāśrukaṇṭhāḥ kiṃ duḥkha nāsti karuṇā ca jane tavāsmin // 253 //
children.translated_text: Your mother and father stand here with tear-choked throats — is there no suffering? Have you no compassion for these people of yours? [253]

children.text: so 'thābravīdguṇacito bhavadoṣadarśī nirviṇṇa saṃskṛtamanarthika kāmabhogaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then he spoke — endowed with virtues, seeing the faults of existence, disgusted, regarding conditioned things as purposeless, [rejecting] sensual pleasures —

children.text: saṃsārapañcaragataṃ jagadīkṣyaṃ cedaṃ mokṣārthikaḥ pitaramāha śṛṇuṣva deva // 254 //
children.translated_text: seeing the world caught in the cage of <s>saṃsāra</s>, desiring liberation, he addressed his father: 'Listen, O king! [254]

children.text: devāpriyaṃ mam kṛtaṃ na hi kenacinme kiṃ tvasti me 'dya na hi kāmaguṇeṣu chandaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nothing displeasing to me has been done by anyone; but today I have no desire for the objects of sensual pleasure.

children.text: sarve priyāṃ ripusamā hi nirānuraktā ye kleśadurgatiprapāta prapātayanti //
children.translated_text: All dear ones are like enemies, devoid of affection, who hurl [beings] down the precipice of afflictions and bad destinies. [255]

children.text: etāḥ striyo hyabudhabālajanābhirāmā mārasya pāśaguṇabaddha mahāprapātāḥ /
children.translated_text: These women, delightful [only] to foolish, ignorant people, are great precipices bound by the snares and cords of <s>Māra</s>.

children.text: nityaṃ tathā vigarhita āryajanena caitāḥ sevāmi kiṃ narakadurgatiśokamūlāḥ //
children.translated_text: Always thus condemned by noble people — why should I serve those who are the root of hell, bad destinies, and grief? [256]

children.text: etāḥ striyo hi chavimātrakarūparabhyāḥ snāyvasthiyantramaśucībhi nirarthako 'ham /
children.translated_text: These women, whose beauty consists of mere skin — [composed of] sinews, bones, and machinery, impure — I would be purposeless [to desire them].

children.text: prasrāviṇī rudhiramūtraśakṛnmalānāṃ vyaktaṃ śmaśānasadṛśīṣu kathaṃ rameyam // 257 //
children.translated_text: Oozing with blood, urine, excrement, and filth — manifestly like charnel grounds, how could I take delight in them? [257]

children.text: gītaṃ na śroṣyamapi vādyarutaṃ na grāhyaṃ svapnāya mābhiratayo 'budhamohanāśca /
children.translated_text: I shall not listen to songs, nor accept the sound of instruments; away with sleep, pleasures, and the delusions of the foolish!

children.text: saṃkalpalālasa gatā abudhā tu nāśaṃ kiṃ kleśadāsa iva bālajano bhaviṣye // 258 //
children.translated_text: Those who are lazy in their imaginings, the foolish, have gone to destruction — shall I become like a slave to afflictions, as ignorant people do? [258]

children.text: sarve ime drumalatā śiśire pravṛtte kāntāravṛkṣasadṛśā hi bhavantyaramyāḥ /
children.translated_text: All these trees and vines, when winter comes, become unlovely like trees in a wilderness.

children.text: sarvaśriyo vidhamanī hi anityateyaṃ mohātpramādamupayāmi cale tu jīve // 259 //
children.translated_text: All splendors are destroyed by this impermanence — shall I, out of delusion, fall into heedlessness when life is fleeting? [259]

body.text: cittaṃ samudra iva tarpayituṃ na śakyaṃ tṛṣṇāpravṛttinirataḥ punareva kāṅkṣa /

children.text: Vaidya, RP 148
anyonyaghāti jagadīkṣya hi kāmahetoḥ meruryathaiva pavanairahamaprampyaḥ // 260 //
children.translated_text: Seeing the world mutually destroying itself for the sake of desires — like <s>Meru</s> by the winds, I am immovable. [260]

body.translated_text: The mind, like the ocean, cannot be satisfied; engaged in the course of craving, it desires again and again.

children.text: na tvaṃ pitā na sahajā mama nāpi bhāryāḥ trātā na bāndhavajanā nṛpate hmapāyāt /
children.translated_text: You are not [truly] my father, nor siblings, nor wives; neither kinsmen nor relatives are protectors from downfall, O king.

children.text: sarve vayaṃ tṛṇagatā iva bindulekhā mā tāta cittavaśagā bhavatāṃ pramattāḥ // 261 //
children.translated_text: We are all like dewdrops on blades of grass — do not, dear father, be heedless, [living] under the power of the mind! [261]

children.text: dhigyauvanena manujeśvara yanna nityaṃ dhigjīvitasya gamanaṃ giritoyaśīghram /
children.translated_text: Shame on youth, O lord of men, for it is not permanent! Shame on the passing of life, swift as a mountain torrent!

children.text: dhiksaṃskṛtaṃ kṣayamidaṃ taḍidabhralolaṃ dhikkaṇḍitasya tribhave nṛpa kāmarāgaḥ // 262 //
children.translated_text: Shame on conditioned existence, this perishing [thing], flickering like lightning in the clouds! Shame on attachment to sensual desire in the three realms of existence, O king! [262]

children.text: saṃcodito 'smi vibudhairbhava apramatto no bodhisattva bhavate viṣayābhilagnaḥ /
children.translated_text: I have been urged by the wise: 'Be heedful in existence! A <s>bodhisattva</s> does not become attached to sense objects.'

children.text: buddho bhaveyamiha lokahitānukampī nāsti pramādacaritasya narendra bodhiḥ // 263 //
children.translated_text: May I become a <s>Buddha</s> here, compassionate for the welfare of the world — there is no awakening for one who lives in heedlessness, O king! [263]

children.text: kāmāturo bhavati yo nṛpa cittadāsaḥ sa hi puṇyanāśanirato vinivṛttasvargaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is tormented by desires, O king, becomes a slave to the mind; he is devoted to the destruction of merit, turned away from heaven.

children.text: hiṃsāsamiddhamapi nābhicareta jātu pakṣīva pañjaragataḥ kathamāśvaseta // 264 //
children.translated_text: One should never engage in what is fueled by violence — like a bird trapped in a cage, how could one find relief? [264]

children.text: dhātūśca sarpasadṛśā vadhakāśca skandhāḥ cittaṃ ca sāsravamanarthaka śūnya grāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: The elements (<s>dhātu</s>s) are like serpents, the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>s) are murderers, the mind with its outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) is purposeless, an empty village.

children.text: viṣastambapuṣpita iveha narendra kāyaḥ oghe 'tiruhyati kathaṃ nu ratirmamātra // 265 //
children.translated_text: This body, O king, is like a poison-tree in bloom — how could I find delight here, carried along in the flood? [265]

children.text: saṃprekṣase jagadidaṃ kugatiprapannaṃ vyaktaṃ padaṃ gaganatulyamapi jvalantam /
children.translated_text: Look at this world fallen into bad destinies — clearly, even a station equal to the sky is ablaze.

children.text: teṣāṃ pramokṣaṇanimittamihādya rājan śivadharmanāva samudānayitāsmi śīghram // 266 //
children.translated_text: For the purpose of their liberation, O king, today I shall quickly prepare the ship of the auspicious <s>Dharma</s>! [266]

children.text: suptān vibodhayitumātura jīvitārthaṃ śalya nimūlayitumutpathagān vinetum /
children.translated_text: To awaken the sleeping, to heal the sick for the sake of life, to remove thorns, to guide those on wrong paths,

children.text: prod ghuṣya bandhanabimokṣa mahāsahasre saṃtarpayaṃściradaridra subhāṣitena // 267 //
children.translated_text: proclaiming liberation from bondage in the great thousandfold [world], satisfying the long-impoverished with well-spoken words, [267]

body.text: sīdanta durgatipathādapi coddhariṣye andhe cakṣurapi tṛṣṇalatāviśoṣī /

children.text: Vaidya, RP 149
prajñārciruttamavimuktikṛtapradīpo drakṣanti yena tribhavaṃ naṭaraṅgakalpam // 268 //
children.translated_text: making a lamp with the flame of wisdom and supreme liberation, by which they shall see the three realms of existence as like a dancer's performance. [268]

body.translated_text: I shall lift up even those sinking on the path of bad destinies — giving sight to the blind, drying up the vine of craving,

children.text: meghaṃ kṛpākaruṇapāramitābhrakūṭaṃ sattvārthagarjita vipaśyanavidyumālī /
children.translated_text: A cloud with the peak of compassion, kindness, and the perfection [of giving], thundering for the welfare of beings, with a garland of lightning that is <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) —

children.text: bodhyaṅgadhārasukhaśītalavṛṣṭijālaiḥ śītīkaromi ca jagaccirakālataptam // 269 //
children.translated_text: with the web of rain-showers, pleasant and cool, of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), I shall cool the world long scorched [by suffering]. [269]

children.text: etatsmarannahamiha kṣitiśopaviṣṭo nāstīha me praṇidhi saṃskṛtasarvakāmaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Remembering this, I sit here, O lord of the earth — my aspiration is not for all conditioned desires.

children.text: bodhyarthiko hi vicarāmiha sattvahetoḥ ekāṃśiko na hi bhavābhiratau mamecchā // 270 //
children.translated_text: Seeking awakening, I wander here for the sake of beings — I am single-minded; my wish is not for delight in existence. [270]

children.text: jānan vasetka iha pārthiva śatrumadhye ko buddhimān sabhayamārgapathaṃ vrajeta /
children.translated_text: Who, knowing, would dwell here amidst enemies, O king? Who, being wise, would travel a fearful road?

children.text: ko vā sacakṣuriha tāta patetprapāte ko bodhimārgamadhigamya bhavetpramattaḥ // 271 //
children.translated_text: Who, having eyes, would fall into an abyss, dear father? Who, having found the path to awakening, would become heedless? [271]

children.text: anusrota sarvajagatī pratisrotā so 'haṃ vācā na śakyamiha pārthiva bodhi prāptum /
children.translated_text: The whole world goes with the current; I go against it — awakening cannot be attained by mere words, O king.

children.text: meruprayātamapi sāgaramutsaheyaṃ na tveva me mana ihābhirameta kāmaiḥ // 272 //
children.translated_text: I would venture even to cross an ocean reaching to <s>Meru</s>, but my mind would never delight in sensual pleasures. [272]

children.text: gacchāśu pārthiva varasvajanena sārdhaṃ sarvāṃ hi rāṣṭraratimutsṛja sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: Go quickly, O king, together with your people; relinquish all delight in the kingdom before the whole world.

children.text: ādāya gacchatu yathābhimataṃ hi yasya gṛhyāpramāda mama tāta na rājyakoṭyā // 273 //
children.translated_text: Let each one take and go as he pleases — my heedfulness, dear father, is not [to be exchanged] for ten million kingdoms. [273]

children.text: śakyā na nārigaṇamadhyagatena bodhiḥ prāptuṃ śivaṃ padamanuttarayogakṣemam /
children.translated_text: Awakening cannot be attained while dwelling amidst a company of women — the auspicious, unsurpassed, secure state.

children.text: gacchāmyahaṃ girivanāntaramāśrayāmi prāptā hyaraṇyaniratena jinena bodhiḥ // 274 //
children.translated_text: I shall go and take refuge in the interior of mountain forests — for awakening was attained by the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) who delighted in the wilderness. [274]

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumāraḥ prāsādatalagata eva tābhiḥ pramadābhiḥ sārdhaṃ caṃkramannudvignamanāḥ saṃstribhirīryāpathairviharati / katamaistribhiḥ ? sthānena caṃkrameṇa niṣadyayā / styānamiddhaparivarjitaḥ upariprāsādatalagato 'ṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau sthitaḥ / so 'rdharātrakālasamaye aśroṣīt - antarīkṣācchuddhāvāsakāyikā devatā buddhasya varṇaṃ bhāṣamāṇā gacchanti, vistareṇa dharmasya saṃghasya varṇaṃ bhāṣamāṇā gacchanti / śrutvā ca rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumāraḥ saṃhṛṣṭaromakūpajātaḥ aśru nipātayati / sa saṃvegajāto 'ñjaliṃ kṛtvā tāṃ devatāṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, while on the upper terrace of the palace, walking back and forth among those women with an agitated mind, conducted himself in three of the four postures. Which three? Standing, walking, and sitting. Free from sloth and torpor, on the upper terrace of the palace, established on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage). At midnight, he heard deities of the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) class passing through the sky, proclaiming the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s>, and extensively proclaiming the virtues of the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>. Having heard this, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, with hair standing on end, shed tears. Filled with religious urgency, having made <s>añjali</s> (palms joined), he addressed those deities with verses:

children.text: Vaidya, RP 150

body.text:
mayi karuṇa janitvā devatā duḥkhite 'smin yadi na kuruta manyuṃ kiṃcidevābhipṛcche / kasya guṇa vadanto gacchetātrāntarīkṣe sukhitamiha mano me vākyametaṃ niśāmya // 275
 //
body.translated_text: Having compassion for me, a suffering one — O deities, if you are not angered, I would ask you something: whose virtues are you proclaiming as you pass through the sky? My mind is gladdened here upon hearing these words. [275]

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla tā devatāḥ puṇyaraśmirājakumāraṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, those deities addressed prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> with verses:

children.text: śravaṇamupagataste kiṃ na buddhaḥ kumāra śaraṇamaśaraṇānāṃ nāma siddhārthabuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Has the name of the <s>Buddha</s> not reached your ears, O prince? He is the refuge of the unprotected, <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> (Fulfilled-Wisdom) by name.

children.text: paracarikuśalo 'sau puṇyaprajñāguṇaḍhyo daśaniyutasahasrādhyāyināṃ tasya saṃghaḥ // 276 //
children.translated_text: Skilled in the welfare of others, rich in the qualities of merit and wisdom — his <s>Saṃgha</s> consists of ten million thousand disciples. [276]

body.text: puṇyarasmirāha -
body.translated_text: <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> said:

children.text: ahamapi jina dṛkṣye kīdṛśaṃ tasya rūpaṃ vadata api ca sarve kīdṛśo cāsya varṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: I too wish to see the <s>Jina</s> — what is his form like? Tell me, all of you, what is his appearance?

children.text: ahamapi paripṛcche kīdṛśī bodhicaryā bhavati yatha caran vai sarvasattvaikanāthaḥ // 277 //
children.translated_text: I also ask: what is the conduct of awakening, by practicing which one becomes the sole protector of all beings? [277]

body.text: atha khalu tā devatāḥ puṇyaraśmiṃ rājakumāraṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those deities addressed prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> with verses:

children.text: snugdharucikeśā dakṣiṇāvartajātā giritatamiva haima śobhate cāsya coṣṇi /
children.translated_text: His hair is smooth and lustrous, growing in clockwise curls; his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) shines like a golden mountain peak.

children.text: gagana iva ca śūnyo bhāsate cāsya ūrṇā sphaṭikamaṇiviśuddhā dakṣiṇā nābhi jātā // 278 //
children.translated_text: His <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the eyebrows) shines like the empty sky, pure as crystal, born curling to the right. [278]

children.text: bhramaragaṇaviśuddhā netra nīlotpalābhā siṃhahanu narendrao bimba oṣṭhaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ /
children.translated_text: His eyes, pure as a swarm of bees, are like blue lotuses; his jaw is like a lion's, the lord of men; his lips are like <s>bimba</s> fruit, the Self-Arisen One.

children.text: sṛjati ca sahasraṃ vai raśmikoṭīranantān sphurati ca trisahasrān durgatīḥ śoṣayaṃśca // 279 //
children.translated_text: He emits a thousand million infinite rays, illuminating the three-thousandfold [world system], drying up the bad destinies. [279]

children.text: samasahitasuvṛttā danta citra suśuklā himarajataviśuddhā viṃśati dveguṇāsya /
children.translated_text: His teeth are even, well-set, well-rounded, variegated, and very white, pure as snow and silver — twenty doubled [i.e., forty].

children.text: jinavarapravarasya tasya daṃṣṭrāścatasraḥ svakamukhapraticchādā tasya jihvā prabhūtā // 280 //
children.translated_text: The supreme among conquerors has four canine teeth; his tongue is extensive, covering his own face. [280]

children.text: giri varasahitārthā tasya pralhādanīyā sahita akuṭilā ca bramhaghoṣā suyuktā /
children.translated_text: His [voice] is delightful, like a great mountain, harmonious and straight, a <s>Brahma</s>-voice, well-composed.

children.text: tūryaśatasahasrairvāgjinasyārhatulyā vimatiśamakarī sā toṣaṇī arthikānām // 281 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Jina's</s> speech is equal to [the sound of] a hundred thousand instruments, allaying doubts, satisfying those who seek meaning. [281]

children.text: Vaidya, RP 151
avikalaguṇacitrā bodhi aṅgānukūlā hāraśatasahasrā gumphitā dharmamālā /
children.translated_text: Variegated with complete qualities, favorable to the factors of awakening, a garland of <s>Dharma</s> strung with a hundred thousand necklaces,

children.text: tūryarativighuṣṭā devatāgītaramyā amararucisvarā vai hlādanī vāgjinasya // 282 //
children.translated_text: resounding with the delight of instruments, lovely with the songs of deities, with voices beautiful as the gods' — gladdening is the speech of the <s>Jina</s>. [282]

children.text: kīnnarakalaviṅkākokilācakravākā barhiṇakalahaṃsāghoṣa konālakānām /
children.translated_text: <s>Kiṃnara</s>s, <s>kalaviṅka</s> birds, cuckoos, <s>cakravāka</s> birds, peacocks, elegant swans, the calls of <s>koṇāla</s> birds —

children.text: bramharutanirghoṣā kinnarāṇāṃ svarāṅgā akhalitamanavadyā sarvārthānubodhā // 283 //
children.translated_text: the sound of <s>Brahmā</s>'s voice, the melodious tones of <s>kiṃnara</s>s — unfaltering, blameless, awakening to all meanings. [283]

children.text: citrasphaṭikaślakṣṇā paṇḍitānāṃ manāpā codanī vinayanīyā bodhanī premaṇīyā /
children.translated_text: Variegated and smooth as crystal, pleasing to the learned, exhorting, disciplining, awakening, and endearing,

children.text: paracarimanakūlā toṣaṇī pṛcchamānā imaguṇa vacanā caitasya dharmeśvarasya // 284 //
children.translated_text: favorable to the welfare of others, satisfying those who ask — such are the qualities of the speech of this Lord of the <s>Dharma</s>. [284]

body.text: kamburucira grīvā śāntasaṃvṛttaskandhaḥ / dīrghaparigha bāhū tasya saptotsadāṅgam /

children.text: kara rucirasuvṛttā dirghavṛttāṅgulīkāḥ tapitakanakavarṇaṃ tasya gātraṃ jinasya // 285 //
children.translated_text: His hands are beautiful and well-rounded, with long, rounded fingers; the body of the <s>Jina</s> is the color of refined gold. [285]

body.translated_text: His neck is beautiful like a conch, his shoulders are peaceful and well-rounded; his arms are long like bars, and his body has seven prominences.

children.text: roma pariṇatāśca dakṣiṇo caikajātā nābhi nikhila durgā guhyakośo hayo vā /
children.translated_text: His body-hair is curled, each growing singly to the right; his navel is deep, his private parts are concealed like a horse's.

children.text: ūru gajakaro vā eṇajaṅghaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ karatala suvicitrā svastikāścakracitrāḥ // 286 //
children.translated_text: His thighs are like an elephant's trunk, his calves like an antelope's, the Self-Arisen One; his palms are beautifully marked with <s>svastika</s>s and wheel-designs. [286]

children.text: gajapatigatigāmī siṃhavikrāntagāmī vṛṣabhalalitagāmī indrayaṣṭipravṛddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: He walks with the gait of an elephant-lord, with the stride of a lion, with the graceful movement of a bull, grown tall like <s>Indra</s>'s banner-staff.

children.text: gaganakusumavṛṣṭiḥ puṣpachatrā bhavanti vrajatimanuvrajanti dharma ete 'dbhutasya // 287 //
children.translated_text: A rain of heavenly flowers and flower-canopies appears as he walks — these wonders attend [him] as they follow the <s>Dharma</s>. [287]

children.text: lābha atha alābhe saukhyaduḥkhe jinasya ayaśasi yaśa evaṃ nindaśaṃsāsu caivam /
children.translated_text: In gain and non-gain, in pleasure and pain for the <s>Jina</s>, in disrepute and fame, in blame and praise likewise —

children.text: jalaruhamiva toyaiḥ sarvato nopaliptaḥ evamiha nṛsiṃho nāsti sattvaḥ samo 'sya // 288 //
children.translated_text: like a lotus unstained by water on all sides — thus is this lion among men; there is no being equal to him. [288]

body.text:
atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumāraḥ buddhasya varṇaṃ śrutvā, vistareṇa dharmasya saṃghasya varṇaṃ śrutvā, tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto 'bhūt /
atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṣparaśme rājakumārasyaitadabhavat - yādṛśaḥ saṃbudho bhagavān, yādṛśī cāsya saṃghasaṃpat, yādṛśaśca tena dharmaḥ sākṣātkṛtaḥ, yādṛśī cāsya śiṣyasaṃpat, yathā viṣayasamavadhānaśca (

children.text: Vaidya, RP 152
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s>, RP 152)

children.text: ) saṃsāraḥ, yathākṛtajñaśca saṃsāraḥ, yathākṝtajñāśca bālapṛthagjanāḥ, yathā viṣamā ca satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ, yathā bahvādīnavaśca gṛhāvāsaḥ, yathā bahudoṣāśca kāmāḥ, yathā garhitaśca paṇḍitaiḥ pramādaḥ, yathā saṃmohaṃ cāvidyāndhakāram, yathā duḥprativedhāśca saṃskārāḥ, yathā durdamaṃ citram, yathā gambhīraṃ nāmarūpam, yathānāsvādaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam, yathā duḥkhavipākaścāparijñātaḥ sparśaḥ, yathā bahvādīnavā vedanāḥ, yathā gāḍhabandhanā tṛṣṇā, yathā duḥpratiniḥsaraṇaṃ copādānam, yathānāryā bhavatṛṣṇā, bhave sati yathā duḥkhasamucchedyā ca jātiḥ, yathā vikārakarī ca jarā, yathā vilopakārakaśca vyādhiḥ, yathā niruvuraktaṃ ca maraṇam, yathālpāsvādā ca pravṛttiḥ, yathā bahvādīnavā ca bhavābhinirvṛttiḥ, yathā ramaṇīyaṃ ca tathāgataśāsanam, nedaṃ śakyaṃ kāmadāsena kleśasaṃmohitena cittakhilena pramādābhiratena bālamadhyagatenāyoniśaścittena saṃsāraraktacittena durjanamadhyagatena na śakyaṃ sugatipanthānamapi viśodhayituṃ kutaḥ punaranuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum / tasyaitadabhūt - yannvahamita eva prāsādātprāṅbhukhaḥ prapateyam, mā me dvāreṇa niṣkramato jñātisaṃgho 'ntarāyaṃ kuryāt //
children.translated_text: the way <s>saṃsāra</s> is ungrateful, the way foolish ordinary beings are ungrateful, the way identity-view (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) is treacherous, the way household life has many dangers, the way sensual pleasures have many faults, the way heedlessness is condemned by the wise, the way ignorance-darkness is deluding, the way conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are hard to penetrate, the way the mind is hard to tame, the way name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) is profound, the way the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>) are without savor, the way uncomprehended contact (<s>sparśa</s>) has painful results, the way feelings (<s>vedanā</s>) have many dangers, the way craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is a tight bondage, the way clinging (<s>upādāna</s>) is hard to escape, the way craving for existence (<s>bhavatṛṣṇā</s>) is ignoble, the way birth (<s>jāti</s>) when there is existence leads to the mass of suffering, the way aging (<s>jarā</s>) causes decay, the way disease (<s>vyādhi</s>) is destructive, the way death (<s>maraṇa</s>) is without affection, the way continued existence (<s>pravṛtti</s>) has little savor, the way rebirth in existence (<s>bhavābhinirvṛtti</s>) has many dangers, and the way the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is delightful — [given all this,] it is not possible for one who is a slave to desires, deluded by afflictions, with a rigid mind, delighting in heedlessness, dwelling among fools, with unwise attention, with a mind attached to <s>saṃsāra</s>, dwelling among wicked people, to purify even the path to good destinies, let alone to fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect awakening.' This [thought] occurred to him: 'What if I were to throw myself headlong from this very palace, lest my kinsmen create an obstacle when I try to leave by the door!'

body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, having heard the virtues of the <s>Buddha</s>, and extensively the virtues of the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, became pleased, elated, uplifted in mind, joyful, and filled with delight and happiness. Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, this thought arose in prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>: 'Given the nature of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Bhagavān</s>, the wealth of his <s>Saṃgha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> he has directly realized, the excellence of his disciples, the way <s>saṃsāra</s> is like a fixation on sense objects,

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumāro yena bhagavān siddhārthabuddhisthathāgatastanmukhastataḥ prāsādādātmānamutsṛṣṭavān, evaṃ ca bhāṣate sma - sacetsa tathāgataḥ sarvaṃ jānāti sarvaṃ paśyati, samanvāharatu māṃ tathāgataḥ / atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla siddhārthabuddhistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho dakṣiṇapāṇiṃ prasārya prabhāṃ prāmuñcat, yayā puṇyaraśmi rājakumāraḥ spṛṣṭo 'bhūt / tasyāśca prabhāyāḥ śatasahasrapatraṃ padmaṃ śakaṭacakrapramāṇamātraṃ prādurbhūtam / tasmācca padmāt raśmiśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti sma, mahāṃścāvabhāso 'bhūt, yenāvabhāsena puṇyaraśmī rājakumāraḥ sphuṭo 'bhūt / aht khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumārastasmin padme sthitvā yena sa bhagavān siddhārdhabuddhistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya namo buddhāyetyudānamudānayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, facing toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, cast himself down from the palace, speaking thus: "If that <s>Tathāgata</s> truly knows all and sees all, may the <s>Tathāgata</s> take heed of me." Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhan</s> (worthy one), <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (perfectly awakened one), extended his right hand and released a radiance, by which prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> was touched. From that radiance there appeared a lotus of a hundred thousand petals, the size of a cart-wheel. From that lotus, hundreds of thousands of rays streamed forth, and a great illumination arose, by which prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> was enveloped. Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, standing upon that lotus, joined his palms in reverence toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Arhan</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, and uttered the inspired exclamation: "Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>!"

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla tena siddhārthabuddhinā tathāgatena sā prabhā pratisaṃhṛtā / sa ca kumārastasya bhagavataḥ pādamūle chinnāpādapa iva prapatitaḥ śatasahasrakṛtvastathāgataṃ vandate sma //
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, that radiance was withdrawn by <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>. And the prince fell at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> like a tree cut at its base, and paid homage to the <s>Tathāgata</s> a hundred thousand times.

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumārastaṃ bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> in verses:

children.text: mayā cirādadya hi vaidyarājaḥ kṛcchrādavāpto 'dya cirātureṇa /
children.translated_text: After long hardship, I have today found the king of physicians,

children.text: ācakṣva me nātha kathaṃ sthito 'haṃ lābhī bhaveyaṃ sugatasya śāsane // 289 //
children.translated_text: Tell me, O Protector, how I should abide so that I may gain a share in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> (well-gone one). (289)

children.text: śruto mayā nāyaka apramādo niśāmya rātrau divi devatābhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: I have heard, O Guide, of diligence, having learned at night from the <s>devatās</s> (deities) in heaven,

children.text: śrutvā ca saṃvigna hi āgato 'haṃ kathaṃ narāṇāṃ bhavate pramādaḥ // 290 //
children.translated_text: And having heard, I have come filled with spiritual urgency — how can there be heedlessness among people? (290)

children.text: pranaṣṭamārgasya bhavādya deśiko jātyandhabhūtasya bhavādya cakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: Be today a guide for one who has lost the path; be today eyes for one born blind,

children.text: mahāprapātādiha māṃ samuddhara śraddhākarā kāruṇikā cikitsakā // 291 //
children.translated_text: Lift me up from the great precipice here, O compassionate physician with hands of faith! (291)

children.text: daridrabhūtasya kuruṣva saṃgrahaṃ baddhasya mokṣaṃ kuru me 'dya nātha /
children.translated_text: Show kindness to one who is destitute; grant liberation to one who is bound, O Protector,

children.text: sasaṃśayebhyo vimatiṃ ca chinda caryāṃ ca me vyākuru bodhimārge // 292 //
children.translated_text: Cut through doubt for those beset by uncertainty, and prophesy my course on the path to awakening! (292)

children.text: Vaidya, RP 153
tīrthaṃ ca saṃdarśaya uhyato me dīpaṃ kuruṣvāpi mamāndhakāre /
children.translated_text: Show me the ford, for I am being swept away; make a lamp for me in this darkness,

children.text: vraṇīkṛtaṃ māṃ hi kuruṣva nirvraṇaṃ śalyaṃ ca me uddhara vaidyarāja // 293 //
children.translated_text: Heal me who am wounded, and extract the thorn, O king of physicians! (293)

children.text: vimocya māṃ durgatisaṃkaṭāttvaṃ bhavopalambhagrahaṇaṃ nikṛnta /
children.translated_text: Free me from the narrow strait of evil destinies; cut off the grasping after existence and apprehension,

children.text: saṃtāra māṃ śokamahaughapāram aṣṭāṅgamārgeṇa mahāpathena // 294 //
children.translated_text: Ferry me across to the far shore of the great flood of sorrow, by the eightfold path, the great highway! (294)

children.text: parīttamāyuḥ kṣayadharmi jīvitaṃ bahvantarāyaṃ kuśalaṃ bhavatyapi /
children.translated_text: Life is short, existence is subject to decay, and there are many obstacles even to what is wholesome,

children.text: puṇyasya sidhyatyacirādvipākaḥ labdhakṣaṇo me 'dya vadaikaniścayam // 295 //
children.translated_text: The fruit of merit ripens quickly — I have obtained my opportunity; now speak to me with a single resolve! (295)

children.text: etaddhi me vyākuru lokanātha syādbodhisattvo hi yathāpramattaḥ /
children.translated_text: Explain this to me, O Lord of the World: how should a <s>bodhisattva</s> (awakening-being) be heedful,

children.text: yathā carannuttamabodhicārikāṃ pramocayeyaṃ bhavabandhanājjagat // 296 //
children.translated_text: So that, practicing the supreme course of conduct toward awakening, I may liberate the world from the bonds of existence? (296)

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla siddhārthabuddhistathāgataḥ puṇyaraśme rājakumārasyādhyāśayaṃ viditvā vistareṇa bodhicaryāṃ saṃprakāśayati, yaṃ śrutvā puṇyaraśminā rājakumāreṇa vimokṣā nāma dhāraṇī praolabdhā, pañcābhijñāḥ pratilabdhāḥ / sa vaihāyase sthitvā puṣpāṇyabhinirmāya taṃ tathāgatamabhyavakirati sma, abhiprakirati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, having perceived the inner disposition of prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, expounded the conduct of awakening in detail. Having heard it, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> obtained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (retention formula) called <s>Vimokṣā</s> (Liberation) and attained the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges). Standing in the sky, he magically created flowers and showered them upon that <s>Tathāgata</s>, scattering them abundantly.

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmi rājakumārastasmādantarīkṣādavatīrya taṃ bhagavantaṃ siddhārthabuddhiṃ tathāgataṃ gāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, descending from the sky, praised that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> with verses:

children.text: vandāmi te kanakavarṇanibhā varalakṣaṇā vimalacandramukhā /
children.translated_text: I pay homage to you whose radiance is like gold, endowed with the excellent marks, whose face is like the spotless moon,

children.text: vandāmi te asamajñānadharā sadṛśo na te 'sti tribhave virajaḥ // 297 //
children.translated_text: I pay homage to you who bear incomparable knowledge — there is none equal to you in the three realms, O stainless one! (297)

children.text: mṛdu cāru snigdha śubha keśa jinā girirājatulya tava coṣṇiriha /
children.translated_text: Soft, lovely, glossy, and beautiful is the hair of the <s>Jina</s> (conqueror); your <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) here is like the king of mountains,

children.text: noṣṇīṣamīkṣitu tavāsti samo vibhrājate bhruvi vare 'pi tavorṇa mune // 298 //
children.translated_text: None is equal to you in beholding your <s>uṣṇīṣa</s>; the excellent <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft of hair) between your brows shines resplendently, O sage! (298)

children.text: kundenduśaṅkhahimaśubhranibhā nīlotpalābhaśubhanetravarā /
children.translated_text: Radiant like jasmine, moon, conch, and snow, with excellent auspicious eyes like blue lotuses,

children.text: kṛpayekṣase jagadidaṃ hi yayā vandāmi te vimalanetra jinā // 299 //
children.translated_text: You gaze upon this world with compassion — I pay homage to your stainless eyes, O <s>Jina</s>! (299)

children.text: jihvā prabhūta tanu tāmrani(bhā) vadanaṃ ca chādayasi yenasvakam /
children.translated_text: Your tongue is large, slender, and copper-hued, with which you cover your own face,

children.text: dharmaṃ vadan vinayase ca jagat vandāmi te madhurasnugdhagiram // 300 //
children.translated_text: Speaking the <s>Dharma</s> (teaching), you discipline the world — I pay homage to your sweet and gentle voice! (300)

children.text: daśanā śubhāḥ sudṛḍha vajranibhāḥ triṃśaddaśāpyaviralāḥ sahitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Your teeth are beautiful, firm, and diamond-like, thirty-two in number, close-set and even,

children.text: kurvan smitaṃ vinayase ca jagat vandāmi te madhurasatyakathā // 301 //
children.translated_text: When you smile, you tame the world — I pay homage to you whose speech is sweet and true! (301)

children.text: rūpeṇa cāpratisamo 'si jinā prabhayā ca bhāsayasi kṣetraśatān /
children.translated_text: In form you are without equal, O <s>Jina</s>; with your radiance you illuminate hundreds of buddha-fields,

children.text: bramhendrapāla jagato bhagavan jimhībhavanti tava te prabhayā // 302 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavān</s>, protector of the world like <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Indra</s>, even they are outshone by your radiance! (302)

children.text: eṇeyajaṅgha bhagavanna samā gajarājabarhimṛgarājagateḥ /
children.translated_text: Your calves are like those of an antelope, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, incomparable; your gait is like that of the king of elephants, a peacock, or the king of beasts,

children.text: īkṣan vrajasyati yugaṃ bhagavan saṃkampayan dharaṇiśailataṭam // 303 //
children.translated_text: Looking ahead a yoke's length as you walk, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, you cause the earth, mountains, and slopes to tremble! (303)

children.text: kāyaśca lakṣaṇacito bhagavan ślakṣṇa cchavī kanakavarṇaṃ tava /
children.translated_text: Your body is adorned with the marks, O <s>Bhagavān</s>; your skin is smooth and of golden hue,

children.text: nekṣan jagad vrajati tṛptimidaṃ rūpaṃ tavāpratimarūpadhara // 304 //
children.translated_text: The world never tires of gazing upon you, O bearer of incomparable form! (304)

children.text: tvaṃ pūrva kalpaśatacīrṇatapā tvaṃ sarvatyāgadamadānarataḥ /
children.translated_text: In former times you practiced austerities for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); you delighted in complete renunciation, self-restraint, and generosity,

children.text: tvaṃ sarvasattvakṛpamaitramanā vandāmi te paramakāruṇika // 305 //
children.translated_text: Your mind was ever filled with compassion and loving-kindness toward all beings — I pay homage to you, O supremely compassionate one! (305)

children.text: Vaidya, RP 154
tvaṃ dānaśīlanirataḥ satataṃ tvaṃ kṣāntivīryanirataḥ sudṛḍham /
children.translated_text: You are always devoted to <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct); you are firmly devoted to <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) and <s>vīrya</s> (energy),

children.text: tvaṃ dhyānaprajñaprabhatejadharo vandāmi te asamajñānadhara // 306 //
children.translated_text: You bear the radiant splendor of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) — I pay homage to you, O bearer of incomparable knowledge! (306)

children.text: tva vādiśūra kugaṇipramathi tvaṃ siṃhavannadasi parṣadi ca /
children.translated_text: You are a champion in debate, crusher of heretical factions; you roar the lion's roar in the assembly,

children.text: tvaṃ vaidyarāja trimalāntakaro vandāmi te paramaprītikara // 307 //
children.translated_text: You are the king of physicians who destroys the three defilements — I pay homage to you, O supreme joy-bringer! (307)

children.text: vākkāyamānasaviśuddha mune tribhaveṣvalipta jalapadmamiva /
children.translated_text: Pure in speech, body, and mind, O sage, untouched in the three realms, like a lotus in water,

children.text: tvaṃ bramhaghoṣa kalaviṅkaravā vandāmi te tribhavapāragatam // 308 //
children.translated_text: Yours is the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, the song of the <s>kalaviṅka</s> (sparrow-cuckoo) — I pay homage to you who have gone beyond the three realms! (308)

children.text: māyopamaṃ jagadidaṃ bhavatā naṭaraṅgasvapnasadṛśaṃ viditam /
children.translated_text: This world has been understood by you as like an illusion, resembling a dramatic performance, a mirage, or a dream,

children.text: nātmā na sattva na ca jīvagati dharmā marīcidakacandrasamāḥ // 309 //
children.translated_text: There is no self, no being, no life-principle; all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are like mirages, water-bubbles, and reflections of the moon. (309)

children.text: śūnyāśca śānta anutpādanaya avijānadeva jagadudbhramati /
children.translated_text: All is empty, peaceful, and unborn; yet the world, not knowing this, wanders in delusion,

children.text: teṣāmupāyanayayuktiśatairavatāratyasyapi kṛpālutayā // 310 //
children.translated_text: For their sake, through hundreds of skillful means and methods, you descend out of compassion. (310)

body.text:
rāgādibhiśca bahurogaśataiḥ saṃtāpitaṃ satatamīkṣya jagad /
vaidyottamo vicarase 'pratimaḥ parimocaya sugata sattvaśatān // 311 // jātījarāmaraṇaśokahataṃ priyaviprayogaparidevaśataiḥ /

children.text: satatāturaṃ ca jagadīkṣya mune parimocayan vicarase kṛpayā // 312 //
children.translated_text: Seeing the world constantly afflicted, O sage, you move about liberating them out of compassion. (312)

body.translated_text: Seeing the world constantly tormented by hundreds of diseases such as <s>rāga</s> (passion) and the rest, you, the supreme physician without equal, move about liberating hundreds of beings, O <s>Sugata</s>! (311) Stricken by birth, old age, death, and sorrow, by hundreds of lamentations and separation from the beloved,

children.text: rathacakravadbhramati sarvajagat tiryakṣu pretaniraye sugatau /
children.translated_text: Like a chariot wheel, all the world revolves — through animal realms, hungry ghost realms, hells, and fortunate destinies,

children.text: mūḍhā adeśika anāthagatāḥ teṣāṃ pradarśayasi mārgam // 313 //
children.translated_text: Deluded, without a guide, without a protector — to them you show the path. (313)

children.text: ye te babhūva purimāśca jinā dharmeśvarā jagati cārthakarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Jinas</s> (conquerors) who came before you, lords of the <s>Dharma</s> and benefactors of the world,

children.text: ayameva taiḥ prakathito 'ryapatho yaṃ deśayasyapi vibho 'pratimaḥ // 314 //
children.translated_text: This very noble path was proclaimed by them, which you too teach, O sovereign without equal! (314)

body.text:
snigdhaṃ hyakarṣaya manojña varaṃ bramhādhikaṃ paramaprītikaram /
gandharvakinnaravarāpsarasāmabhibhūya tāṃ giramudāharase // 315 // satyārjavakṣayamupāyanayaiḥ pariśodhitāṃ giramanantaguṇām /

children.text: śrutvā hi yāṃ niyutasattvaśatā yānatrayeṇa jina yānti śamam // 316 //
children.translated_text: Having heard which, hundreds of millions of beings, through the three vehicles, O <s>Jina</s>, attain peace. (316)

body.translated_text: With an affectionate, captivating, charming, excellent, surpassing even <s>Brahmā</s>'s, supremely delightful voice, surpassing even those of <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and the finest <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), you utter that speech. (315) Purified through truth, uprightness, inexhaustibility, and skillful means, that speech of infinite virtues,

children.text: tava pūjayā sukhamanekavidhaṃ divyaṃ labhanti manujeṣu tathā /
children.translated_text: Through worship of you, they obtain manifold happiness, both divine and among humans,

children.text: āḍhyo mahādhana mahāvibhavo bhavate jagaddhitakaro nṛpatiḥ // 317 //
children.translated_text: One becomes wealthy, of great riches and great splendor, a king who brings benefit to the world. (317)

children.text: valacakravartyapi ca dvīpapatiḥ jagadāvṛṇoti daśabhiḥ kuśalaiḥ /
children.translated_text: One becomes even a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), lord of the continents, covering the world with the ten wholesome deeds,

children.text: ratnāni sapta labhate suśubhāṃ tvayi saṃprasādajanako 'pratima // 318 //
children.translated_text: One obtains the seven treasures, most auspicious — in you, O incomparable one, faith is engendered! (318)

children.text: bramhāpi śakra api lokapatiḥ bhavate ca saṃtuṣitadevapatiḥ /
children.translated_text: One becomes <s>Brahmā</s>, or <s>Śakra</s>, or lord of the world, or lord of the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods,

children.text: parinirmito 'pi ca suyāmapatiḥ tvatpūjayā bhavati cāpi jinaḥ // 319 //
children.translated_text: Or lord of the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> (gods who control others' emanations), or lord of the <s>Suyāma</s> (heaven) — and through worship of you, one even becomes a <s>Jina</s> (conqueror)! (319)

children.text: evaṃ hyamogha tava pūja kṛtā saṃdarśanaṃ śravaṇamapyasamam /
children.translated_text: Thus your worship, performed with purpose, is never fruitless; even the sight and hearing of you is incomparable,

children.text: bhavate jagadvividhaduḥkhaharaḥ spṛśate paraṃ padavaraṃ hyajaram // 320 //
children.translated_text: One becomes a remover of the manifold sufferings of the world, and touches the supreme, excellent, undecaying state. (320)

children.text: mārgajña mārgakuśalā bhagavan kupathānnivārayasi lokamimam /
children.translated_text: O knower of the path, skilled in the path, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, you turn this world away from wrong paths,

children.text: kṣeme śive viraja āryapathe pratiṣṭhāpapyasyapi jagadbhagavan //321 //
children.translated_text: And establish the world upon the safe, auspicious, stainless, noble path, O <s>Bhagavān</s>! (321)

children.text: Vaidya, RP 155
puṇyādhikasya tava puṇyanidheḥ satatākṣayā bhavati puṇyakriyā /
children.translated_text: For you who are rich in merit, O treasury of merit, the creation of merit is perpetual and inexhaustible,

children.text: bahukalpakoṭīṣu na yāti kṣayaṃ yāvanna saṃspṛśati bodhicarām // 322 //
children.translated_text: It does not diminish even through hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> (ten millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), until one attains the course of awakening. (322)

children.text: pariśuddha kṣetra labhate ruciraṃ paranirmitābha sada prītikaram /
children.translated_text: One obtains a pure and beautiful buddha-field, radiant like the <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> (heaven), always delightful,

children.text: śuddhāśca kāyavacasā manasā sattvā bhavantyapi ca kṣetravare // 323 //
children.translated_text: And beings in that excellent field are pure in body, speech, and mind. (323)

children.text: ityevamādiguṇa naikavidhān labhate jinārcanakṛtān manujaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus these and many other kinds of virtues does a person obtain through honoring the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: svargāpavarga manujeṣu sukhaṃ bhavate ca puṇyanidhi sarvajage // 324 //
children.translated_text: Both heavenly bliss and liberation, happiness among humans — one becomes a treasury of merit for all the world. (324)

children.text: kīrtiryaśaśca prasṛtaṃ vipulaṃ tava sarvadikṣu bahukṣetraśatān /
children.translated_text: Your fame and glory spread vast and wide, through hundreds of fields in all directions,

children.text: saṃkīrtayanti sugatāḥ satataṃ tava varṇamāla parṣatsu jinā // 325 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Sugatas</s> (well-gone ones) constantly proclaim the garland of your praises in their assemblies, O <s>Jina</s>! (325)

children.text: vigatajvarā jagati mokṣakarā priyadarśanā paramakāruṇikā /
children.translated_text: Free from affliction, liberators of the world, beautiful to behold, supremely compassionate,

children.text: śāntendriyā śamaratā bhagavan vandāmi te naravarapravarā // 326 //
children.translated_text: With senses at peace, delighting in tranquility, O <s>Bhagavān</s> — I pay homage to you, best among the foremost of men! (326)

children.text: labdhā abhijña jina pañca mayā gagane sthitastava niśāmya giram /
children.translated_text: I have attained the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), O <s>Jina</s>; standing in the sky, having heard your speech,

children.text: bhavitāsmi vīra sugatau pratimaḥ vibhajiṣya dharmamamalaṃ jagataḥ // 327 //
children.translated_text: I shall become, O hero, an image of the <s>Sugata</s> (well-gone one), and shall distribute the stainless <s>Dharma</s> to the world! (327)

children.text: stutvādya sarvaguṇapāragataṃ naradevanāgamahitaṃ sugatam /
children.translated_text: Having praised the <s>Sugata</s> who has gone to the far shore of all virtues, honored by gods, humans, and <s>nāgas</s> (serpent-beings),

children.text: puṇyaṃ yadarjitamidaṃ vipulaṃ jagadāpnuyādapi ca buddhapadam // 328 //
children.translated_text: May the vast merit generated here lead the world to attain the state of <s>Buddhahood</s>! (328)

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla rājā arciṣmāṃstasyā rātryā atyayenāśroṣītkumārasyāntaḥpure ruditaśabdam / śrutvā ca śīghraṃ tvaramāṇarūpo yena ratipradhānaṃ nagaraṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat / upasaṃkramyaitadavocat - kiṃ bhavantyo rudanti ? tā avocān - puṇyaraśmī rājakumāro na dṛśyate / atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla rājā arciṣmān kumārasyārthe chinnapādapa ina dharaṇītale prapatitaḥ / sa utthāya dharaṇitalāt sahasraśaśca tannagaraṃ paricarati rudamānaḥ / atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla yā tasminnagare nagaradevatā sā rājānamarciṣmantametadavocat - gato mahārāja kumāraḥ pūrvasmin digbhāge siddhārthabuddhiṃ tathāgataṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya //
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, King <s>Arciṣmān</s>, at the passing of that night, heard the sound of weeping in the prince's inner quarters. Having heard it, he hastened swiftly to the city called <s>Ratipradhāna</s>. Approaching, he said: "Why are you weeping?" They replied: "Prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> is nowhere to be seen." Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, King <s>Arciṣmān</s>, for the sake of the prince, fell upon the ground like a tree cut at its base. Rising from the ground, he searched that city a thousand times, weeping. Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, the city goddess of that city spoke to King <s>Arciṣmān</s> thus: "The prince has gone, O great king, to the eastern quarter, to see, honor, and attend upon <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>."

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla rājā arciṣmān kumārasyāntaḥpureṇa sārdhaṃ caturaśītibhiḥ prāṇakoṭiniyutaśatasahasrairyena pūrvo digbhāgastenopajagāma / yena siddhārthabuddhistathāgato 'rhan samyassaṃbuddhastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivanditvā ekānte 'tiṣṭhat / ekāntasthitaśca rājā arciṣmān bhagavantamābhirgāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt -
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, King <s>Arciṣmān</s>, together with the prince's inner court and eighty-four <s>koṭī-niyuta</s>-hundred-thousands of beings, proceeded toward the eastern quarter. He approached <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Arhan</s> <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and stood to one side. Standing to one side, King <s>Arciṣmān</s> praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these verses:

children.text: vandāmi guṇajñānasāgaraṃ naravīraṃ yasya nāsti samaḥ kuto 'dhikastribhave 'smin /
children.translated_text: I pay homage to the hero among men, an ocean of virtues and knowledge, who has no equal — whence then a superior? — in these three realms,

children.text: devendrāsurarājasatkṛtaṃ varasattvaṃ tṛptiṃ naiti jano nirīkṣatastava rūpam // 329 //
children.translated_text: Honored by lords of gods, <s>asuras</s> (demons), and kings, O excellent being — the world never tires of gazing upon your form! (329)

children.text: dvātriṃśattava kāyalakṣaṇā suviśuddhā merurvā vararatnacitritaḥ pariśuddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Your thirty-two bodily marks are perfectly pure, like <s>Meru</s> adorned with the finest jewels, utterly resplendent,

children.text: ślakṣṇaṃ kāñcanavarṇasaṃnibhaṃ jinakāntaṃ vandāmi priyarūpadarśanaṃ munikāyam // 330 //
children.translated_text: Smooth and resembling the color of gold, the body of the <s>Jina</s> is beautiful — I pay homage to the body of the sage, lovely to behold! (330)

children.text: Vaidya, RP 156
kalpānacintya śatāśca koṭiyo vrata cīrṇā buddhakoṭiśatāśca satkṛtā bahukalpān /
children.translated_text: For inconceivable hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> (ten millions) of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), vows were fulfilled, and hundreds of <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> were honored over many aeons,

children.text: yaṣṭā yajñaśatā acintiyāparimāṇā kāyastena tavābhirājate abhirūpaḥ // 331 //
children.translated_text: Innumerable, inconceivable hundreds of sacrifices were offered — therefore your body shines forth, resplendent! (331)

children.text: dānaśīlasamādhiprajñayāpi ca kṣāntyā vīryadhyānamupāyaśodhitaṃ tava rūpam /
children.translated_text: Your form has been purified through <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (energy), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and skillful means,

children.text: candrārkamaṇidyutiprabhā na virāji śakrabramhaprabhā na bhāsate purataste // 332 //
children.translated_text: The radiance of moon, sun, and jewels does not shine before you; the splendor of <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s> does not gleam in your presence! (332)

children.text: rūpaṃ darśayate manoramaṃ jagadarthe pratibhāsodakacandrasaṃnibhaṃ yatha māyā /
children.translated_text: You display a form that delights the mind, for the sake of the world, resembling a reflection, water-moon, or an illusion,

children.text: sarvāsveva ca dikṣu dṛśyate jinakāyo no cā rūpapramāṇu dṛśyate sugatānām // 333 //
children.translated_text: The body of the <s>Jina</s> is seen in every direction, yet not even an atom of form can be perceived in the <s>Sugatas</s>! (333)

children.text: tuṣiteṣu kvacideva dṛśyase nivasaṃstvaṃ vyūḍhamānaśca punaḥ supāṇḍaragajabhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sometimes you are seen dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> (heaven), and then descending, having become a great white elephant,

children.text: mātu kukṣigataśca dṛśyase 'pi ca vīraḥ sarvatrānugato mahāmune nabhatulyaḥ // 334 //
children.translated_text: You are seen entering a mother's womb, O hero — yet you pervade everywhere, O great sage, like the sky! (334)

children.text: jātiṃ saṃdarśayase kvacidbhavān diśatāsu gacchan sapta padāni dṛśyase kvacidurvyām /
children.translated_text: Sometimes you display birth; in certain regions you are seen taking seven steps upon the earth,

children.text: hyeṣṭho 'haṃ sanarāmare jage atidevo mociṣye jaga duḥkhasāgarādgira muñcan // 335 //
children.translated_text: "I am the foremost in the world with its gods and mortals, surpassing even the gods; I shall liberate the world from the ocean of suffering!" — thus releasing your speech. (335)

body.text: dharmasaṃśayu nāsti te mune kvacideva śikṣāṃ cāpi ca loka dṛśyate lipijñāne śāntaṃ dhyānasamādhigocaramanuprāptaṃ strīṇāṃ madhyagataśca dṛśyate kvacideva // 336 //
body.translated_text: There is no doubt in you regarding the <s>Dharma</s>, O sage; anywhere one sees [you] training, and the world sees [you] peaceful, within the domain of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), having attained [these]; and you are also seen somewhere dwelling among women. [336]

children.text: tyaktvā mātāpitā mahītale pramadāśca jñātīn śokahatān vimūrcchitān viruvantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned mother and father on the earth, along with women and kinsmen who are grief-stricken, fainting, and wailing,

children.text: niṣkrānto vanavāsamīkṣyase padamekaṃ devākoṭiśataiḥ parivṛto varasattvaḥ // 337 //
children.translated_text: you are seen as one gone forth, dwelling in the forest, going alone, surrounded by hundreds of millions of gods — a supreme being. [337]

children.text: mārāste caturo 'pi nirjitāścirakālaṃ mārān dharṣayamāṇa dṛśyate 'pi ca kṣetre /
children.translated_text: Even the four <s>Māra</s>s have been conquered by you; for a long time you are seen overcoming the <s>Māra</s>s, even in [various] fields.

children.text: cakraṃ vartayase 'pyacintiyaṃ purimeṇa cakraṃ vartayamāna dṛśyase kṛpayā tvam // 338 //
children.translated_text: You also turn the inconceivable wheel [of <s>Dharma</s>]; you are seen turning the wheel as before, out of compassion. [338]

children.text: Vaidya, RP 157
nityaṃ śāśvatadṛṣṭisaṃjñitaṃ jagadīkṣya nirvāsya iti vāca bhāṣase pariṣatsu /
children.translated_text: Seeing the world always characterized by the view of permanence, you speak the words 'it will pass away' in the assemblies.

children.text: saṃsārābhirataṃ jagatsatatamīkṣya śāntāṃ śītagatiṃ ca nirvṛtiṃ vadasi tvam // 339 //
children.translated_text: Seeing the world constantly delighting in <s>saṃsāra</s>, you proclaim the peaceful, cool state of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation). [339]

children.text: puṇyajñānamupāyaprajñato na samaste sphurase kāyaprabhāya tvaṃ mune bahukṣetrān /
children.translated_text: Through merit, knowledge, skillful means, and wisdom, not fully [comprehensible] are you, O sage — you illuminate many fields with your bodily radiance.

children.text: bhāṣante tava varṇa nāyakā diśatāsu vande tvāmasamantagocaraṃ munirājam // 340 //
children.translated_text: The leaders in all directions proclaim your virtues — I salute you, O king of sages, whose domain is everywhere. [340]

children.text: vandāmo 'pi ca dharmatāmakhilaprāptaṃ sarvasattvakriyāsu dṛśyase yatha māyā /
children.translated_text: We also worship the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality) that you have fully attained; in the activities for all beings, you appear like an illusion.

children.text: na ca te 'styāgamanaṃ kvacidgamanaṃ vā māyādharma sati pratiṣṭhitamabhivande // 341 //
children.translated_text: There is neither coming nor going for you anywhere — I worship [you] who are established in the nature of illusion-like <s>dharma</s>s. [341]

children.text: sādhu tvaṃ naravīra bhāṣase varamārgaṃ bodhiryena varā hyavāpyate jagadarthe /
children.translated_text: Well do you, O hero among men, proclaim the supreme path by which the supreme awakening is attained for the welfare of the world.

children.text: etāmapyahamāśu dharmatāmanubuddhā deśeyaṃ naravīraṃ dhamatāṃ jagadarthe // 342 //
children.translated_text: May I too quickly understand this <s>dharmatā</s> and teach the <s>dharmatā</s> of the hero among men for the welfare of the world! [342]

children.text: sarvajñaṃ vigatajvaraṃ naravīraṃ yasya nāsti samaḥ kuto 'dhikastribhave 'smin /
children.translated_text: Having praised the Omniscient One, the hero among men free from fever, who has no equal — whence then a superior in this triple existence? —

children.text: stutvā puṇyamupārjitaṃ mayā yadiha tena śāntāṃ bodhivarāmanuttarāṃ spṛśatu lokaḥ // 343 //
children.translated_text: by whatever merit has been earned by me here through praise, may the world attain the supreme, peaceful, unsurpassed awakening! [343]

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla sa tathāgataḥ siddhārthabuddhiḥ rājño 'rciṣmato 'dhyāśayaṃ viditvā tathā dharmaṃ deśayāmāsa yathā sarve avaivartikā abhūvannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau //
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s>, having understood the deep intention (<s>adhyāśaya</s>) of King <s>Arciṣmat</s>, taught the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that all became irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) from unsurpassed, perfect awakening.

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumārastaṃ bhagavantaṃ siddhārthabuddhiṃ tathāgatametadavocat - adhivāsayatu bhagavānasmākāṃ nagare śvobhaktena / adhivāsayati ca bhagavān puṇyaraśme rājakumārasya tūṣṇībhāvenānukampāmupādāya //
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Siddhārthabuddhi</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept a meal tomorrow in our city.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> through silence, out of compassion.

body.text: atha khalu puṇyaraśmī rājakumārastau mātāpitarau tāśva pramadā āmantrayati sma - anumodayantu bhavantaḥ sarve sahitāḥ sarve samagrāḥ / yathālaṃkṛtaṃ ratipradhānaṃ nagaraṃ tathāgatasya niryātayāmuanapekṣaḥ / tairekasvareṇānumoditam //
body.translated_text: Then prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> addressed his parents and those women: 'May all of you together, assembled as one, approve! I shall offer the city, adorned as it is and filled with pleasures, to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, without attachment.' They all approved with one voice.

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla puṇyaraśmī rājakumāro yathālaṃkṛtaṃ ratipradhānaṃ nagaraṃ tathāgatāya niryātayati sma anapekṣaḥ / pañcarasaśatavyūhena ca bhojanena taṃ tathāgataṃ pratipādayati sma sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena / sarveṣāṃ teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ saptaratnacitān vihārān kārayāmāsa maṇicaṃkramān prajñaptānupari ca ratnajālavitānavitatān vāmadakṣiṇena puṣpavṛkṣasupariniṣṭhitān / puṇḍarīkapuṣkariṇyupaśibhitānyubhayato mukhanirmaladūṣyaśatasahasraprajñaptāni (

children.text: Vaidya, RP 158
children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s>, RP 158)

children.text: ) śayyāsanāni / ekaikasya ca bhikṣorabhivandya cīvaro dīyate sma ekaikaḥ / anyonyāni cīvarāṇyanipradīyante divase divase / sa tribhirvarṣakoṭibhiḥ styānamiddhaṃ nāvakrāmitavān, nātmaprema kṛtavān, buddhapūjāṃ prati nānyamanasikāraḥ / etasminnantare na kāmavitarkaṃ vitarkitavān, na vyāpādavitarkaṃ na vihiṃsāvitarkaṃ na rājyatṛṣṇām / sarvathānapekṣo 'bhūtkāye jīvite ca, prāgevānyatarasmin bāhyavastuni / etasminnantare yadbhagavatā bhāṣitaṃ tatsarvamavadhāritam, na ca dvirapi sa tathāgataḥ pṛṣṭaḥ / etasminnantare na snāto na sarpitailena vā gātraṃ mrakṣitam, na pādadhāvanaṃ kṛtam, na klāntasaṃjñotpāditā, na jātu niṣaṇṇo 'nyatra bhaktaparibhogārthamuccāraprasrāvaṇārthaṃ ca / yasmiṃśca samaye sa tathāgataḥ parinirvṛtastasmin samaye lohitacandranasya citā kāritā / yatra sa tathāgato dhmāpitastasminneva ca pṛthivipradeśe varṣaśatasahasraṃ dhātūnāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtavān / sarvaṃ jambūdvīpaṃ sarvapuṣpaiḥ sarvamālyaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ sarvavādyairyāvat sarvapūjāsatkārān kṛtvā pañcāccaturnavatiḥ stūpakoṭyaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitavān / te ca stūpāḥ saptaratnamayā ratnajālasaṃchannā muktājālavitānavitatāḥ / saptānāṃ ratnānāṃ pañca pañca chatraśatānyekaikasmin stūpe āropitavān / sarvatra ca stūpe tūryaśatasahasrāṇi niścāritavān / samantataśca jambūdvīpe puṣpavṛkṣān ropitavān / ekaikatra dīpyate sarvagandhatailasya / sarvagandhamālyavilepanaiśca pūjāmakarot / anenopāyena varṣakoṭiṃ pūjāṃ kṝtvāḥ tataḥ pravrajitaḥ / sa pravrajitā traicīvariko 'bhavat / nityaṃ piṇḍapātacāriko 'naiṣadyikaḥ / na jātu pārśvaṃ dattavān, na styānamiddhamavakrāmitavān / tena nirāmiṣacittena catako varṣakoṭyo dharmadānaṃ dattam / na cānenāntaśaḥ / sādhukāro 'pi parasyāntikātpratikāṅkṣitaḥ, kutaḥ punarlābhasatkāraḥ / nāpi klānto 'bhūddharmaśravaṇena dharmadeśanayā ca / tasya devatāḥ paricaryāṃ kurvanti sma / tasya cānuśikṣitvā sarvajanapado 'ntaḥpuraṃ sarvapādamūlaṃ sarvasahāyāśca pravrajitāḥ //
children.translated_text: beds and seats furnished with a hundred thousand pure and spotless cloths. To each and every monk, he gave robes, bowing [to each]. Different robes were given day after day. For three million years he did not succumb to sloth and torpor, did not give in to self-love, and had no other mental preoccupation than worship of the <s>Buddha</s>. During this time, he did not entertain thoughts of sensual desire, nor thoughts of malice, nor thoughts of harm, nor craving for kingship. He was entirely without attachment to body and life, let alone to any external object. During this time, he retained everything spoken by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and never questioned the <s>Tathāgata</s> a second time. During this time, he did not bathe, nor anoint his body with ghee or oil, nor wash his feet, nor generate the perception of fatigue, nor ever sat down except for the purpose of eating food and for bodily evacuations. At the time that <s>Tathāgata</s> passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, a pyre of red sandalwood was prepared. In that very spot where the <s>Tathāgata</s> was cremated, for a hundred thousand years he performed worship of the relics (<s>dhātu</s>). He made the entire <s>Jambudvīpa</s> [fragrant] with all flowers, all garlands, all incenses, all instruments, and performed all forms of worship and honor. He established ninety-four and a half million <s>stūpa</s>s, all made of the seven jewels, covered with nets of jewels, with canopies of pearl-nets spread above, with five hundred parasols of each of the seven jewels placed upon each <s>stūpa</s>. Everywhere at each <s>stūpa</s>, he produced the sound of a hundred thousand instruments. All around <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, he planted flower-trees. At each place, lamps of all fragrances and oils were lit. With all fragrant garlands and unguents, he performed worship. Having thus performed worship for ten million years, he then went forth [as a monk]. Having gone forth, he wore the three robes. He always went on alms-round, practiced the sitting posture [without lying down]. He never lay on his side; he never succumbed to sloth and torpor. With a mind free from material desire, for forty million years he gave the gift of <s>Dharma</s>. Not even a 'well done!' did he expect from anyone, let alone gain and honor. He was never wearied by hearing or teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Deities attended to him. Following his example, the entire populace, the inner palace, all attendants, and all companions went forth.

body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> offered the city, adorned and filled with pleasures, to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, without attachment. With food of five hundred flavors, he served that <s>Tathāgata</s> together with the community of monks. For all those monks, he had monasteries constructed, adorned with the seven jewels, with gem-paved walkways, covered above with canopies of jewel-nets, flanked on left and right by well-established flower-trees, beautified on both sides by white lotus ponds, with

body.text: atha khalu rāṣṭrapāla śūddhāvāsakāyikānāṃ devaputrāṇāmetadabhavat - puṇyaraśmeranuśikṣamāṇaḥ sarvarājyajanakadaḥ pravrajitaḥ / asmābhistasyopasthānaparicaryā kartavyā / trayāṇāṃ ratnānāmupasthāna kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati / tasya punastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya catuḥṣaṣṭivarṣakoṭyaḥ saddharmastasthau / sarvasya puṇyaraśminā bhikṣuṇā buddhasahasrasya caivaṃrūpā pūjā kṛtābhūt //
body.translated_text: Then, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, this thought arose in the minds of the <s>Śuddhāvāsakāyika</s> (Pure Abode) gods: 'Following the example of <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>, all the people of the kingdom have gone forth. We should render service and attendance to him; service to the Three Jewels will have been performed.' Furthermore, the true <s>Dharma</s> of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, endured for sixty-four million years. The monk <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> performed worship of this kind to all those thousand <s>Buddha</s>s.

body.text:
syātkhalu punaste rāṣṭrapāla etarhi kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayenārciṣmān nāma rājābhūt / na khalu punastvayaivaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ ? amitāyuḥ sa tathāgatastena kālena tena samayenārciṣmānnāma rājābhūt / syātkhalu punaste rāṣṭrapāla - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena puṇyaraśmirnāma rājakumāro 'bhūt / na khalu punastvayaivaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatkasya hetoḥ ? ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena puṇyaraśmirnāma rājakumāro 'bhūt / yāpi sā nagaradevatā, akṣobhyastathāgato 'bhūt /

children.translated_text: (<s>Vaidya</s>, RP 159)

children.text: ) tasmāttarhi rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvena mahāsattvenānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhukāmena tasya puṇyaraśmirājakumārasyāniśikṣitavyamadhyāśayapratipattyā priyāpriyaparityāgitayā apramādacaryayā - evaṃ duḥkhābhisaṃskārapratilabdhā me 'nuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti / tatte 'nabhiyuktā lābhasatkāraślokagurukā jñātyadhyavasitā mānahatā lābhahatāstapasvino vihanyante, lābhahetoḥ śāsanāddūrībhavanti, nirarthakaṃ pravrajitāḥ śramaṇadūṣakā bodhisattvakhaṭukāḥ kāyavākcittavaṅkāḥ naimittikāḥ vitathapratijñāḥ svapratijñātaścyutāḥ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayyāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāranimittamadhyavasitāḥ / ahrīkā anapatrapā acāritrā asaddharmaprasṛtā gocaravirahitā buddhagocarāddūrībhūtā buddhajñānavirahitāḥ mokṣacittavirahitāḥ bodhicittavirahitāḥ / tasmāttarhi rāṣṭrapāla imamevaṃrūpaṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā boddhavyam - pāpamitrānyudyuktāni na sevitavyāni lābhārthikānām //
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, a <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> (great being) who wishes to fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect awakening should train following the example of prince <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s> — through deep intention and practice, through abandoning what is dear and what is not dear, through the conduct of heedfulness — [thinking]: 'Unsurpassed, perfect awakening has been obtained by me through such painful effort.' Those who are not diligent, who are intent on gain, honor, and fame, who are under the influence of kinsmen, struck down by pride, struck down by gain — those ascetics are obstructed. For the sake of gain, they become distant from the teaching. Having gone forth to no purpose, they are corrupters of the ascetic life, bitter toward <s>bodhisattva</s>s, crooked in body, speech, and mind, fortune-tellers, making false promises, fallen from their own vows, devoted to obtaining robes, alms-food, beds, seats, and medicine for the sick. Shameless, without moral dread, without proper conduct, following wrong <s>dharma</s>s, devoid of proper resort, far from the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>, devoid of the <s>Buddha's</s> knowledge, devoid of the mind of liberation, devoid of the mind of awakening. Therefore, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, having heard this kind of <s>Dharma</s>, one should understand: 'The evil companions who are intent [on gain] should not be associated with by those who seek [true] gain.'

body.translated_text: Perhaps, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, you might now have doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation [thinking]: 'It was someone else who at that time, at that occasion, was the king named <s>Arciṣmat</s>.' You should not view it thus. Why? The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> was at that time, at that occasion, the king named <s>Arciṣmat</s>. Perhaps, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, [you might think]: 'It was someone else who at that time, at that occasion, was the prince named <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>.' You should not view it thus. Why? I myself at that time, at that occasion, was the prince named <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>. And as for that city-deity, she was the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Akṣobhya</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: aprameye daśabalacalite lābhe jñātau parigatahṛdayā /
children.translated_text: Those whose hearts are possessed, known [only] for gain, in the immeasurable [teaching] set in motion by the One with Ten Powers —

children.text: hitvā bodhiṃ guṇaśatanicitāṃ lābhārthaṃ te parakulanicatāḥ // 344 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned the awakening adorned with a hundred virtues, they bow down in others' households for the sake of gain. [344]

children.text: dhvāṅkṣā duṣṭā hrīdhṛtirahitā kṣetrārthaṃ te namucivaśagatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Crows, wicked, devoid of shame and steadfastness, for the sake of possessions they have fallen under the power of <s>Namucī</s> (<s>Māra</s>).

children.text: kleśādhīnā bhavagatipraṇatā bhāṣantyevaṃ vayamapi guṇinaḥ // 345 //
children.translated_text: Subject to afflictions, bent toward the courses of existence, they speak thus: 'We too are endowed with virtues!' [345]

children.text: kāyo 'raṇye smṛtirapi nagare lābhārthaṃ te caritavikalpe /
children.translated_text: Their body is in the forest, but their mind is in the city; for the sake of gain, their conduct is confused.

children.text: dūre mokṣo nabha iva dharaṇi dūre jāhu bhujagavadetān // 346 //
children.translated_text: Liberation is as far from them as heaven is from the earth — keep far away from these, as from a serpent's mouth! [346]

children.text: buddho dharmo na ca priyavadatāṃ tadvatsaṃgho guṇaśatabharitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither the <s>Buddha</s> nor the <s>Dharma</s> is [attained] by those of [merely] pleasant speech; likewise the <s>Saṃgha</s>, filled with a hundred virtues.

children.text: hitvā svargaṃ kupathaprayātā aṣṭavighātairbhavaśatavihatāḥ // 347 //
children.translated_text: Having abandoned heaven, they have gone on the wrong path, struck by the eight adversities, beaten by a hundred existences. [347]

children.text: śrutvaināṃ mama cārikāṃ samupadiṣṭāṃ bhūtādhyāśayato 'tra yujyathā pratipattyā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this conduct of mine, which has been taught from a sincere deep intention, apply yourselves here in practice.

children.text: duṣprāpyaṃ bahukalpakoṭibhiḥ kṣaṇaprāptā tasmādatra yathoktadharmatāmabhiyujyet // 348 //
children.translated_text: What is hard to obtain even in many millions of aeons — having obtained this moment, one should apply oneself to the <s>dharmatā</s> as it has been taught. [348]

children.text: yo hīcchedvarabodhi budhyituṃ varayāne smāryāstena mahīpate guṇāstasya /
children.translated_text: Whoever wishes to awaken to the supreme awakening — in the supreme vehicle, O lord of the earth, the virtues of that one should be remembered.

children.text: saṃcintya yathābhūta yoniśaḥ sthātavyamevaṃ bodhi asaṅga ridhyate sugatānām // 349 //
children.translated_text: Having reflected truly and wisely, one should stand thus — the unattached awakening of the <s>Sugata</s>s (Well-Gone Ones) is accomplished. [349]

children.text: āryaṃ vaṃśaṃ niṣevate guṇaprekṣī jñānaṃ tatra utpādayecchu ivātra /
children.translated_text: One who observes the noble lineage (<s>āryavaṃśa</s>), looking to virtues, should generate knowledge there, as if a needle [of urgency] were here.

children.text: mā evaṃ pravijahya śāsanaṃ guṇamaṇḍaṃ sarvāsvetagatīṣu pañcasū yatha bālāḥ // 350 //
children.translated_text: Do not thus abandon the teaching, the ornament of virtues, in all five destinies, as fools [do]. [350]

children.text: Vaidya, RP 160
śailāraṇyaguhānijāsino bhavateha tatrasthāśca ma ātma manyathā paṭapaṃsī /
children.translated_text: Those dwelling in mountain forests and caves should not regard themselves [proudly] — those who are there, clothed in rags.

children.text: ātmānaṃ paribhāṣathā satatanitya - manusmaranto buddhakoṭi virāgitā purimā ye // 351 //
children.translated_text: Constantly reproach yourself, always remembering — those former ones, the millions of <s>Buddha</s>s, became free from passion. [351]

children.text: kāye jīvita tṛṣṇa utsṛha anapekṣā dharme yujyata tīvra gauravaṃ janayitvā /
children.translated_text: Abandon craving for body and life; without attachment, apply yourself to the <s>Dharma</s>, generating intense reverence.

children.text: pratipattiśca mayāpi bhāṣitā iha sūtre paścā bodhi na teṣu durlabhā iha sthitvā // 352 //
children.translated_text: The practice has been taught by me in this <s>sūtra</s> — for those who abide in it, awakening afterward is not hard to obtain. [352]

children.text: ye yuktāśca ihāpi harṣitā jinayāne śrutvā yukta sudurmanā bhavitāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are diligent and delighted here in the <s>Jina</s>-vehicle — having heard [it], those who are diligent will become supremely resolved.

children.text: tasmādvai janayeta śāsane adhimuktiṃ mā paścādanutāpa bheṣyathā vicaramāṇāḥ // 353 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should generate faith in the teaching — do not afterwards be in anguish as you wander! [353]

body.text: yaśca punā rāṣṭrapāla bodhisattvaḥ pañcapāramitāsu caret, yaśceha dharmaparyāyapratipatyā saṃpādayet - ahamatra śikṣiṣye 'hamatra saṃvare sthāsyāmi / eṣa puṇyaskandho 'sya puṇyaskandhasya purataḥ śatatamāmapi kalāṃ nopaiti sahasratamāmapi śatasahasratamāmapi koṭiśatasahasratamāmapi, saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapi upamāmapi upanisāmapi dhṛtipadamapi nopaiti / asmin khalu punardharmaparyāye bhāsyamāṇe triṃśatāṃ niyutānāṃ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāśca prajāyā anutpadantapūrvāṇyanuttarasyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpannāni / avaivartyāścābhūvannanuttarasyāḥ samyaksambodheḥ / saptānāṃ ca bhikṣusahasrāṇāmanupādāyāsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni //
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, if a <s>bodhisattva</s> were to practice the five <s>pāramitā</s>s (perfections), and another were to accomplish [the merit] through the practice of this <s>dharma</s> discourse — [thinking] 'I shall train here; I shall abide in this discipline' — this mass of merit does not reach even a hundredth part of that [former] mass of merit, nor a thousandth, nor a hundred-thousandth, nor a hundred-thousand-millionth; it does not reach it by any calculation, fraction, computation, comparison, or analogy, or any ground of comprehension. Furthermore, when this <s>dharma</s> discourse was being proclaimed, in thirty million [beings], including gods, humans, <s>asura</s>s, and the [whole] generation, minds directed toward unsurpassed, perfect awakening arose that had never arisen before. And they became irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) from unsurpassed, perfect awakening. And seven thousand monks had their minds liberated from the outflows (<s>āsrava</s>) without further clinging.

body.text: atha khalu āyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālo bhagavantametadavocat - kiṃnāmāyaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyaḥ,kathaṃ cainaḥ dhārayāmi ? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ rāṣṭrapālametadavocat - amoghapratijñāviśuddhamiti nāma dhāraya / satpuruṣavikrīḍitaṃ bodhisattvacaryāviniścayaṃ nāma dhāraya / arthapāripūrī ca nāma dhāraya //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s> addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What is the name of this <s>dharma</s> discourse, <s>Bhagavān</s>, and how should I retain it?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>: 'Retain it as "The Purification of Unfailing Vows" (<s>Amoghapratijñā-viśuddha</s>). Retain it as "The Play of the Noble Being, the Determination of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> Conduct" (<s>Satpuruṣa-vikrīḍita-bodhisattva-caryā-viniścaya</s>). And retain it as "The Fulfillment of Purpose" (<s>Artha-pāripūrī</s>).'

body.text: idamavocadbhagavān / āttamanā āyuṣmān rāṣṭrapālaḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The venerable <s>Rāṣṭrapāla</s>, uplifted in mind, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>asura</s>s, and <s>gandharva</s>s rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

body.text: iti puṇyaraśmeḥ satpuruṣasya pūrvayogasūtraratnarājaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the Jewel King of <s>Sūtra</s>s on the Former Practice (<s>pūrvayoga</s>) of the Noble Being <s>Puṇyaraśmi</s>.

body.text: āryarāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the Noble <s>Rāṣṭrapālaparipṛcchā</s>, a <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s>.
